title: Premier League club enter the race to sign Barcelona defensive prodigy – report
description: The influence of new manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been evident in Fulham’s transfer strategy this summer, with the former Real Madrid bringing in the likes of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios.Arbeloa...
fullText:
The influence of new manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been evident in Fulham's transfer strategy this summer, with the former Real Madrid bringing in the likes of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios.

Arbeloa continues to scour the market for more Spanish talents as he looks to kickstart a new era at Craven Cottage.

Hector Fort has no future at Barcelona. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Arbeloa's search has now led him to Barcelona, with Fulham eyeing a move for the club's defensive prodigy Hector Fort, reports Diario SPORT.

According to the report, Arbeloa is on the hunt for a right-back and has asked Fulham to sound out the economic conditions required to lure Fort to the Premier League.

Fulham are not the only English club keen either, with several outlets insisting Everton also retain an interest in the Barcelona academy graduate.

Fort, who is valued at around €10 million, could therefore have no shortage of options should he decide his future lies away from Camp Nou.

The full-back currently continues to train under Hansi Flick, but his long-term prospects at the club appear uncertain.

Hector Fort likely to fall behind Espart in the pecking order. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Fort is considered one of the candidates to leave in the final stretch of the window in search of regular minutes.

He already spent last season on loan at Elche, where he recovered from a serious injury to finish the campaign strongly, and another temporary or permanent move could now be on the cards.

The right-back position at Barcelona looks well stocked. The continuity of Jules Kounde, combined with the expected permanent return of Joao Cancelo from Al Hilal, suggests Fort may struggle for opportunities.

Not to mention, coach Hansi Flick is extremely happy with the progress of Xavi Espart, who might even move ahead of Fort in the pecking order.

For Fort, a switch to Fulham would represent an exciting opportunity to test himself in the Premier League under a coach clearly willing to trust young players.

title: Luther Burden III set to miss time with groin injury, depleting Bears' already-thin WR depth
description: Between trading away DJ Moore this offseason and the Burden III injury, Chicago's WR depth is looking very thin early.
fullText:
Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III is expected to miss some time as he recovers from a groin injury, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Burden went down awkwardly in practice Saturday and was seen leaving early with a trainer. While the good news was that the wideout was able to walk off under his own power, he was walking gingerly.

It looked like a lower-body issue, and now we know it is a groin injury. These issues can be problematic and easily aggravated, so the Bears may be a little more cautious with his recovery. The good news is that Chicago's regular season start is more than a month away, giving Burden time to recover.

The biggest problem in the interim is that without Burden, the Bears' wide receiver depth looks very thin.

Chicago opted to trade away veteran wide receiver DJ Moore to the Buffalo Bills in the offseason. That puts a lot of pressure and faith into the Bears' young wide receiver foundation in Rome Odunze and Burden.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

With Burden now sidelined, Chicago has a glaring lack of depth at wide receiver. Odunze is clearly the top wide receiver, but he is currently joined by Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, Jahdae Walker and Scotty Miller as the best options at the position.

Odunze is heading into his third season. Last year, he played in 12 games and finished with 661 yards and six touchdowns.

Raymond spent the last five years with the Detroit Lions, but jumped ship and signed with the Bears this offseason. The 5-foot-8 receiver played in 15 games last year, but finished with 289 yards and a touchdown.

The Bears drafted Thomas in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He spent his final two years of his college career at LSU after beginning at Mississippi State. Thomas played in 13 games for the Tigers last season and finished with 488 yards and four touchdowns.

Walker went undrafted last year, but landed with Chicago. He saw action in nine games and finished his rookie season with 87 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions.

Miller is another veteran option for Chicago. He spent the last two seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Miller played in 13 games last year and had just 62 yards on nine receptions.

Chicago's wide receiving group was already expected to be inexperienced, but losing the talent of Burden for the foreseeable future definitely hurts.

Quarterback Caleb Williams will rely on Odunze, running back D'Andre Swift and tight ends Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet as his main options while Burden is sidelined unless one of the depth wide receivers steps up.

title: Cornell bans bear butchering after students carved up creature in dorm kitchen
description: Cornell University now bans wild game processing in dorm kitchens after two students went viral for butchering a black bear in Ganędagǫ Hall.
fullText:
Cornell University has added a new rule banning the processing of wild game in school kitchens, months after two students went viral for carving a bear in a dormitory kitchen.

"Processing wild/game animals in community kitchens is strictly prohibited," the school's new policy states.

The school confirmed to a student newspaper that the rule's addition was a direct response to the 2025 incident, which saw two students drag the carcass of a black bear they had killed into Cornell's Ganędagǫ Hall for preparation.

One of those students, Aaron Chin, revealed himself as one of the butchers on a podcast a few months after the incident.

Cody Johnson Fires Back At Critics, Calls Alaska Grizzly Bear Hunt A 'Conservationist Effort'

Chin explained that he and his hunting partner, a fellow Cornell student, had planned on bringing the bear from the hunting grounds located roughly two hours from the school to a friend's house to prepare it, but claimed the friend had an emergency that left them unable to use his home.

Chin also said that, before bringing the bear meat on campus, he and his partner ensured they weren't breaking any campus rules.

"We were really diligent in reading all of the rules [and] regulations," Chin told the MeatEater podcast in September. "We made sure we did everything by the book because we knew we were going to be under scrutiny."

The incident incurred swift social media and on-campus backlash, prompting state regulators to investigate.

However, after an inspector from New York's Department of Environmental Conservation visited the kitchen where the carving took place, the agency found no code violations, according to an NBC report.

Fox News Digital contacted Cornell and Chin for further comment.

title: Slain California fire captain’s wife admits murder after Mexico capture, serving time for killing first spouse
description: Surveillance footage captured Cal Fire Capt. Rebecca Marodi fleeing before the fatal stabbing at the couple's San Diego County home in Ramona.
fullText:
A California woman pleaded guilty to murdering her fire captain spouse last year, decades after she was convicted in the fatal stabbing of her former husband.

Yolanda Olejniczak Marodi, 54, pleaded guilty Tuesday to second-degree murder in the death of her wife, Rebecca "Becky" Marodi, 49, a longtime California firefighter who was found fatally stabbed at the couple's Ramona home in February 2025.

When asked by the judge how she pleaded to count one, second-degree murder, Marodi said, "Guilty."

Slain California Fire Captain's Fugitive Wife 'Scared' Ex Mother-in-law

As part of her plea, Marodi also admitted to having a prior serious felony conviction from the 2000 stabbing death of her husband, James Joseph Olejniczak.

She pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter in that case in 2003 before her release in 2013, according to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.

Marodi, a veteran Cal Fire captain, suffered multiple stab wounds during the Feb. 17, 2025 attack.

Prosecutors said surveillance footage captured her fleeing the home as Yolanda Marodi pursued her. Rebecca was found with several injuries to her neck, chest and back that authorities said were consistent with a stabbing.

Investigators later alleged Marodi fled to Mexico after the killing, where she remained for more than a month before being arrested in Mexicali and being returned to the United States.

Marodi had initially pleaded not guilty to Rebecca's murder before changing her plea to guilty to second-degree murder.

Like What You're Reading? Click Here For More

She is scheduled to be sentenced Sept. 2.

Rebecca Marodi served more than 30 years with Cal Fire, mainly in Riverside County, starting as a volunteer in Moreno Valley. Most recently, officials confirmed she helped battle the Eaton Fire.

CAL Fire Riverside acknowledged Rebecca Marodi's death and said it is a "profound loss."

"Her legacy of mentorship, service, and dedication will be felt for years to come. Her passing is a profound loss to her family, friends, and all who had the privilege of working alongside her," the department wrote in a previous statement on their Facebook page.

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.

title: ‘I’ve definitely lost followers’: influencers face backlash over Meta ‘pervert glasses’ content
description:
Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators 
It was hardly an offensive video. Amid the buzz of the Tour de France finale, Oliver Hooson filmed himself whipping up a delicious-looking flat white for a fellow cycling enthusiast. But after posting the footage on social media, the comments that soon rolled in were a real shock. “PERV,” read one. “Out here pushing creep glasses,” said another.
fullText:
Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators

It was hardly an offensive video. Amid the buzz of the Tour de France finale, Oliver Hooson filmed himself whipping up a delicious-looking flat white for a fellow cycling enthusiast. But after posting the footage on social media, the comments that soon rolled in were a real shock. “PERV,” read one. “Out here pushing creep glasses,” said another. His mistake? Documenting the moment with Meta’s “spy glasses”.

Despite being marketed as the latest must-have gadget, Meta’s smartglasses, which can record video footage while being worn, have faced a vicious backlash, particularly relating to concerns about surveillance. There are widespread fears about the glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent, and the resultant footage being posted on social media. This has earned them the label of “pervert glasses”, and content creators, no matter how they are used, have faced a flood of negative comments for deploying them.

Things reached a peak this summer when Kylie Jenner collaborated with Meta to launch a pair, leading to a flurry of influencers showing off their trendy, Kardashian-approved goggles. Some content creators have been forced to apologise for plugging the specs. Rida Tharana, a content creator with 1.6 million followers on Instagram, “took accountability” for taking part in a Meta campaign to promote the glasses, criticising men who misuse them to “record and harass women”. Self-described pickup artists have used the glasses to film themselves trying to chat up women in public without their knowledge, sometimes making disparaging, misogynistic comments afterwards.

Hooson says that, while some of the comments left on his video were “savage”, he is fully in support of their message. “It definitely caught me off guard. It was a real ignorant move,” he says, adding that he hates that the glasses are being used against “women mainly being filmed against their knowledge”. The backlash was even coming from those close to home. “Funnily enough, my wife predicted it. She was going to post a banterous comment in a similar tone to the others but she didn’t press send.”

After posting the video, Hooson, who shares his passion for home design and cycling to his 224,000 Instagram followers, says he lost a “good 50 to 100” followers. He called the term “pervert glasses” a “defence mechanism” to dissuade people from using them. “If everybody gets round that they are pervert glasses, which evidently they have, then it’s a really easy way of limiting sales and the usage of them,” he says. “People do not need any more of their privacy stripped away. I’m fully in support of that.”

His interest in the glasses, which he received at a PR event, was far more innocent. “I saw [chefs at] high-end restaurants filming themselves with the glasses on, showing off their process. It was stupid, poetic and beautiful to watch. I wanted to have a play about and show people the things that I enjoy doing,” he says, adding that it is very hard to capture a point of view (POV) angle otherwise. “It was intended as a simple way of capturing a human POV of my morning coffee routine or my fast cycling descents. I think that’s vastly different from somebody going into the centre of Soho and asking somebody a divisive question and clipping them up for views without their knowledge,” he says.

But, for now, it’s not worth using the glasses. “Would I rather just not have that little fun point-of-view shot for the greater good? Yes, I would definitely get rid of them,” he says.

While the glasses have proved unpopular with some online, they sold 7m pairs in 2025 alone. Meta says the tiny, flashing LED light that activates on the glasses will let people know when they are being filmed, but there have been multiple instances of people complaining they have been videoed without prior knowledge.

In one instance, a woman told the BBC a man had recorded her, and then demanded money to remove the videos from social media. Another woman described being recorded during sexual encounters without her consent. Last month, police in Scotland said they were investigating a far-right TikToker who allegedly filmed himself making sexualised comments to young women and telling a Sikh shopkeeper about a plan to “breed out the white race” without their knowledge.

Restaurants, theatres and pubs in the UK, including Wetherspoons, have even joined in on the backlash, banning the Meta glasses over privacy fears.

Deena Lang, a parenting influencer, first got her hands on a pair of the glasses from Meta. “I didn’t really know what they were capable of,” she says, but she thought they could be a cool gadget for her son. This was especially true as the family were heading to Europe for a trip and the glasses could, very usefully, translate foreign text live.

But things took a turn when Lang wore them to a cooking class. After looking at the footage she had captured, she says she was “horrified because I just kept catching people giving me dirty looks or side-eye. For me, that was a real awakening.” She posted the footage to her 110,000 followers on Instagram with faces blurred out to act as a “cautionary tale”. She was soon flooded with comments criticising the glasses.

She says she felt “a lot of embarrassment” for using them in a public place in the first instance but understood where the criticism had come from, especially after looking at how they are used in nefarious ways. “I still think they can be used for good. People who are blind said the glasses had helped them navigate life better but the negatives just far outweigh the positives,” she says. “I heard from some people who were dancers that men were invading their privacy and wearing them into the clubs. Others said they caught their waxers wearing them during appointments.

“I don’t believe that we are in an age where technology like this can exist without people with bad intentions making use of it.”

As for now, the glasses remain out of sight. “They’re in a drawer,” she says.

A Meta spokesperson said: “We designed our AI glasses with privacy and safety features built in from the start – informed by engagement with safety experts, including women’s safety organisations. Our glasses have always had an LED light that activates whenever someone captures a photo or video for their gallery.

“They also feature tamper detection technology, and we are updating the glasses to disable the camera if they detect the LED was physically tampered with or destroyed. No other kind of camera has done this and we’re proud to lead the industry forward.”

title: Trump has squandered Republicans’ typical advantages in 2 key areas
description: President Donald Trump’s political stature is so poor right now that he has squandered the Republican Party’s typical advantage on both the economy and national security.
fullText:
President Donald Trump's political stature is so poor right now that he has squandered the Republican Party's advantage on two major issues that almost always favor the GOP: the economy and national security.

A Reuters-Ipsos poll this week showed Democrats and Republicans virtually tied on "war, foreign conflicts and terrorism." The GOP led on that issue by 11 points after the 2024 election. Today, 37% of US adults say Democrats have a better approach, compared to 36% who say the GOP does.

Fox News polling a couple weeks back showed something very similar: On national security, 50% of registered voters preferred the GOP, to 48% who preferred the Democratic Party. That's compared to a 12-point edge for Republicans in January, before the Iran war.

Both recent findings are within the margin of error. But the numbers even being that close is basically unheard of.

Fox polling has regularly tested how registered voters compare the two parties on terrorism and national security. Until the Iran war, Democrats had never even been within double-digits of the Republican Party on either issue.

Republicans have also led consistently on national security in Gallup polling. Democrats only nosed ahead on that issue once in the 21st century: in 2007.

Gallup's data on which party is better on "international terrorism and military threats" has been even more lopsided in the GOP's favor.

Across 22 polls conducted since a year after 9/11, Democrats have led on that issue only once — again, in 2007 — and most of the time Republicans led by double-digits.

The most recent Fox survey showed Democrats leading on that issue by nine points, 54%-45%. That was the biggest Democratic advantage since 2006, when they led by 20 points.

And when they took a lead on the economy back in April, it marked the first time they were ahead since 2010, shortly after the 2008 financial crisis that began during the George W. Bush administration.

CNN polling back in May showed a closer split between the two parties on the economy, with 35% of adults preferring Democrats, compared to 33% who preferred the GOP.

The poll previously asked people to choose between congressional Republicans and congressional Democrats. The last time Republicans didn't lead on that question was 2009.

The numbers on both fronts seem to illustrate that Trump greatly miscalculated the fallout from launching the Iran war — as well as other controversial policies like his global tariffs.

Americans don't love Democrats; in fact, the blue side remains pretty unpopular in polls. So the fact that they've apparently taken a lead on the economy really says something.

And the national security numbers might be even more striking — because Democrats hardly ever even compete with Republicans on the topic.

Just as education and health care almost always favor Democrats, national security and defending the homeland are almost always signature GOP issues, and lopsidedly so.

That remained true even when Bush launched wars in the Middle East that gradually became pretty unpopular.

Trump, though, seems to have botched the Iran war so badly that Americans suddenly see Democrats on equal footing with the GOP — in terms of issues on the GOP's own turf.

title: Passengers evacuated after Delta flight returns to Atlanta due to report of fumes in the flight deck, airline says
description: A Florida-bound Delta flight on Saturday returned to Atlanta and evacuated passengers on slides after reports of smoke in the cockpit.
fullText:
A Florida-bound Delta flight on Saturday returned to Atlanta and evacuated passengers on slides after reports of smoke in the cockpit.

"Delta 2204, change of plans. We now have smoke in the back, and we need to deplane immediately," according to air traffic control audio captured by ATC.com.

"The flight crew followed procedures to return to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport after reports of fumes in the flight deck," Delta Air Lines said in a statement.

"A slide evacuation occurred on a taxiway … Safety is paramount at Delta, and we apologize to our customers for their experience."

Flight 2204 from Atlanta to Orlando was carrying 199 passengers and six crew members, according to Delta. Passengers and crew on the Boeing 757 evacuated via slides on the taxiway and returned to the terminal on a bus. The flight departed at 7:23 a.m., according to flight tracking site FlightAware.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

CNN's Graham Hurley contributed to this report.

title: Africa wants more homegrown solar to boost self-reliance, but China's shadow remains
description: Africa’s largest economies are accelerating plans to build more domestic solar manufacturing capacity, a shift industry analysts say reflects both industrial ambition and growing unease over dependence on imports from China that dominate the global market.  Ethiopia, South Africa, Morocco and Nigeria have been stepping up efforts to localize manufacturing of equipment for solar power, from module assembly to more advanced manufacturing, according to industry experts.  Chinese renewable energy investment and related construction projects in Africa reached $66 billion between 2010 and 2024, according to the think tank ODI Global.
fullText:
NAIROBI, Kenya (AP) — Africa's largest economies are accelerating plans to build more domestic solar manufacturing capacity, a shift industry analysts say reflects both industrial ambition and growing unease over dependence on imports from China that dominate the global market.

Ethiopia, South Africa, Morocco and Nigeria have been stepping up efforts to localize manufacturing of equipment for solar power, from module assembly to more advanced manufacturing, according to industry experts.

However, they say China is likely to retain its dominant global role in making solar cells and other components. Its exports of such equipment have soared, partly due to a glut in supply back home.

Chinese renewable energy investment and related construction projects in Africa reached $66 billion between 2010 and 2024, according to the think tank ODI Global.

"Growing economies, coupled with recent energy shortages in countries like Zambia and the ongoing need to provide access to underserved populations, make it (Africa) a perfect market for China to channel its overcapacity in the sector," said Olena Borodyna, a senior geopolitical risk advisor with the London-based think tank.

Africa's largest economies are keen to build their own solar manufacturing capacity.

South Africa's utility, Eskom, plans to develop a 1-gigawatt solar manufacturing facility to capture more value from its fast-expanding solar market and respond to changing electricity demand.

Production of solar panels in Nigeria, meanwhile, is expanding rapidly, with local assembly capacity rising from about 120 megawatts to roughly 300 megawatts in the last two years. Its annual solar imports, mostly from China, also put it near South Africa's level.

The homegrown manufacturing push is tied to structural shifts in Africa's power markets. Rising adoption of rooftop and distributed solar systems in South Africa is reducing national grid demand, squeezing utilities' revenues and prompting interest in diversification.

South Africa is already the continent's largest importer of solar equipment, bringing in more than 3 gigawatts annually, also largely from China. Industry analysts say this scale of demand makes it one of the continent's strongest candidates for localized production.

The increased interest in solar power represents a significant shift, said Benjamin Clarke, policy director at the Africa Solar Industry Association, even if actual manufacturing capacity remains limited. He said nations pursuing solar manufacturing tend to already have industrial capacity and strong domestic demand.

title: Michigan military exercise preparing thousands of troops for changing battlefield
description: More than 9,000 service members are training in Michigan under the Northern Strike exercise, which adapts to changing warfare, emerging technology and lessons from global conflicts.
fullText:
Tanks fire across training grounds in northern Michigan as thousands of service members practice for a battlefield military leaders say is changing rapidly.

More than 9,000 participants from 36 states and territories and five international participants are taking part in Northern Strike 26-2, one of the nation's largest reserve-component military readiness exercises.

Northern Strike began in 2012 and is held twice a year. David Kennedy, a public affairs officer with the Michigan National Guard, said this summer's exercise is the largest since it began.

Brig. Gen. Ravindra Wagh of the Michigan National Guard said lessons emerging from conflicts around the world are shaping how troops train.

Us Says North Korea Missile Launch Poses No Immediate Threat, 'Consulting Closely' With Allies

"You see what's happening in Ukraine right now. You see what's happening globally with some of our other emerging conflicts that you see," Wagh said. "And I think that this is a place where you can test and innovate."

Northern Michigan gives troops access to more than 200,000 acres of land, the Great Lakes and air, space and cyber capabilities.

The exercise also brings together different military branches and international forces to practice operating alongside one another.

"We want to train with the allies and partners we're going to go to war with," Wagh said. "We want our soldiers, sailors, airmen, marines to see it here. Figure it out here."

Fox News followed troops from the United Kingdom as they moved through a practice attack, one of several combat training exercises taking place during Northern Strike.

During another exercise, a crew inside a Paladin howitzer rehearsed a fire mission before moving on to live-fire training.

Us Army Offering Defense Firms 'Concierge Access' To Test Weapons At Military Ranges

Preparing for combat involves more than the troops on the front line. Northern Strike also puts the units responsible for keeping them supplied and supported through the same kind of training.

That includes the 445th Quartermaster Company, which runs shower and laundry operations.

"Our main goal is to provide, I would say, logistical support and really strengthen the morale of the soldiers that are out there actually doing the big booms in combat," Company Commander Captain Kelson said.

For Pfc. William Flores, whose unit is from Trenton, New Jersey, the exercise offers a chance to practice before a potential deployment.

"This is like a practice run," Flores said. "So when we do get deployed, if we do get deployed, we are ready."

Technology is also changing the training.

Nearly 90 industry partners are participating in Northern Strike, according to Wagh, allowing troops to work with developing capabilities before potentially encountering them in conflict.

Those capabilities include autonomous resupply and drones used to deliver blood by air. Other drone systems can hover over a battlefield, assess casualties and relay information so medical resources can be directed where they are needed.

Fort Hood Soldiers Shift To Underground Training To Prepare For Battlefield Medical Care

3D printing is also being incorporated to produce parts and adapt capabilities.

"If you would have told me a few years ago, that'll be, you know, on the front lines, but we're doing it here," Wagh said.

Wagh said the speed of change is forcing the military to innovate more quickly and use exercises like Northern Strike to test those lessons before troops encounter them in combat.

"I hope they're a little bit better, a little bit more capable," Wagh said. "We want all of our units to have a higher, more capable state of readiness."

Northern Strike 26-2 continues through Aug. 14.

title: Hearts agree £1.7m deal to sell Kyziridis to unnamed Turkish club
description: Heart of Midlothian agree a deal to sell Greece winger Alexandros Kyziridis to a Turkish club for a fee of around £1.7m.
fullText:
Heart of Midlothian have agreed a deal to sell Greece winger Alexandros Kyziridis to an unnamed Turkish club for a fee of around £1.7m.

The 25-year-old joined the Tynecastle club last summer from Slovakian outfit Zemplin Michalovce, signing a three-year contract, and has been attracting interest from a number of clubs over the summer.

After Sunday's 4-0 win over Dundee United, Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken told BBC Scotland: "The club accepted a bid.

"It's a good deal for the club, a good deal for him. He came in for nothing and goes out for a good deal. This is football, we focus on the players who are here.

"I wish him all the best because he's a great player and also a great person."

Kyziridis impressed early on at Hearts as a key attacking player under head coach Derek McInnes as they went close to clinching a historic league title.

He scored six goals and recorded 11 assists in 42 appearances and made his international debut in a friendly against Italy this summer.

Kyziridis played in Lisbon against Benfica last week but will now travel to Turkey to finalise his move.

Under Hearts data-orientated recruitment partner Jamestown Analytics, Josh McPake and Calvin Miller - who has played a prominent role in the early part of this season - have been signed in a similar position this summer.

title: Sevilla close to signing Scottish striker Ure in £7.9m deal
description: Sevilla near a £7.9m move to sign Scotland Under-21 striker Robbie Ure from Swedish club IK Sirius.
fullText:
Sevilla are closing in on a deal worth up to 9.2m euros (£7.9m) for Scotland Under-21 striker Robbie Ure from Swedish club IK Sirius.

The 22-year-old is set for a medical at the Spanish club on Monday and ready to sign a five-year contract after being offered the chance to lead the line at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan Stadium.

La Liga side Sevilla will pay 6.5m euros (£5.5m) up front, with the remainder in add-ons.

Ure has been in demand across Europe after scoring 20 goals and providing three assists in 20 matches in all competitions this season.

He began his club career at Rangers, where he scored once in three appearances, before joining Belgian club Anderlecht in 2023, where he made just one senior appearance.

It is in Sweden, however, where his career has taken off, with 31 goals and seven assists in 50 appearances since joining Sirius a year ago.

His 15 league goals have propelled the Swedish top-flight club to the top of the Allsvenskan table, where they have built a commanding 13-point lead at the midway stage of the season.

The Scotland under-19s international has yet to declare his allegiance for a national team, while also eligible for Ukraine, but told BBC Scotland last month his preference is to wait for a call-up to the Tartan Army.

title: Fernandez dominates to win British MotoGP at Silverstone
description: Trackhouse Racing's Raul Fernandez wins the British MotoGP, ahead of Aprilia's championship leader Jorge Martin, at Silverstone.
fullText:
Trackhouse Racing's Raul Fernandez led from the opening lap to win the British MotoGP ahead of championship leader Jorge Martin at Silverstone.

The 25-year-old, who crashed out of Saturday's sprint, cruised to his second MotoGP victory, 2.5 seconds ahead of the rest of the pack.

Martin was on pole but suffered technical issues at Turn One and briefly dropped to fourth before recovering to finish behind Fernandez.

Despite that setback the 25-year-old, who won the sprint race, extended his lead at the top of the championship to 31 points.

Martin's Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi took third to complete the podium and move up to second in the championship, with Ai Ogura dropping to third after failing to finish for the first time this season.

Defending champion Marc Marquez finished seventh to sit fourth in the drivers' standings.

Six more riders crashed out of the race on Sunday, with Alex Rins and Joan Mir out after a first lap collision.

Enea Bastianini, Iker Lecuona, Cal Crutchlow and Francesco Bagnaia also did not finish.

MotoGP announced earlier this week that it had extended its contract with Silverstone to keep the British Grand Prix on the calendar until at least 2028.

The next race of the 2026 is the Aragon Grand Prix in Spain on 30 August.

title: Royalty, bombers and racing fairytales - Chepstow at 100
description: BBC Sport Wales recalls the major events at the Monmouthshire track that is celebrating its centenary.
fullText:
It came close to closing within months of first opening, was transformed into an RAF base during World War Two and has staged various music concerts, but this month marks a century of horse racing at Chepstow Racecourse.

The track was the brainchild of 10 local dignitaries who put their money together to purchase 370 undulating acres of picturesque Monmouthsire parkland.

Since opening its doors to about 20,000 spectators in August 1926 for its inaugural meeting, Chepstow has welcomed royalty, Wellington bombers and musicians including Tom Jones.

It has also hosted the richest race in Wales - the Welsh Grand National - for more than 70 years.

BBC Sport Wales recalls the major events at the south east Wales venue, where new milestones continue to be set.

Lords Tredegar, Glanely and Queenborough helped pay for the near-two-mile course on what was Piercefield Park.

Lord Harewood's Conca D'Oro won that first race a century ago before the first jumps meeting held a year later.

Financial concerns almost saw the course fail to survive the first 10 years before steadily establishing itself one of only a handful of courses that hosts both flat and jumps action all year round.

Former Welsh jump jockey Alan Johns says the course has wide appeal among riders.

"Unanimously, Chepstow is loved by jockeys," he said.

"It's what we call a big galloping track so it has really long straights, big sweeping bends and generally that means the best horse wins.

"It probably has the the nicest fences in Britain, horses tend to jump very well here.

"The Aintree Grand National, the Gold Cup at Cheltenham and the Welsh Grand National would be in that sort of breath."

Memorable Chepstow moments have included the Welsh Grand National winner that inspired a Hollywood film, a jockey's world record 12 consecutive wins and another home-favourite winner of the Welsh National.

No rider has managed to match the achievements of champion jockey Sir Gordon Richards who, in October 1933, followed victory in Nottingham with six out of six the next day in Chepstow before adding five more a day later at the same meeting. That run of 12 wins remains a world record., external

But perhaps the biggest fairytale was the remarkable return from injury of Dream Alliance, a horse raised on an allotment near Blackwood by Janet Vokes and owned by a syndicate of friends all paying £10 a week.

In 2008, the horse suffered a severed leg tendon, an injury that under many owners might have led to a horse being put down. But the syndicate refused to give up, paying £20,000 for pioneering stem-cell treatment.

Dream Alliance returned to action and repaid their faith as jockey Tom O'Brien rode the then eight-year-old to Welsh Grand National glory in 2009 at odds of 20-1.

The story was perfect for Hollywood, with Dream Horse released in 2021 starring Toni Collette and Damian Lewis.

Since 1949, the highlight of Chepstow's callendar has been the Welsh Grand National, traditionally held during the Christmas festive period.

The race has grown in stature with Bindaree, Corbiere, Earth Summit, Rag Trade and Silver Birch among those to complete the Aintree and Chepstow double.

Meanwhile Burrough Hill Lad, Cool Ground, Master Oats and Native River have proven their pedigree at Chepstow before Cheltenham Gold Cup glory.

One of the most memorable modern occasions came when Welsh-trained Haiti Couleurs won the 2025 edition of the the Welsh Grand National in front of a passionate home crowd.

The horse was trained by Pembrokeshire-based Rebecca Curtis and ridden by champion jockey Sean Bowen.

"As a Welsh jockey or a Welsh person in racing, it's one of the races at the very top of the list to be involved in," added Johns.

Among plans for the future of Chepstow is a three-day jump racing festival which organisers hope will offer an "intimate" alternative to the Cheltenham Festival.

The Welsh Racing Festival was first held last October to launch British National Hunt season.

But for now, racecourse executive director Luke Admans is happy to celebrate the past at a centenary dinner at Chepstow on Thursday.

"I wanted to do something that was going to pay tribute to the 100 years of the racecourse and all the effort it took to get the racecourse open and the work that everyone's done [in that time] to make it such an amazing venue," he said.

"We've got an amazing team. We have a lady who's been working in the annual members area for 53 years and a couple of guys on the grounds team that have been here more than 40 years.

"It's one of them places that I think you come and you fall in love with working here which is amazing and the staff are a tribute to the venue."

title: Fulham agree £30m fee for Southampton's Charles
description: Fulham agree a deal worth up to £30m for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles, subject to a medical.
fullText:
Fulham have agreed a deal worth up to £30m for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Subject to a medical, the 22-year-old will move to Craven Cottage on a five-year contract and become the most expensive Northern Irish footballer of all time.

Charles, who started his career at Manchester City, also attracted interest from Leeds United but has opted to move to west London to replace Sasa Lukic following his move to Ipswich Town last week.

He becomes Fulham's third signing since the appointment of new manager Alvaro Arbeloa after his spell leading Real Madrid on an interim basis during the second half of last season.

Arbeloa's arrival - following the departure of Marco Silva to take charge of Benfica - has led Fulham to sign two players from Madrid, striker Gonzalo Garcia and midfielder Cesar Palacios, before the capture of Charles.

The Cottagers travel to Malaga on Wednesday and host face German club Stuttgart on Saturday, 15 August before Chelsea are their visitors on Monday, 24 August in their Premier League opener.

title: Coleman training with Killybegs - but no GAA return for now
description: Former Everton defender Seamus Coleman has been training with Killybegs but a return to his local Gaelic football club is unlikely to be on the cards for now.
fullText:
For a few hours on Sunday, social media lit up with rumours and speculation that Seamus Coleman had found himself a new club.

Not on the football pitch but with his local Gaelic football side, Killybegs.

The 37-year-old left Everton at the end of the last season, bringing a 17-year tenure with the Premier League club to a close.

Republic of Ireland captain Coleman has been without a club since, despite featuring in June's international friendlies, but it was rumoured he would make a sensational return to Gaelic football.

The Donegal Senior Football Championship started on Saturday and Killybegs travelled to Four Masters in their opener on Sunday afternoon, with Coleman in attendance as a spectator at Pairc Tir Conaill.

While Coleman did not line out for his hometown club - despite the rumours - it is understood he has been training with Killybegs GAC to keep his fitness up as he looks for a new football club.

The making of the £60K bargain who became an Everton legend

Growing up in the fishing village of Killybegs in the north west of the island, Coleman played Gaelic football - an amateur sport in Ireland - for his hometown and football for St Catherine's.

He was an accomplished Gaelic football player and was selected for Donegal at minor level, which is a big honour for underage GAA players.

Coleman ultimately decided to focus on a professional career in football and joined Everton from Sligo Rovers in the League of Ireland in 2009, and went on to make 433 appearances for the Toffees.

He has often spent time off back in Donegal back with St Catherine's or watching his county and Killybegs, who lost their Donegal SFC opener by 0-15 to 0-10 without Coleman.

In May it was announced that Coleman would leave Everton, who had offered him a coaching contract to remain on Merseyside but he had declined that in a bid to continue his playing career.

Speaking ahead of June's international friendlies, Coleman said the prospect of adding to his 81 Republic of Ireland caps was key to wanting to continue playing.

"I think if we had got to a World Cup then things would have been different, but I spoke to the manager [Heimir Hallgrimsson] and he said if I can be fit and perform then he would like to have me around," Coleman said.

"So as soon as the carrot of Ireland was dangled in front of me, that became a massive factor in my decisions."

Coleman has yet to join a new club despite the start of the new season in England just weeks away, and has returned to his roots to keep his fitness up as he searches for a new side.

He has previously said a return to playing Gaelic football with Killybegs could be on the cards at some point, but it is unlikely while his professional career is still ongoing - even if he is a free agent for now.

title: Five-time Super League champion Makinson to retire
description: Catalans Dragons winger Tommy Makinson announces he will retire at the end of the season.
fullText:
Catalans Dragons winger Tommy Makinson has announced he will retire at the end of the season.

The 34-year-old former England international won five Grand Finals and a Challenge Cup during a trophy-laden spell with St Helens between 2011 and 2024.

Saturday's 42-20 defeat for Catalans at Huddersfield Giants all but confirmed the end of their slim play-off hopes meaning Makinson's final game will be at his hometown team Wigan Warriors on Friday, 11 September.

"As the 2026 season moves towards its final stages, I feel now is the right time to announce that this will be my final season as a professional rugby league player," Makinson posted on social media.

"Rugby league has been incredibly kind to me, and when I look back on the journey I've been on, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude.

"I've been very fortunate to live out a dream I had as a kid and represent some of the biggest clubs in England and France and also the pinnacle which is representing my country."

He added: "I've still got a few games left, and I want to enjoy every second of them.

"I'll be taking it all in, appreciating the moments and giving everything I have to finish this chapter of my career in the best possible way."

title: German trade deficit with China grows as Beijing relies less on European industry
description: Germany's trade deficit with China widened in the first half of 2026, even as the Asian powerhouse remained its top trade partner, preliminary data from state-
fullText:
BERLIN, Aug 9 (Reuters) - Germany's trade deficit with China widened in the first half of 2026, even as the Asian powerhouse remained its top trade ‌partner, preliminary data from state-run agency Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI) showed on Sunday.

German exports to ‌China fell over 12% year-on-year to just under €37 billion between January and June, the data showed, as Chinese firms cut ​reliance on European imports, making China only the ninth-biggest market for German goods.

How do US tariffs affect Germany's trade relationships?

What factors are driving declining German exports to China?

Why did Germany's trade deficit with China widen?

How has China's ranking as German export destination changed?

As recently as 2021, China was the second-biggest export market. That year, Germany sold China merchandise worth €104 billion, despite the effects of the pandemic.

Now, German manufacturing is struggling with both U.S. tariffs and Chinese competition, triggering major job ‌cuts at bulwarks of industry ⁠such as carmaker Volkswagen.

China, though, is selling more and more to Germany.

In the first half of last year, Germany ran a trade deficit of €40 billion ⁠with China. That had swelled to some €55 billion during the same period this year.

German imports from China rose 8.9% to €91.8 billion over the period. Total trade was over €128 billion, €3 billion more than with the United ​States.

"The ​reasons for declining exports to China are the weak ​domestic economy and increasing (Chinese) focus on ‌domestic value chains," said GTAI East Asia expert Corinne Abele.

German firms are now producing more inside China itself, while China's property crisis and cash-strapped regional governments are curbing investment, Abele added.

Far smaller economies like Austria and Switzerland have bought more German goods than China in 2026, the data showed.

China's diminishing reliance on Germany showed it is becoming more independent of Western powers and catching ‌up technologically, said Commerzbank economist Vincent Stamer.

China overtook the ​U.S. as Germany's top trading partner in 2025 after U.S. ​President Donald Trump returned to the ​White House and launched protectionist tariff policies that have eroded German exports to ‌the United States.

The U.S. remains Germany's single-biggest ​foreign market, but exports ​there fell about 6% through June to just over €74 billion, Abele said. By contrast, German imports from the U.S. grew 7.1% to nearly €51 billion.

France and the Netherlands were the ​next biggest export markets. Overall, German ‌exports rose 3.7% to €817 billion through June as global growth kept orders flowing.

"But the 'Made ​in Germany' brand must still reinvent itself," said Commerzbank's Stamer.

title: Email 'hoax' nearly ended Falconer's Hundred hopes
description: How concerns over phishing online, rather than fishing outside off stump, nearly scuppered Caleb Falconer's hopes of a contract in The Hundred.
fullText:
It was concerns over phishing online, rather than fishing outside off stump, that nearly scuppered Caleb Falconer's hopes of a contract in The Hundred.

At the time the Middlesex batting all-rounder did not have an agent, had not yet made a professional appearance and was thousands of miles from home, away with England at the Under-19 World Cup in Zimbabwe and Namibia.

But the teenager had a hunch he should pick up the phone to his father.

"I actually gave him a call and said, 'It might be worth chucking my name in' for The Hundred auction," Falconer told BBC Sport.

His father Stuart - a coach, a major influence on his son's career and, for one day only, became his unofficial player representative.

There was just one hitch. The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) was not quite convinced he really was Falconer's father.

"They had to get back to him to find out if he actually was my dad and it wasn't just a hoax email," Falconer laughed.

"It was a bit of a process and it took him a few hours to sort it. I've no idea what my dad wrote!"

A few phone calls, emails and a presumably an identity check later, Falconer senior had managed to get Caleb on to the auction list.

It turned out to be quite an important email, not least for his son's bank balance.

Several months later, his name was being fought over by two Hundred franchises, with Southern Brave eventually winning the bidding at £55,000.

"My mindset was that even being in the auction was a really cool achievement," Falconer said.

"To get picked up, and also getting a bit of a bidding war, that was unbelievable."

The Hundred: Who needs what to progress from group stages?

It is quite a jump for a teenager who only moved to the UK in 2023, having been born and raised in South Africa, with the aim of cracking it as a professional cricketer.

Falconer has yet to make an appearance for Brave this summer, but has been soaking up the experience of training alongside players he grew up watching and "picking their brains as much as possible".

With Brave unable to reach The Hundred knockout phase, Falconer could be given his chance in their final group game against Trent Rockets on Monday.

He caught the eye at the Under-19 World Cup, finishing as the tournament's sixth highest run scorer with 309 runs from six innings at an average of 61.80.

His batting is built around power and innovative strokeplay all round the ground, with AB de Villiers - the original 'Mr 360' - among his inspirations.

"I like playing the old paddle, or the scoop, especially when it's a big quick bowler and you just use their pace," he said.

Stuart Falconer, as you would expect, has a view on that, too.

"My dad is always telling me to pack them away until needed!" the 19-year-old said.

The ambition now stretches well beyond The Hundred, with Falconer keen to play for England's senior side one day.

"I would love to play in all three formats," he added.

"I'd like to see myself as an all-round player who can adapt to the different formats.

"I think that's every kid's dream to represent your country in all three formats. Hopefully, off the back of that, I can play some franchise cricket as well."

title: 'Surviving cancer isn't the end of the story'
description: An ovarian cancer survivor is backing Manchester Cancer Research Centre's study into new treatments.
fullText:
A cancer survivor who always dreamed of having children has opened up about the heartbreaking reality of going into surgical menopause at the age of 34.

Gemma Coleman, who was diagnosed with two separate cancers affecting her ovary and womb in 2022, was told she would never be able to become pregnant after needing two major operations.

The 37-year-old, from Turton, Lancashire, said her diagnosis had "felt like a death sentence, but surviving cancer isn't the end of the story" as she now hopes to adopt in the future.

"You have to learn to live with the long-term physical and emotional impact of treatment," she said.

Gemma underwent two major operations, including the removal of her ovaries, womb, fallopian tubes, lymph nodes and affected abdominal tissue, followed by eight months of chemotherapy.

Now three years into remission, Gemma has regular scans and blood tests while managing the long-term effects of treatment including chronic pain, fatigue, bone weakness and fibrosis.

"People often tell me I'm an inspiration, but although I tried to look brave on the outside, inside I was struggling," said Gemma, who lives with her husband Jak, 39, and their cat Moggie.

"My life was completely tipped upside down. We always dreamed of having children. Having that choice taken away was heartbreaking.

"We're hoping that one day, when my health allows, we'll be able to adopt."

She has welcomed the news of a £2.5m Cancer Research UK grant for the next phase of an ovarian cancer research programme to develop better treatment options.

"Research gives people like me hope that one day cancer won't be something people fear in the same way, but something that can be treated much more effectively," said Gemma.

The five-year award will fund the next phase of the study led by Prof Stephen Taylor at The University of Manchester based at the Manchester Cancer Research Centre.

Prof Taylor said: "Our laboratory is home to the largest resource of living ovarian cancer cell cultures of its kind in the world.

"By understanding how these cancers grow and respond to treatment, we can identify new weaknesses that could be targeted with future drugs.

"Every discovery brings us a step closer to more personalised treatment for women with ovarian cancer."

Trump posts examples of alleged Reflecting Pool vandalism amid push for Pirro to revisit decision
description: President Trump on Saturday posted photos of alleged vandalism to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool amid a push for U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro to revisit a recent deci...
fullText:
President Trump on Saturday posted photos of alleged vandalism to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool amid a push for U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro to revisit a recent decision to drop charges related to the pool.

Late Saturday, the president posted two photos of what appeared to be graffiti and some peeling of the coating of the pool. Both photos were labeled with the word "Vandalism."

Trump is pushing for the Department of Justice (DOJ) to backtrack on its move to drop criminal charges against people accused of damaging the site. The president pressed for Pirro to "re-visit her hastily made decision" on Friday.

Pirro's office has stated contractors who undertook renovation efforts on the pool were behind the damage.

Trump posted a screenshot of a post on the social platform X which he claimed showed proof of vandalism in the pool.

"The material was cut right where the video tape showed, for 300 feet or more. People were on their knees with their hands in the water at the exact location of the 'slashes,'" Trump wrote. "Additionally, there were witnesses to the VANDALISM, and the flexible areas of the material were cut with a knife."

The president has previously seemed to point to vandalism to divert blame for the water quality of the Reflecting Pool and maintenance problems in the wake of a renovation project, in which he had the pool drained and coated in "American flag blue" paint.

Trump suggested that fertilizer had been poured into the pool to cause the expansion of algae blooms, also previously claiming that vandals used a box cutter or knife to slice a nearly 300-foot slit through the pool's coating.

title: World number one Sinner to miss Cincinnati Open
description: World number one Jannik Sinner withdraws from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month.
fullText:
World number one Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month.

The 24-year-old Italian won his fifth Grand Slam singles title by beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final last month, but has not played since.

"After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati," Sinner said.

"My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept I'm not ready to compete yet.

"I'm very disappointed not to be able to play in Cincinnati. I can't wait to be back next year and I'm now focusing on getting ready for the US Open."

The Cincinnati Open main draw begins on 13 August, with the final on 23 August. Zverev and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic are among those in action.

Spain's Carlos Alcaraz won the 2025 event and was leading 5-0 in the final against Sinner, before the Italian had to retire because of illness.

But world number two Alcaraz, 23, will not be there to defend his title as he has not played since the Barcelona Open in April because of a wrist injury.

The US Open, the last Grand Slam of the year, takes place in New York from 30 August to 13 September.

A Gen Z worker got called out by their CEO for leaving 10 minutes early. Workplace experts debate who was in the wrong
description: “Is this normal?” A new workplace etiquette debate initiated from a young worker getting in trouble with senior leadership after leaving the office slightly early.
fullText:
Gen Z has long been chastised for being lazy, even though some research begs to differ. It's moreso that they just have a different approach to professional settings and work-life balance.

But one Gen Z employee recently brought up a genuinely interesting debate in a now-partially deleted Reddit post: whether they should have been directly chastised by their company's CEO for leaving the office 10 minutes early.

Other news outlets had obtained and kept screenshots of the Reddit post showing the exchange between the CEO and the employee, and posed a simple question: "Is this normal?"

What made the post go viral wasn't the 10 minutes. It was everything underneath. The employee claimed managers routinely vanished for hour-long breaks and colleagues took 30 minutes without comment, while the new hire rarely took a proper break at all. They also described covering work expenses out of pocket and waiting 17 days to be paid back, and claimed a supervisor had pressured them to recruit an unpaid social-media intern or they'd have to produce all the company's video and social content alone.

While the exchange was anonymous and essentially unverifiable, it's likely a workplace conundrum other employees have faced. It also split workplace experts Fortune spoke with. Some put the CEO on trial, while others saw fault in the employee.

Jason Walker, an associate professor of industrial-organizational and applied psychology at Adler University, saw the situation as problematic for the CEO.

"If a CEO is watching the clock instead of the horizon, that is the story," he said. "Ten minutes is not a performance problem, it is a symptom of something further upstream."

Walker's first instinct was the question the CEO skipped: Why was the person leaving early? It could have been that they had a sick kid at home to get to, an appointment, or their work was already done.

"Leaders who skip that question have already decided the answer, and their people know it," he said. "We hire adults. We should trust them like adults and measure what they produce, not when they walk out the door."

Habitual clock-policing, he added, also usually means an organization has no real way to measure contribution, "so it counts the one thing it can see," and it "rarely travels alone."

Etiquette expert Nick Leighton, cohost of the podcast Were You Raised by Wolves?, put it in terms of what a workplace is rewarding.

"If an employee is meeting expectations and delivering their work, a CEO chastising them over 10 minutes isn't necessarily enforcing standards," Leighton said. "It's just saying that the theater of it all matters more than results."

To be sure, he recognized some jobs come with a hard end-time baked in, like a flight attendant who can't leave the plane early and a bartender who stays until close.

If coverage is the point, staying is the job. But for most jobs, he argued, clock-watching should be a last resort.

"If the only measurement tool you have is the number of minutes an employee is sitting in the chair, that might say more about the measurer than the measured," Leighton added.

But not everyone saw it from the employee's point of view. Kim Bode, founder and CEO of communications agency 8THIRTYFOUR, aimed directly at Gen Z

"This isn't about someone leaving 10 minutes early or watching the clock," Bode said. "It's about a much bigger issue with early-career professionals: entitlement."

"They didn't ask if it was okay, they just did it. And when you do that, someone else has to pick up what you didn't do," she continued. The minutes aren't trivial, she argued, because they compound. "Before you know it, it's a full day of not showing up, not being available, not delivering."

Loren Margolis, the founder of leadership-development firm Training & Leadership Success, who spent nine years coaching leaders at Columbia Business School, was a little softer, but still made a point leaving early once could cause a pattern of bad behavior.

She called it a failure of "impression management." Had the worker flagged it in advance—"I have to leave early today, but I'll come in early tomorrow"—it would have signaled emotional intelligence instead.

"Leaving 10 minutes early in front of the CEO shows poor judgment," Margolis, who now teaches career strategy in the State University of New York's Women in STEM program, told Fortune.

But it could just simply be a misunderstanding between two very different generations. A 2024 survey of more than 1,000 adults by the meeting platform Meeting Canary found nearly half of those aged 16 to 26 considered arriving five to 10 minutes late as essentially on time, but tolerance of that fell to 20% among baby boomers.

The experts Fortune spoke with were wary of leaning too hard on age in this debate.

"No matter how old you are, us humans have a long tradition of complaining about the people we work with," Leighton said. "Nothing new there."

Gen Z treats output as separate from hours, while older workers still see chair time as proof of effort, Walker said. But plenty of them felt the same friction—they just paid a higher price for saying it aloud.

"The values gap is smaller than we think," he said. "The willingness gap is enormous. The objection is not new. What is new is that it now has an audience."

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

Brazilian top-flight club wear name of English fan with MND on shirts
description: Brazilian top flight club Coritiba wear the name of an English fan from Norwich on their shirts to raise awareness of motor neurone disease.
fullText:
When the players of Brazilian team Coritiba walked out of the tunnel for their league match against Chapecoense on Saturday evening, their shirts looked a little different.

Rather than the usual front-of-shirt sponsor, the kits were adorned with the name of English fan Jonny Butcher, to raise awareness of motor neurone disease (MND).

The 29-year-old from Norwich was diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) - a form of MND - in February.

MND is an incurable condition that damages parts of the nervous system, destroying motor neurones (specialist nerve cells) in the brain and spinal cord, causing muscles to weaken, waste away and eventually stop working.

A Norwich City fan since childhood, Butcher took an interest in Brazilian Serie A club Coritiba for two reasons.

In March 2023 he met his wife and Coritiba native Ana Clara on a Christian dating app, and a few months later he visited her in Brazil and fell in love with the city.

The couple married in 2024, but in February Butcher's diagnosis turned their lives upside down.

Butcher made a bucket list of things he wanted to experience while he still could, and among them was attending a Coritiba match at their Couto Pereira stadium with his brother-in-law.

While breathing difficulties and a loss of mobility have prevented that, Coritiba heard about Butcher's story and decided to honour him before their Serie A win against Chapocoense.

As well as bearing his name, the front of the players' shirts read: "Your strength inspires us. We stand as one."

Incorporated into the design was a sunflower, the international symbol of awareness for non-visible disabilities.

Following the Brazilian national anthem, the players posed with a banner bearing Butcher's name and the signatures of Coritiba fans, players and staff.

"We sat there watching it all from England, completely overwhelmed and honestly struggling to believe that this was really happening," Ana Clara told BBC Sport.

"To see Jonny's name inside Couto Pereira, surrounded by thousands of people who had never even met him but chose to stand behind him, was incredibly emotional."

Coritiba said some of the shirts will be sent to Butcher's family and an institution that provides assistance for people with rare diseases, including MND.

"Last night Jonny said he wishes he could shake every hand and tell each person individually what this meant to him," added Ana Clara.

"We may never be able to properly express our gratitude, but we hope they know that this is something we will carry with us for the rest of our lives.

"Even in the hardest chapter of our lives, there is still so much love and kindness in the world. This will forever be a part of our story."

title: Litchfield helps Sunrisers boost knockout hopes
description: Sunrisers Leeds keep their hopes of making The Hundred knockout phase alive with a six-wicket win over Welsh Fire, which simultaneously eliminates their opponents.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Headingley

Welsh Fire 121-8 (100 balls): Kemp 72* (45); Sharma 3-13

Sunrisers Leeds 122-4 (74 balls): Litchfield 55 (25); Smale 2-23

Sunrisers Leeds won six wickets

Sunrisers Leeds kept their hopes of making The Hundred knockout phase alive with a six-wicket win over Welsh Fire, which simultaneously eliminated their opponents.

Set 122 for victory, Sunrisers opener Phoebe Litchfield delivered a stellar knock in the must-win encounter as she made a superb 55 off 25 balls to break the back of the chase.

Her side remain fourth in the standings but moved on to 16 points - two behind third-placed Manchester Super Giants.

The Super Giants host Sunrisers at Old Trafford on Tuesday with the victor progressing to the Eliminator.

However, Fire's bid to finish in the top three was extinguished by the result, with one match of their group stage campaign left.

Litchfield hit shots all round the 360 - cutting, pulling, driving and ramping a Fire attack which struggled to contain the Australian's skill and aggression.

The opening batter's knock featured six fours and three sixes and when she was eventually dismissed - caught via a leading edge off Georgia Wareham's bowling - Sunrisers required 31 off 48 balls.

Annabel Sutherland's 28 off 18 balls had Sunrisers within striking distance, before Dani Gibson and Jess Jonassen got them over the line with a mammoth 26 balls remaining.

"Our team is gaining momentum and things are starting to fall into place," said Litchfield, who was named the player of the match.

"I've just walked out and tried to keep it simple by watching the ball. Our bowlers set things up and I've had the freedom to play pressure free."

Earlier, Fire had been restricted to 121-8 after a disciplined bowling performance by the Sunrisers.

Deepti Sharma was the pick of the home side's attack with 3-13, while fellow spinner Hannah Baker took 2-15.

That Fire were able to post anything like a competitive target was largely due to an aggressive knock from Freya Kemp.

The England all-rounder used her leavers to good effect as she whacked an unbeaten 72 off 45 balls, including six fours and three sixes.

There was an element of fortune, though, as Kemp benefited from some poor fielding from the Sunrisers.

She was dropped three times - twice by Sutherland and once by Cassidy McCarthy - as only she and Georgia Voll, with 16 off 18 balls, made double figures for Fire.

The Hundred women's competition, Lord's

London Spirit 140-4 (100 balls): Kapp 72* (28); King 2-18

Birmingham Phoenix 108-8 (100 balls): Lamb 36 (26); Dean 3-17

London Spirit earned their second win of the tournament with a 32-run victory over Birmingham Phoenix in a dead rubber at Lord's.

Spirit were indebted to some late big hitting from Marizanne Kapp as they recovered from a cumbersome middle period to post 140-4.

Kapp whacked six sixes as she finished unbeaten 57 off 28 balls, while Alana King claimed 2-18 to finish the pick of the Phoenix bowlers.

Phoenix struggled for momentum in their chase and fell well short of the target, despite Emma Lamb's breezy 36, as Charlie Dean bagged 3-17 including the dangerous Ellyse Perry for six.

Both sides are already eliminated but victory for Spirit helped them move up to 10 points while Phoenix remain bottom of the standings on six.

Nottingham is the venue for Monday's action in The Hundred, with Trent Rockets hosting Southern Brave.

The women's side match at 15:00 BST is a top-of-the-table tie with leaders Rockets aiming to rubberstamp their place in the Lord's final.

Victory over Brave in their final match would secure their spot in the final, although given they have a superior net run-rate they could go directly to Lord's even if they lose.

Brave are in a strong position to secure a place in the Eliminator and would be certain if they win.

The Rockets' men's side will also secure their spot in the final on 16 August with victory over Brave in their match, which gets under way at 18:00 BST.

Brave men's are playing for pride having been already eliminated and a win would guarantee they will avoid the wooden spoon.

title: Everton's McNeil & Palace's Johnson poised for swap
description: Everton and Crystal Palace are in talks about a swap deal that would see Toffees' winger Dwight McNeil join the Eagles, and Wales international Brennan Johnson move in the opposite direction.
fullText:
Everton and Crystal Palace are in talks about a swap deal that would see Toffees' winger Dwight McNeil join the Eagles and Wales international Brennan Johnson move in the opposite direction.

Both clubs are hoping to conclude the deal this week.

McNeil, 26, nearly moved to Selhurst Park at the start of February when Palace agreed a loan-to-buy deal, which would have turned into a £20m permanent move this summer.

However, the transfer fell through as the required paperwork could not be completed in time, even though McNeil had already passed a medical.

In a social media post, his partner Megan Sharpley had been critical of Palace, writing on Instagram: "We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is.

"So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that's OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it's just part of the job?

"To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster and to be toyed with until the final minute. For that to be torn away from you at the last second with absolutely no explanation has hurt more than I can say."

But the deal has been revived, with Johnson now involved in the exchange.

The 25-year-old, who has played 45 times for Wales, scored the winning goal for Tottenham in their 1-0 victory over Manchester United in the Europa League final in May 2025.

Johnson moved to Palace in a £35m deal in January and helped them reach the Conference League final, although he was an unused substitute in their 1-0 victory over Rayo Vallecano as the Eagles won their first European trophy.

Johnson failed to score in 26 appearance for Palace in all competitions, including 13 starts in the Premier League.

McNeil joined Everton from Burnley for £20m in July 2022, scoring 15 times in 128 games in all competitions.

Everton finished 13th in the Premier League last season, while Palace were two places below in the table, but will play in the Europa League in 2026-27 after their Conference League success.

The two sides meet at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday, 22 August in the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign.

title: Yemen's Houthis attack Saudi refinery after kingdom signs defence pact
description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, they said on Sunday, two days after the kingdom signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan in response
fullText:
Aug 9 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, they said on Sunday, two days after the kingdom signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan in response to growing regional instability from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

The alliance with Sunni Muslim U.S. ‌allies, Turkey and Pakistan, is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression and stipulates that an armed attack against any of the ‌three would be regarded as an attack on all.

It was not clear whether or how either Pakistan or Turkey would join in any Saudi response to the latest attacks.

The Houthis declared a naval blockade ​against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea last month, citing what they said was a Saudi siege on them, an allegation Riyadh denies.

The Saudi energy ministry said a fire had broken out at the refinery but was later extinguished with no injuries and authorities were dealing with the incident, without giving a cause.

The Houthis used a drone to target the refinery, military spokesperson Yahya Saree posted on X. They had struck Aramco sites before in Jazan, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day in southwestern Saudi Arabia. ‌They had also hit Yanbu on the Red Sea.

In ⁠a separate statement, Saree said the Houthis carried out missile and drone strikes on the Yemeni Red Sea port city of Mocha.

The port, controlled by the Aden-based government, is close to the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait, which links the southern Red Sea with the ⁠Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

Should it be closed, Saudi Arabia would be deprived of an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

JAZAN REFINERY WAS SHUT IN LATE JULY

Three Yemeni government sources told Reuters that air defences were engaging drones launched by the Houthis towards the commercial quay and storage in the port.

Saree said the Houthi strikes targeted Saudi troops and ​weapons ​arsenal in the area. There was no Saudi comment on the attacks in Yemen.

Rashad al-Alimi, head ​of Yemen's Saudi-backed presidential council, on Sunday briefed U.S. Mission to ‌Yemen Chargé d'Affaires Neil Hop on the developments, according to a statement.

He said the Houthis' attack put a responsibility on the international community, foremost among them the U.S., to "move beyond only containing the Houthi threat to addressing its sources and instruments".

SEVEN PEOPLE KILLED, YEMENI SPOKESPERSON SAYS

The Yemeni military spokesperson said the attack on the port killed seven people.

The Yemeni transportation ministry said in a statement that the attack caused severe damage to the port's infrastructure.

"This marks yet another assault on a vital civilian facility that serves citizens and contributes to boosting commercial and maritime activity in the Red Sea," the ministry said.

Iran and its allied Shi'ite Muslim armed groups have been firing on ‌Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states and blockading their energy shipments since the U.S. and ​Israel attacked the country on February 28 in a major escalation after years of regional tumult.

Talks have ​dragged on between the U.S. and Iran in pursuit of a peace ​deal, with access to the Strait of Hormuz, a major conduit for energy supplies, proving a major stumbling block.

Houthi attacks in the ‌Red Sea have aggravated the disruptions of supplies to global markets.

No ​one from the Pakistan government could immediately ​be contacted and the Turkish government did not respond to a request on Sunday for comment on the implications of the refinery attack.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Friday, as the alliance was announced, that it was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a ​general pledge to support the three allies' security.

Fidan said the ‌allies would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of support they would ask for in the event of an attack on any ​of them.

title: Colombia's new president signals energy policy shift, backs oil and gas
description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella on Friday pledged to revive the country’s oil and gas sector, restore state-owned energy company Ecopetrol and strengthen the electricity system, arguing t...
fullText:
BOGOTA, Colombia (AP) — Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella on Friday pledged to revive the country's oil and gas sector, restore state-owned energy company Ecopetrol and strengthen the electricity system, arguing that energy security would be a cornerstone of his administration.

Speaking during his inauguration, de la Espriella said Colombia would pursue an energy transition — a shift away from oil, gas and coal toward cleaner energy sources such as wind and solar power — but insisted it must not come at the expense of the country's oil and gas industry.

"I believe in the energy transition," he said. "But that transition must be built from strength, not from weakness, from self-sufficiency and not from dependence."

The remarks reinforce a sharp shift from former President Gustavo Petro, who stopped awarding new oil and gas exploration contracts while pushing Colombia toward renewable energy and making protection of the Amazon a centerpiece of his environmental agenda. Just four months ago, Petro's government hosted an international summit in the Caribbean city of Santa Marta aimed at building support for a global transition away from fossil fuels.

The commitments echo promises de la Espriella made throughout his presidential campaign, when he repeatedly vowed to expand oil and gas production and reverse key elements of Petro's energy policy.

Calling energy security "a matter of national sovereignty," de la Espriella said Colombia could not expect long-term prosperity by leaving its natural resources undeveloped.

He said rebuilding Ecopetrol, Colombia's majority state-owned oil company and one of the country's largest sources of government revenue and export earnings, would be "a definitive and absolute priority" after accusing the previous administration of weakening the company.

The new president also confirmed his government would authorize fracking — a method of extracting oil and gas by injecting water, sand and chemicals underground to crack rock formations — under what he described as "the strictest technical and environmental standards." He said his administration would also expand oil and gas exploration to rebuild Colombia's declining reserves, guarantee the country's energy security and attract investment back into the sector.

The president warned Colombia's energy system was in a "critical situation," citing declining oil and gas reserves, delayed energy projects and rising electricity demand.

He said the approaching El Nino weather phenomenon, which typically brings prolonged drought and can reduce hydroelectric power generation, meant there was little time to act.

"The El Nino phenomenon won't wait for us. To overcome it, it is imperative to implement urgent solutions," he said.
