title: Digne completes move to PSG from Aston Villa
description: France international Lucas Digne has completed his move from Aston Villa to European champions Paris St-Germain.
fullText:
France international Lucas Digne has completed a move from Aston Villa to European champions Paris St-Germain.

The 33-year-old left back has signed a three-year deal at the Parc des Princes.

Digne, who joined Villa from Everton in 2022, spent three years with PSG at the start of his career.

He returns to the club after eight years in England, following PSG's decision to activate a £8.5m release clause in his contract.

"I am very honoured to be returning to Paris St-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than ten years ago," said Digne.

"I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years."

Digne is set to provide competition for first-choice left-back Nuno Mendes.

The Frenchman joins a PSG side which have won the Champions League twice in succession, most recently after beating Arsenal on penalties in the 2026 final.

Digne made 30 appearances for PSG during his first spell, before leaving for Barcelona in 2016.

The left-back was part of a Villa side which won the Europa League last season - the club's first piece of silverware since 1996.

He is the third senior departure from Villa Park this season, following the exits of Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and Youri Tielemans to Manchester United.

title: Como sign defender Chalobah from Chelsea
description: Como have signed defender Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea in a deal worth more than £30m.
fullText:
Italian club Como have signed defender Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea in a deal worth more than £30m.

The 27-year-old has signed a five-year contract with Cesc Fabregas' side, who secured Champions League qualification by finishing fourth in Serie A last season.

Chelsea will receive an initial £25.7m, with a further £5.1m available in add-ons following protracted negotiations.

The centre-back, who has two senior England caps and was a late call-up to their World Cup squad, leaves his boyhood team after nearly 20 years, having joined Chelsea as a child.

"Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club," said Fabregas, who was briefly a team-mate of the centre-back during his time at Stamford Bridge.

"He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como."

Chalobah said: "I'm thrilled and honored to be here at Como: it's an ambitious, rising project, and working with manager Cesc Fabregas again is truly special."

The England international made 151 appearances in all competitions for Chelsea and won five trophies, including the FA Cup in 2018 and Conference League in 2025.

He also had loan spells with Ipswich, Huddersfield, Lorient and Crystal Palace.

title: Guimaraes can take us to the next level - Arteta
description: Mikel Arteta said the signing of Bruno Guimaraes will help Arsenal go to the "next level" and hints that the Gunners are not done with their summer transfer activity.
fullText:
Mikel Arteta said the signing of Bruno Guimaraes will help Arsenal go to the "next level" and hinted that the Gunners are not done with their summer transfer activity.

The signing of Guimaraes for £75m from Newcastle United was officially announced on Saturday and the 28-year-old midfielder was introduced to the fans inside Emirates Stadium before the match against Borussia Dortmund.

Guimaraes was not included in the matchday squad for the 3-2 loss to Dortmund but is likely to be involved in the game against Como on Wednesday.

Arteta was quick to explain why he was so keen to bring the Brazilian to north London.

"I'm delighted to have him," he said. "We see very clearly - especially the energy that he brought immediately to the training ground - the hunger, the desire to come here and create a big history at the club.

"And that's the ambition that we need.

"We want to go to the next level and are very, very much convinced that we're going to need players with such a personality, desire and character to push everybody inside the organisation to go even higher."

The signing of Guimaraes means Arteta now has plenty of choice in midfield with Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino all options in the middle of the pitch.

And Arteta went into detail about what he hopes Guimaraes can bring to the Arsenal side this season as they look to defend their Premier League title.

"On the pitch, versatility to play in two different positions in relation to what we want or the opponent does," he said.

"A player which obviously has tremendous timing and intuition to win the ball back and progress play very, very fast.

"He's a player that is very comfortable putting people through, moving between the lines, moving in behind.

"And then he's a goal threat. He's got a smell and a really good timing to get in the box. And he has the capacity to finish the actions."

Arsenal have already completed the signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge and brought in goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer.

The Gunners pursued Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr but the forward signed a new six-year deal to remain in Spain. Yet Arteta was clear Arsenal are going to continue to try to be ambitious in the transfer market

"Well, that's what we're trying to do. If we have the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very much looking forward to that."

The Arsenal manager also gave an update on the fitness of Jurrien Timber, saying he is still "weeks away" from returning to fitness, while William Saliba is another long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

title: We cannot sustain the level we want - Iraola
description: After throwing away a two-goal lead for the second match in a row, Andoni Iraola says his Liverpool side "cannot sustain the level we want".
fullText:
Liverpool fans lined the streets outside Anfield to welcome Andoni Iraola and his squad for his first home match in charge.

It was a sell-out crowd and there was certainly a sense of excitement around the ground for the start of a new era under a new manager.

But for the second match in a row, Iraola's side threw away a two-goal lead - albeit after he made a string of substitutions - and when it comes to quality squad depth, Liverpool have a problem.

"It was quite similar to the game we played against Leeds," Iraola told LFC TV after the match.

"We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

"We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do."

Who was 'a class apart'? How Liverpool rated in Monaco defeat

Iraola has two pre-season games remaining - a double-header against Como on 16 August - before their Premier League season gets under way.

In two weeks time, when they begin their top-flight campaign at Newcastle, the question remains as to who will partner Virgil van Dijk at centre-back.

Alongside Alisson and Cody Gakpo, Van Dijk made his return against Monaco after an extended post-World Cup break.

Van Dijk started the game with 18-year-old Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who looks like a terrific talent but will have to go on loan this season due to work permit issues. It spoke volumes that Liverpool finished the game with Luke Chambers and Wataru Endo at centre-back.

Ronald Araujo, 27, completed his medical on Sunday as his season-long loan move from Barcelona - with an option to buy for around £47.2m - nears completion, while Jeremy Jacquet, 21, is yet to be involved in full training since completing his move from Rennes.

Jacquet suffered a shoulder injury in February and has recently struggled with a minor knee problem, but Liverpool are optimistic he could play next weekend against Como.

"Jeremy Jacquet, we were in doubt whether to put him in," said Iraola. "We decided not to, but he should be fine for the next one. It's taking a bit more time than we were expecting."

In his programme notes, Iraola spoke about giving the fans a team that they could really identify themselves with and be proud of. He added that this friendly would be an important step on that journey.

Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak will play an integral part and despite the defeat by Monaco, the performances of the pair who cost a combined fee of £225m last summer will give Iraola and the fans plenty of optimism for the season ahead.

They combined well, with Wirtz operating in behind Isak in the number 10 role and it was Isak who scored the first goal with a lovely right-footed finish.

Wirtz was Liverpool's best player on the pitch and, after scoring last weekend against Leeds in Chicago, it looked like he scored the second here - but Isak told reporters post-match he didn't know which of the pair got the final touch.

"I think we agreed that me and Flo [Florian Wirtz], we both got a touch on the ball, but honestly I don't know who got the first one or the last one," Isak told LFC TV.

On how much he's enjoying working with Iraola, Isak added: "Really good. I feel like the spirit is good in the group and we're all working hard to make things work. We're going to make sure that we're ready for the start."

title: Sunrisers thump Fire to close in on qualification
description: Sunrisers Leeds move closer to securing qualification for The Hundred's knockout stages with a comprehensive 71-run win over Welsh Fire.
fullText:

Sunrisers Leeds 201-4 (100 balls): Marsh 50 (34); Woakes 2-41

Sunrisers Leeds moved closer to securing qualification for The Hundred's knockout stages with a comprehensive 71-run win over Welsh Fire.

Mitch Marsh, the tournament's leading run-scorer, struck his fourth half-century of the season for second-placed Sunrisers as they made 201-4.

The Australian opener hit a 34-ball 50 and added 89 for the first wicket with Ryan Rickelton.

Chris Woakes, who took 2-41, claimed the breakthrough when he had Rickelton caught for 40, while Harry Brook (23 from 11 balls) and Marsh fell within the space of five balls, caught off Jordan Clark and Lockie Ferguson respectively.

title: Dad sues after school allegedly won't say if biological males can use daughter's bathroom
description: A North Carolina father sued Cabarrus County Schools after officials allegedly refused to say whether biological males can use his daughter's bathroom.
fullText:
EXCLUSIVE: A North Carolina father is suing his children's school district after he says officials would not answer whether biological males could be permitted to use the same restrooms as his fourth-grade daughter.

Brandon Matthews, whose daughter attends Mount Pleasant Elementary School, and whose son is entering his senior year at Mount Pleasant High School, asked both principals in May to notify him if a member of the opposite biological sex was permitted to use bathrooms or locker rooms used by his children.

Matthews did not ask officials to identify any student, according to his federal lawsuit.

But Matthews still doesn't know the answer, his attorney says.

Trump Administration Opens Four Title Ix Investigations Into Michigan And North Carolina School Districts

"Brandon Matthews does not currently know whether a male is using his fourth grade daughter's bathroom," Nicholas Barry, senior counsel at America First Legal Foundation, told Fox News Digital.

"And does he have a constitutional right to know that? We say 'yes,'" Barry said. "Without that information, he's just in the dark and... He really can't make any good decisions without that information."

Matthews' concerns over the district's bathroom practices predate the lawsuit.

At a May 11 school board meeting, Matthews appeared with his daughter and urged officials to keep boys and girls in separate bathrooms.

"Nobody's targeting a child," Matthews told the board. "All we're asking is that the bathrooms are accessible to each gender. If they want that, then create a new bathroom."

Loudoun County High School Student Accused Of Filming Students In Bathroom Under Investigation

WATCH: NORTH CAROLINA DAD CONFRONTS SCHOOL ON BATHROOM ACCESS:

Matthews then turned to his daughter and asked her to address the board.

"I'm personally a girl and I wouldn't want a boy following me in the girls' bathroom," she said. "It's inappropriate."

Matthews also used heated language during his remarks. He repeatedly warned officials that he could "get aggressive" and, while discussing protecting his daughter, said, "Anytime somebody touches this little girl, I'm gonna hang them from my garage."

Less than three weeks later, Matthews put his concerns in writing.

He asked his daughter's principal to notify him "in the event that any biological male is permitted to use the female restroom facilities" she uses. He made a similar request concerning his son's facilities.

Christian Counselors Challenge Wisconsin Conversion Therapy Ban After Supreme Court Ruling

Both principals responded June 8, according to court filings.

The elementary school principal said that "[b]ecause matters involving individual students are confidential," the school "cannot confirm, disclose, or provide advance notice regarding the status, identity, or accommodations of any particular student."

The principal told Matthews that if he or his daughter became aware of a specific situation affecting her experience, they could contact the school to discuss his concerns. The high school principal sent a nearly identical response, according to the filing.

Barry argues that didn't answer Matthews' question.

"The explanation is fairly straightforward. They don't want to answer him," Barry told Fox News Digital. "Well, nobody asked for individual student information, so that's a non-answer," he added.

Virginia School District Sued Over Alleged Policy Of Keeping Students' Gender Transitions Hidden From Parents

Matthews filed suit in the Middle District of North Carolina against the Cabarrus County Board of Education, Superintendent Dr. John Kopicki and the principals of his children's schools. America First Legal Foundation and co-counsel Philip Thomas are representing him.

On Friday, Matthews also sought a preliminary injunction asking the court to require the district to disclose its policies governing sex-separated bathrooms and locker rooms and whether members of the opposite sex are permitted to access, or have accessed, facilities used by his children.

Matthews, a practicing Christian, says in his sworn declaration that his religious beliefs include that sex is immutable and that his children should not be expected to undress or use restrooms in the presence of members of the opposite sex.

The lawsuit does not allege that Matthews knows a biological male has used his daughter's bathroom. His attorneys argue that he cannot determine whether it has happened or is permitted to happen.

Matthews said in a sworn declaration that he has been unable to locate a written, publicly available policy explaining when students at either of his children's schools may be expected to share restrooms or changing facilities with members of the opposite sex.

Trump Admin Targets Woke Schools Accused Of Hiding Students' Gender Transitions From Parents

At an April 13 school board meeting, School Board attorney William Isenhour said "the district addresses the [bathroom and locker room] situation at each school on a case-by-case basis with the goal of addressing concerns of all students and their families," according to court filings.

Fox News Digital sent Cabarrus County Schools detailed questions about the allegations, the district's bathroom policies, whether parents receive advance notice and its response to the lawsuit.

Matthews says he ultimately seeks advance notice and a meaningful opportunity to opt his children out before they are expected or required to use intimate facilities in the presence of a member of the opposite sex. His preliminary-injunction motion asks the court, while the case proceeds, to require the district to disclose its policies and whether opposite-sex individuals are permitted to access, or have accessed, facilities used by his children.

It also seeks notice when a member of the opposite sex "has been authorized to enter, or is expected to enter" a facility used by their child.

Barry told Fox News Digital that a victory could have implications beyond Cabarrus County.

"Yes, I think if we continue to push Mahmood forward, and we start getting wins on it, schools around the country are going to have to start disclosing to parents what their policies are and providing parents the opportunity to opt out," Barry said.

Sjsu Volleyball Scandal Probe Finds Team Allegedly Recruited Male For Advantage Without Telling Female Players

"I do think as Mahmoud percolates out and as cases like this get decided, it's going to require that school districts provide notice and an opportunity to opt out to parents on this specific issue."

That is Barry's interpretation of what a victory could require. The court has not yet ruled on Matthews' claims.

Matthews' attorneys rely heavily on the Supreme Court's decision in Mahmoud v. Taylor, which involved parents seeking notice and an opportunity to opt their children out of certain LGBT classroom instruction on religious grounds.

AFL argues that if parents are entitled to notice in that context, the same principle should apply to children sharing bathrooms, locker rooms or changing facilities with members of the opposite sex.

Matthews alleges the district violated his rights under the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment and the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

The case is America First Legal's second lawsuit against Cabarrus County Schools over sex-separated facilities.

Its first lawsuit alleges female students at Cox Mill High School were required to share girls' restrooms, locker rooms and changing spaces with a biological male.

Those allegations are separate from Matthews' case and do not establish that a biological male has used the restroom at his daughter's elementary school.

Barry drew the same distinction in his interview with Fox News Digital.

Washington Mother Says She Found Adult Male Showering In Women's Locker Room During Children's Swim Meet

"The first lawsuit we filed, there are allegations that a male is using our three client females' restroom and locker rooms and changing spaces," Barry said. "Which is different than what we're doing here. Here, it's a straightforward attack on Cabarrus County Schools policy to get information about it and to know whether it's impacting our clients' daughter and son at school right now."

Matthews' attorneys also stressed in their preliminary-injunction motion that he is seeking information and notice, not an order barring another student from a particular facility.

"Plaintiff seeks only notice and information—he does not seek to prevent any student from using any facility," they wrote.

Cabarrus County Schools did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Orioles minor league recap: Eyanson debuts with nine strikeouts in five innings
description: It was a night of organizational debuts
fullText:
Luis De León's second Norfolk start wasn't as successful as his first. In four-plus innings, De León allowed six earned runs. In the second inning, he allowed three runs thanks to five straight singles. He started the fifth inning with a home run, a single, and a HBP. He exited after the HBP but both runners on base came in when Anthony Nunez gave up a grand slam.

The Tides rallied to tie the game in the eighth inning, but Nick Raquet gave up two runs in the bottom of the inning for the loss.

Enrique Bradfield had two hits and a bases-loaded walk from the top of the lineup and Creed Willems had two hits as well. Rece Hinds and Luis Vázquez had three hits apiece; two of Hinds's were doubles. Those doubles were the only extra base hits of the game.

New top prospect Anthony Eyanson made his organizational debut and it went pretty well! The centerpiece of the Adley Rutschman trade allowed two run runs in five innings, both on solo home runs. He struck out nine batters, walked one, and allowed four hits total.

The Baysox had only four hits, but they made them count. Victor Figueroa homered in the second, then doubled in the fourth. He came in to score on Frederick Bencosme's two-run double. Tavian Josenberger capped the scoring with a two-run home run in the sixth. Griff O'Ferrall walked ahead of Josenberger's bomb.

Another new prospect, Kyson Witherspoon, debuted today. Listed as the #7 prospect for the Orioles on MLB Pipeline, he allowed just one unearned run in 4.1 innings last night. That sounds great! The offense got on the board in the fourth inning with an RBI triple from Fernando Peguero. It was a two-hit, one walk day for Peguero. They added two

The Firebells kicked off their season with an 11-3 win over the Boston Hunters on Sunday. Kelsie Whitmore went three innings, allowing just one run on one hit with one strikeout and a walk. Amanda Gianelloni (2B) batted leadoff and went three-for-five with three RBI, setting the tone for the rest of the offense. Leblanc (P/1B) led the team on offense as well, going three-for-four with two RBI. Alexia Jorge (C) scored two runs, and Jill Albayati (LF/1B) knocked in two as well, but the Firebells fell a few runs short of a comeback, even with a five-run sixth inning.

title: Now that Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett has his new deal, can he now focus on his team?
description: Arizona has a new offense to learn
fullText:
We all know that last year, during training camp for the Arizona Cardinals, Jacoby Brissett was brought in as an experienced QB to back up starter Kyler Murray. That was the plan. If Murray became injured, there would be experience and knowledge behind him.

At the time of the signing, Brissett (6'-4", 235 pounds) had nine years in the league and had played in 87 NFL games with 53 starts.

However, he was considered a career backup. He did start two seasons while with the Indianapolis Colts back in 2019 and 2020. And he started the first 11 games of the 2022 season for the Cleveland Browns while their new quarterback, Deshaun Watson, was serving a league suspension.

But on the remaining contracts with the five NFL clubs he was a roster member of, he was the team's backup option. Even in 2024, when he was named the starter for the New England Patriots in Week 1, after just five starts, he was replaced by rookie Drake Maye.

So, when he signed that two-year deal for $12.5 million during the 2025 free agency period, he was penciled in as Murray's backup with Clayton Tune set as QB3. No drama, no quarterback competition, no worries.

Except Murray became injured in the Tennessee Titans loss and was placed on IR. His practice window came up, and the team just kept him there as the offense had come alive with Brissett at the helm despite not winning games. Then Murray was released after Jonathan Gannon was fired and Mike LaFleur became the head coach, and a decision was made. Whether it was LaFleur or GM Monti Ossenfort who officially pulled the trigger to let Murray seek employment elsewhere, what remained was that Brissett was in line to become the starter for 2026.

The #AZCardinals and veteran QB Jacoby Brissett have reached a deal to increase his compensation for 2026, as its new one year worth $15.5M with a chance to get $21M. 

AZ’s starter is now locked, already having begun practicing. pic.twitter.com/LwnQqqupIX

And after he was told he was the starter going forward, he wanted more money than an NFL starting QB should be getting, and not backup funds. And he got a pay bump for $15.5 million with incentives that could raise it to $21 million.

Which, in NFL circles, is less than half the price that most league starters are getting. Of course, Brissett will turn 34 years old this season. He has been in the league 10 years and has had few opportunities to be considered any team's starting quarterback.

Brissett joined guys like Colt McCoy, Marcus Mariota, Blake Bortles, Case Keenum, Josh Dobbs, Kenny Pickett, Gardner Minshew, and Josh Johnson, who were all considered career backups.

But now Brissett has his shiny new deal and is listed on the Cardinals' first official depth chart as this year's starting quarterback.

With Brissett's new contract signed, he started showing up for what he was being paid to be: Arizona's leader on offense.

He was set to make $1.5 million as the starting QB for one of 32 NFL clubs. He then showed up to work out in the Cardinals' first training camp practice. Now, for the hard part. By hiring LaFleur, this meant installing a brand-new offense similar to what the Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, and Green Bay Packers operate under.

Brissett suddenly needed to learn the Cardinals' playbook cover to cover. Not that he had not even cracked it open yet. But he missed out on all of the class meetings and practice sessions, which are extensions of the playbook.

LaFleur took his time with Brissett. He penciled him in at the back of the line with practice reps, basically labeling him QB4. After a few practices, he finally got his first-team reps on a Sunday with LaFleur calling all the plays. The scheme is new, as is the system, so there was plenty to learn, mistakes to learn from, and finally become comfortable with.

"Obviously, after this night of sleep that I do get, I'll go back to three hours of sleep for work purposes now. So, I'm not naive to understand that it's still a lot of work to be done."

Getting up to speed on a newly installed offense isn't as simple as changing out the battery in your vehicle. It's like installing a new starter. In some vehicles, it is easy to get to with comfortable access. Whereas in others, things need to be removed just to get to the starter's bolts. Most of the Europeans vehicles, you can barely get a hand in a crevice to reach it. Some are buried deep inside the engine valley under the intake manifold. The Audi S4 houses the starter unit directly through or inside the engine mount assembly.

The point is, each NFL offense is different. But Brissett has been forced to catch on with many offenses with the five teams he has been hired by, with six different offenses since he was with the Patriots twice. This is just another offense to learn.

"I think that's what gave me even more confidence in myself is knowing that I've been through so many different phases of this thing of football that I knew once the business got handled. Now, the football is the football. I know I'll take care of that. And I had no doubt that I'm going to put the work in."

Which comes at the right time. Veteran Minshew and the rookie Carson Beck have been at every OTA and minicamp. They have attended each class session. Both have been practicing and receiving tutelage this entire time. And each showed flashes that they could run this team come Week 1.

Beck has been seen early to late at the practice facility since being selected in the third round of April's NFL draft. So, he and Minshew have a leg up on learning this new offense.

Brissett understood that without actually participating in team activities, he was getting behind:

"I think that's the reason why we did get a deal done because they knew I would get the work done, and I think my teammates understood that. And obviously Coach LaFleur doesn't know me as well, but somebody told him that I'll do the work."

Carson Beck is about to tell Jacoby Brissett to take your pay raise and get comfortable on the bench if this keeps up in the preseason https://t.co/r48YRWkGby

And while Minshew is perfectly capable of running an offense, it is Beck who is getting the most attention. Especially since he balled out during the Hall of Fame Game. Yes, Beck played with the second-string against the Carolina Panthers' second-team defense. We get that and can easily place these facts in perspective.

Playing well and having talent are one thing. What Beck showed in the team's first exhibition game was that he understood this new offense. He might not have everything down pat, but by golly, he certainly displayed that he was fully grasping what LaFleur is teaching and wanting from his quarterback.

After all, this year's new offense has proven to be a winning system. The Rams, 49ers, and Packers were all playoff clubs last year. With basically this same offense. What these teams execute on that side of the ball is what Arizona will now be doing.

And the Cardinals have the offensive weapons while simultaneously attempting to revamp the offensive line. All they need is a capable quarterback. Is that Brissett? He admitted that during his time off from the team activities, he hadn't been completely through the playbook but had an overall idea of the general base. He didn't state that he filled his days playing the latest version of "Call of Duty," but that he will start to digest the wrinkles of the scheme as each page of the playbook is turned.

"I got a long way to go. I mean, I'm willing to put the work in. But it's training camp. We're all learning. It's the first time in this offense."

A lot of new stuff going on with this Cardinals offense with new faces that have to get used to. Both of his starting running backs in Tyler Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love, two new guards with rookie Chase Bisontis and Isaac Seumalo, a new right tackle between either Elijah Wilkinson or Josh Fryar, and several receivers: Kendrick Bourne, Jalen Brooks, and the rookie Reggie Virgil.

It's not remembering each new teammate's name; it is working as one cohesive unit with just a few short months to accomplish this. In a new system. With a new play caller.

"That's the ultimate reward in this game: your respect from your teammates. I kind of pride myself on and really that's the only thing I really value. Contracts come and go, but your teammates and the people that you go to work with and the ones that want to go to bat for you. I think that's what matters the most."

title: Dana White shares bizarre reason behind ring card girl exclusion
description: The inclusion of ring card girls at big combat sports events has been a custom for decades, but that could now be another change fans will have to get used to following Zuffa Boxing 10. Zuffa Boxing is Dana White's new passion, seemingly pouring his all into the resurection of a once beautiful ...
fullText:
The inclusion of ring card girls at big combat sports events has been a custom for decades, but that could now be another change fans will have to get used to following Zuffa Boxing 10.

Zuffa Boxing is Dana White's new passion, seemingly pouring his all into the resurection of a once beautiful sport. White and his partners have an idea on how to make their promotion click; signing big names and putting on even bigger fights is one way to grab fans' attention and steal viewers from the competition. However, for what seems like the first time in modern history, a global boxing event didn't feature ring girls, but the reason why is highly unusual.

Callum Walsh remained undefeated, strolling his way to a unanimous decision, while fellow countryman Aaron McKenna handed prospect Etinosa Oliha his first professional loss on his way to capturing the vacant IBF world middleweight title. It's safe to say Zuffa Boxing 10 didn't disappoint, delivering a massive night of fights at the 3Arena on Saturday. However, boxing tradition was missing one key component.

The ring aprons were bare after the exclusion of ring card girls. Appearing ringside on a live broadcast with the popular Nina Drama, White was questioned about why the event lacked its usual ring card girls. As he has come accustomed to, White did not hold back his frustrations, saying:

"Don't even get me started," White said in response to the lack of ring card girls at Zuffa Boxing 10. "The UK won't use ring card girls unless you have ring card boys."

His outrage was matched by Nina Drama, who labeled the thought of having ring card boys weird and perverted.

While there is no actual law requiring ring card boys, some European broadcasters and venues push modern equality guidelines, pressuring promotions to display an equal number of ring card girls as ring card boys. Dana White rejected the notion and scrapped them entirely for his show on Saturday.

Dana White just said the UK didn’t allow ring girls unless they included ring boys too 😭

“Don’t even get me started…” pic.twitter.com/UhQraoJU4w

title: Grant Holmes takes the mound in Yankees finale
description: The Atlanta Braves are once again in a position of avoiding a sweep. The New York Yankees pulled off two low-scoring wins and are looking to accomplish a third in this finale before the Braves return home to face the team just across the city. Grant Holmes is currently boasting a 3.77 ERA and is […]
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves are once again in a position of avoiding a sweep. The New York Yankees pulled off two low-scoring wins and are looking to accomplish a third in this finale before the Braves return home to face the team just across the city.

Grant Holmes is currently boasting a 3.77 ERA and is coming off a successful outing against the Miami Marlins just five days ago. Reestablishing his starting campaign after a shaky first half of the season, Holmes has found his command and played up to what fans were expecting coming into the season.

It's just been one game, so let's not get ahead of ourselves.

The outing, however, was a sign that Holmes still has what it takes to keep his starting spot and put on a stellar performance. He will not only have to match that showing, but top it, as it's uncertain what version of the Braves' offense will show up after their recent losses. And they need all the defense they can muster to hold the Yankees' offense.

As for New York, Cam Schlitter is set to take the start. Holding a 2.26 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and a five-pitch arsenal that's touching high velocities, it's no wonder Boston is keeping him in their conversations.

Cam Schlittler, Nasty 94mph Cutter. ✂️ pic.twitter.com/In8VOYRtW1

Though not coming off his best outing against St. Louis on August 3 with four earned runs in his three innings pitched, don't get fooled, Schlittler is a beast on the mound. And it'll take the dominant version of the Braves to stop him and avoid a sweep. They'll have to strike early with Holmes on the defensive end to continue his strong stint.

One could only hope, but the Braves will have to execute if they want this hope to turn into action.

title: Gattuso to Test Best Lazio Starting XI Against Frosinone
description: Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso will take the opportunity to field his ideal starting lineup in Sunday’s friendly against Frosinone.Frosinone to Host Lazio on SundayThe Biancocelesti have already w...
fullText:
Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso will take the opportunity to field his ideal starting lineup in Sunday's friendly against Frosinone.

The Biancocelesti have already won their first five summer fixtures, beating their Primavera team and four sides from the lower Italian divisions. Therefore, the Canarini will be their only top-flight opponent in this pre-season, having earned a promotion to Serie A at the end of last season. The contest will take place at the Stadio Benito Stirpe, and it kicks off on Sunday at 20:45 CET.

As Il Messaggero explains, Gattuso is planning to field his best available starting XI, as this will be his last test before next weekend's Coppa Italia tie against Mantova, which will be followed by the first Serie A fixture of the season against Bologna on August 24.

The 48-year-old tactician will start with Christos Mandas in goal. The Greek in now the first-choice custodian following Ivan Provedel's transfer to Inter Milan. With Alessio Romagnoli's future shrouded in mystery, Oliver Provstgaard will be promoted to a starting role at the heart of the defence alongside new signing Danilho Doekhi, while Adam Marusic and Alfonso Pedraza will complete the backline.

In the middle of the park, Nicolo Rovella will reclaim his Regista role after a season plagued by injuries. The Italian international will connect with Kenneth Taylor, while Fisayo Dele-Bashiru could feature in a hybrid role between a box-to-box midfielder and an attacking midfielder, with Gattuso going back and forth between his favorite 4-2-3-1 system and Maurizio Sarri's 4-3-3.

In attack, the misfiring Boulaye Dia should lead the line, as Petar Ratkov could be sold to Dynamo Moscow, who reportedly offered €18 million for his services. The Senegalese striker will be flanked by Lazio captain Mattia Zaccagni and Tijjani Noslin, who has usurped Matteo Cancellieri in the pecking order, while Gattuso's first-choice right-winger, Gustav Isaksen, is still recovering from surgery.

Lazio Probable XI (4-3-3): Mandas; Marusic, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Dele-Bashiru, Rovella, Taylor; Noslin, Dia, Zaccagni.

The report also expects more than 2,500 Lazio supporters to flock to the stadium, creating a similar scene to the one witnessed in Ascoli last Sunday. The organized fan groups will continue to boycott all home fixtures as part of their protest against club president Claudio Lotito, but they intend to make their voices heard on the road.

title: Arizona football training camp: Defense striving to be Desert Swarm 2.0
description: Danny Gonzales always has high hopes
fullText:
In addition to being defensive coordinator, Danny Gonzales is Arizona's unofficial historian.

Without blinking he can tell you the last time the Wildcats finished in the top 20 nationally in total defense in consecutive seasons (1993 and 1994) and also the last time the program recorded back-to-back years with at least nine wins (1974-75).

He also knows the UA's infamous history of struggling to replicate results after a big year, which includes his first season at the school in 2024 when a 10-win performance was followed up by a 4-8 record.

While most other coaches on the staff are looking solely forward, Gonzales makes sure to keep himself aware of the past. And he's not afraid to use some of the program's best results—like the Desert Swarm era of the 1990s—and worst ones as motivation.

"Is there going to be a Swarm 2.0? We actually have the opportunity to make that a real thing, and I am excited about that," Gonzales said Thursday, after Arizona's second preseason practice. "But I've said it several times over the last bit, we can't be like the '94 team, the '99 team, the '24, the '15 team."

Gonzales was the linebackers coach and special teams coordinator in his first year with the program. Moved to DC in 2025, the results were splendid: Arizona finished 19th nationally in total defense, allowing 308.5 yards per game, and ranked 7th in pass defense, 2nd in turnovers forced and 2nd in turnover margin.

Those numbers were key to the UA going 9-4, a 5-win improvement from the previous season. But since Jim Young went 9-2 in 1974 and 10-2 in 1975, the Wildcats have traditionally had a backslide the year after. The drop from 2023 to 2024 was just the latest in a long string of them, but Gonzales feels the way Arizona has worked since finishing last season has it uniquely equipped to prevent history from repeating itself.

"Now, there's there's not a great expectation nationally, and I don't even know that there's a great expectation in our league," Gonzales said. "But there is an expectation around Tucson when we walk around, and I think that's cool. That's that's the first step in building a major problem here in Tucson for the rest of the Big 12."

Arizona returns a good chunk of experience in the front seven, maybe more if linebacker Max Harris returns (along with running back Ismail Mahdi) as hoped. But the strength of last year's defense, the secondary, is almost starting from scratch. Cornerback Jay'Vion Cole and safety Gavin Hunter are the only returners who started multiple games, and 12 of the 20 DBs on the roster are in their first year in the program.

"Everybody keeps asking, 'well, who are they going to replace, and who are they going to play at corner?,'" Gonzales said. "You lost four DBs to the NFL draft, which is a record, by the way. If the secondary is no good this year, it's because we stunk up front. Because if those guys get pressure on the quarterback, guys in the secondary will be just fine. We have enough talent back there."

Arizona intercepted 22 passes last season despite having the 110th-best pass rushing grade out of 136 FBS teams, per Pro Football Focus. The Wildcats' 21 sacks were 4th-fewest in the Big 12, and they also ranked in the middle of the pack nationally against the run.

The UA rotated heavily on the defensive line last season and that could also become a thing at linebacker and in the secondary. To see if that's possible, during 11-on-11 periods so far in fall camp the defense has switched its entire unit between plays to help with conditioning.

"They do a great job of of getting in cardiovascular shape for July, but once you get into fall camp and you start practicing, it's like when you're in high school and if you play football and then you go to basketball," Gonzales said. "You might be in great football shape, but you try and play basketball, the first practice, you will die. Well, football is no different. That conditioning piece for the first few days is trying to get their hearts back into it. It's a one-play role, so they have to sprint 40 yards every single rep, so wherever the ball's from, they have to sprint all through the sideline."

title: O’Cyrus Torrence’s new deal represents a first for Bills under Beane
description: A deep dive into Brandon Beane’s long Buffalo Bills history of signing offensive guards.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills dominated NFL headlines on Friday, August 7 in signing right guard O'Cyrus Torrence to a massive contract extension. Torrence's new deal will pay him $78.4 million, including $46 million guaranteed over the course of four years, beginning with the 2027 NFL season.

It's certainly true that Torrence's latest contract is set to carry massive cap weight against Buffalo's salary cap, adding to an already astronomically priced offensive line. It's also an immediate point of contention for people who aren't fully versed in the role of an offensive guard, as well those quick to pass judgment on the recently promoted president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane.

This latest deal is far from the first offensive guard contract that Beane has signed during his time at One Bills Drive. How do others Bills contracts at the position during his tenure stack up? Let's take a quick stroll down memory lane, a path paved with plenty of hyperlinks leading to the archives of Buffalo Rumblings.

Buffalo signed offensive guard Vladimir Ducasse to a three-year, $3.5 million free-agent contract ahead of the 2017 NFL season. Ducasse started 12 games (after spending the first 4 weeks inactive) in his first season with Buffalo. After making nine starts to begin the 2018 season, Ducasse was benched in favor of rookie offensive guard Wyatt Teller.

Ducasse was released in August of 2019. During two seasons with the Bills, Ducasse made 21 regular-season starts (22 games played), adding one playoff start in 2017.

Wyatt Teller's history with the Bills is fraught fan angst. Buffalo originally selected Wyatt Teller 166th overall (Round 5) during the 2018 NFL Draft. Teller would only last one season with the Bills after signing his rookie deal, starting seven games in eight total appearances.

Days prior to the start of the 2019 NFL regular season, Beane traded Teller (and a 2021 seventh-round pick) to the Cleveland Browns in exchange for a pair of picks (fifth- and sixth-round) in the 2020 NFL Draft. Teller went on to a stellar seven-season tenure with the Browns.

Selected by Buffalo in Round 2 (38th overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft, Ford signed his four-year rookie deal and spent the entirety of that first season playing right tackle. In that season's playoff race, Ford was fined more than $28,000 for a blindside block in a game against the Houston Texans. It was a play that garnered plenty of controversy, and one that was ultimately levied as a reduced fine of $4,000 for Ford.

Ford succeeded Spain at left guard in 2020, making seven starts in the regular season, though ultimately benched in favor of Ike Boettger and then later Ryan Bates. The trouble with Ford was his and the team's inability to nail down a starting spot for long anywhere along the offensive line.

In 2021, Ford moved over to right guard and made seven starts in 15 games played. Ahead of the 2022 NFL season, Ford was traded to the Arizona Cardinals in return for a 2023 fifth-round pick.

Offensive lineman Ike Boettger entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent, signing a three-year, $1,71 million deal with Buffalo following the 2018 NFL Draft. After being waived ahead of Week 1 that season, Boettger was claimed by the Kansas City Chiefs.

Boettger made his way back to the Bills following his release from KC later that month, and he went on to play in six games at offensive tackle over the next two seasons. Buffalo tendered (as a restricted free agent/RFA) then re-signed Boettger to a one-year RFA deal for the 2021 NFL season.

Boettger made 10 regular-season starts (15 games played) at left guard during the 2021 season before a torn Achilles claimed the remainder of his season. He re-signed on a one-year, $$1,047,500 million deal with the Bills for the 2022 NFL season, but spent majority of the campaign on Buffalo's reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list as a result of that late-season Achilles injury.

The Bills signed Boettger to another one-year contract ($1,182,500) for the 2023 NFL season, ultimately releasing him at final cutdowns ahead of Week 1.

Offensive guard Jon Feliciano originally arrived in Buffalo in 2019 as a free agent on a two-year, $8.3 million deal that included $2.4 million guaranteed. Beane later re-signed Jon Feliciano to a three-year, $17 million contract. In three seasons with the Bills, Feliciano started 31 of 34 regular-season games, adding four playoff starts among six total postseason games. Buffalo eventually released Feliciano ahead of the 2022 NFL season.

The Bills signed offensive guard Spencer Long to a three-year, $12.6 million contract early in 2019. The team picked up his second-year option for the 2020 NFL season, ultimately releasing him during training camp later that summer. Long announced his retirement from the NFL two weeks later.

After playing out his four-year, undrafted rookie free-agent (UDFA) contract with the Tennessee Titans, Quinton Spain signed a one-year free-agent contract to play for the Bills during the 2019 NFL season. Following a promising season playing every offensive snap in which he didn't give up a sack, Spain was rewarded with a three-year, $15 million contract extension ahead of the 2020 NFL season.

It was a contract that failed to meet expectations, with Spain starting at left guard only for Weeks 1 and 2 before being benched in favor of Cody Ford and later Brian Winters.

At the close of training camp in 2019, Buffalo made a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles that sent defensive end Eli Harold to Philly to acquire versatile undrafted rookie offensive guard Ryan Bates.

Though Bates' rookie contract was initiated by the Eagles' front office, he never played a snap with the team. As a rookie, Bates did appear in eight regular-season games and three postseason contests with Buffalo. Bates would go on to play out his rookie contract with the Bills, starting four games in 41 games played over three seasons.

Buffalo tendered Bates, a restricted free agent following his UDFA rookie deal, ahead of free agency in 2022. Bates would pay visits to the Minnesota Vikings and New England Patriots before meeting with and signing an offer sheet to play for the Chicago Bears during the 2022 season.

We soon learned that Beane decided to match the Bears' offer to Bates, signing him to a four-year, $17 million deal with the first two years fully guaranteed to the tune of $8.85 million. Bates would go on to play two more seasons with the Bills, starting 15 regular-season games and two playoff matchups in 2022; then appearing in 17 regular-season and two playoff games in 2023.

Beane then decided to trade Bates to Chicago in March of 2024, receiving a fifth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft in return. In five seasons with Buffalo, Bates made 19 starts in 73 regular-season games for the Bills, adding four starts in nine playoff games.

The Bills signed offensive guard Brian Winters to a one-year, $3 million contract ($2 million guaranteed) ahead of the 2020 NFL season. In one season with Buffalo, Before being benched ahead of a Monday Night Football game late in 2020, Winters started nine regular-season games (16 total), adding in three playoff appearances.

Winters signed a contract to play for the Arizona Cardinals after his lone season with the Bills.

A former fourth-round pick of the Carolina Panthers, offensive lineman Daryl Williams signed a one-year, $2.5 million contract to play in Buffalo during the 2020 season. That first year he started at right tackle in every game for the team, including 16 regular-season games, plus three playoff matchups.

The following offseason, Beane managed to re-sign Williams ahead of free-agency's start, inking him to a three-year deal worth a total of $24 million. The 2021 NFL season saw Williams make the switch (primarily) to right guard, where he again started every game for the team (17 regular-season; 2 playoff). Unfortunately, that was the final season with the Bills — and in the NFL — for Williams, who was released ahead of the 2022 season in part due to cap savings and the emergence of Spencer Brown (at right tackle, where Williams also played).

Buffalo brought in Rodger Saffold on a one-year, $6.25 million free-agent contract for the 2022 season. Saffold brought stability to the position, starting all 16 regular-season games and two playoff matchups, and earning his second career Pro Bowl nomination (as an alternate). The 2022 season would prove to be Saffold's final NFL campaign.

The Bills originally signed offensive guard/center Connor McGovern to a three-year, $22.35 million free-agent contract as a means to replace Saffold's departure. McGovern started at left guard for every (17) regular-season game and two playoff games of the 2023 NFL season.

For the 2024 NFL season, McGovern took over the starting center role vacated by Mitch Morse. An accomplished multi-role lineman, McGovern played lights out in 16 regular-season games plus three playoff affairs, earning a Pro Bowl alternate nomination in the process.

McGovern signed a four-year $52 million contract extension, a deal that included $32 million guaranteed, in the spring of 2026, which prevented his signing elsewhere in free agency.

Brandon Beane signed offensive guard David Edwards to a one-year free-agent contract in March of 2023. Edwards played a total 16 regular-season and two playoff games in his first season with Buffalo.

Edwards signed a two-year, $6 million extension ahead of the 2024 season, and went on to make 16 regular-season starts and three playoff starts that campaign. In his final season with the Bills, Edwards started 16 of 17 regular-season games played, adding two more starts in the playoffs. Buffalo and Edwards parted ways this past offseason, with him signing a four-year $61 million contract to play for the New Orleans Saints.

As chance would have it, another former Panthers player landed with the Bills during the 2026 offseason. Corbett actually entered the NFL with the Cleveland Browns, who made him the 33rd overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft. Corbett played out his rookie contract in Cleveland before signing to play for Carolina beginning with the 2022 season.

This offseason, Austin Corbett signed a one-year, $1,487,500 deal, which, when considering the veteran salary benefit, will actually count slightly less at $1,262,500 for the 2026 NFL season.

The Bills selected offensive guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams with pick 241 (Round 7) of the 2026 NFL Draft. Reed-Adams signed a four-year rookie contract worth $4,509,752 overall.

An oft-chosen first-round mock draft pick of Buffalo in the lead-up to the 2023 NFL Draft, the Bills ultimately selected O'Cyrus Torrence in Round 2 (pick 59 overall). He signed a four-year, $6,220,978 rookie deal following the draft. Adding Torrence in the second round was a move applauded by many due to his fit in the team's offensive scheme.

Torrence started every game (including playoffs) at right guard for the Bills as a rookie in 2023. He again started every meaningful game for Buffalo during the 2024 NFL season.Torrence reprised that starting streak in 2025, and he led the team in offensive snaps a third consecutive season.

Entering the final year of his four-year rookie contract, Torrence signed a new four-year, $78.4 million contract extension It's a contract managed by Beane that represents the first of its type given to an offensive guard drafted during his tenure.

title: Commanders lineman Sam Cosmi calls back Stefon Diggs joke in welcoming new teammate
description: Stefon Diggs signed on for a one-year deal with the Commanders on Wednesday, giving quarterback Jayden Daniels another solid weapon as Washington looks to return to the heights they reached in 2024. Offensive lineman Sam Cosmi decided to welcome his new teammate to the squad by bringing back an old joke that has followed Diggs…
fullText:
Stefon Diggs signed on for a one-year deal with the Commanders on Wednesday, giving quarterback Jayden Daniels another solid weapon as Washington looks to return to the heights they reached in 2024.

Offensive lineman Sam Cosmi decided to welcome his new teammate to the squad by bringing back an old joke that has followed Diggs since his time with the Vikings.

Asked for his first impressions of Diggs, Cosmi said, "He's a heck of a ballplayer. From a perspective of media, I wouldn't let him date my sister. I don't know where that came from in the locker room, so we'll see if that's a true thing."

Cosmi's comment calls back to a viral video that made Diggs infamous in his early seasons with the Vikings. Several players in the Minnesota locker room were asked which teammate they wouldn't want dating their sister, and Diggs was the immediate answer for many.

Sam Cosmi with a callback to this almost decade-old viral video when I asked him about Stefon Diggs
“I wouldn’t let him date my sister” https://t.co/NnK6my5bi4 pic.twitter.com/sdfkSuEFJU

— John Doran (@JohnDoranTV) August 7, 2026

Diggs had a good attitude about the initial video. "Nobody wants me to date their sister?" Diggs asked when he was informed that his name had been floated. "I'm a great guy! I'm actually a great guy. They just don't know me well enough."

At least Cosmi seems open to learning about his new teammate before making any final judgments. For the time being, the question might be mostly moot, as Diggs has a child with rapper Cardi B, and the two appear to have an on-again, off-again relationship of sorts. When Diggs was asked about their relationship status as of June, he responded, "You have to ask her."

The post Commanders lineman Sam Cosmi calls back Stefon Diggs joke in welcoming new teammate appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: Mercury conclude road trip, Kelsey Plum reunites with Sparks
description: The Phoenix Mercury will conclude their five-game road trip with a reunion in Los Angeles for Kelsey Plum and her former team.
fullText:
Kelsey Plum joined the Phoenix Mercury at the beginning of a five-game road trip and will finish the stretch against her former team, the Los Angeles Sparks.

This week, Phoenix will play two games, starting with the Washington Mystics on Sunday, Aug. 9, before traveling to Los Angeles on Tuesday, Aug. 11.

Phoenix has yet to face the Mystics this season. Two-time All-Stars Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen lead Washington's young core, while Shakira Austin and rookie Lauren Betts provide an intimidating frontcourt.

The Mystics have the WNBA's youngest average roster of 22 years and 9 months, while the Mercury are the league's oldest at 30 years and six months.

Plum was traded to the Mercury from the Sparks on Aug. 2, which also sent point guard Monique Akoa Makani to Los Angeles. In 12 games with the Sparks, Plum averaged a career-high 23.9 points and 6.4 assists.

Entering their Wednesday, Aug. 5, road matchup with the Atlanta Dream, Phoenix star Kahleah Copper was averaging 21.2 points per game, followed by Alyssa Thomas' 15 points, 8.4 assists and 7.3 rebounds.

On Aug. 3 against the Chicago Sky, Thomas posted her 21st career triple-double in the win.

title: Donte Whitner Drops Eight-Word Admission on San Francisco 49ers Injuries
description: As soft-tissue strains and training camp casualties mount, a former Pro Bowler challenges the franchise to stop blaming misfortune and address a recurring pattern of medical mismanagement.
fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers have a unique problem on their hands. Injuries have necessitated that the team reconsider an intersquad scrimmage with the Tennessee Titans.

Not long ago we asked if the 49ers had an injury problem, and in full disclosure, we really did not think that they did. After a couple weeks of training camp, that contention is getting more and more difficult to make.

After the conclusion of the 2025 season, general manager John Lynch was asked what the team's approach would be to the injury issues plaguing the team. Lynch shared that the team would take a data-driven and trend-driven approach in dealing with the injuries. It appears that plan has not come to fruition at least not fully. The approach may take time.

What we do know is, whatever precautions the Niners took prior to training camp simply are not working. One former 49ers player is sounding off about what led to the rash of injuries.

Donte Whitner said how he feels about the sudden rise in injuries on The Grit Code podcast per 49ers Webzone's David Bonilla. Whitner summed it up succinctly: "You have to stop calling it bad luck."

Here's more of what he had to say.

"You have to stop calling it bad luck. [WR Ricky] Pearsall, [TE George] Kittle, [WR Christian] Kirk, [RB] Kaelon Black, [RB Isaac] Guerendo, [S Malik] Mustapha, and several more. Some injuries are random. Football is a violent sport, but when the same problem shows up every year, it becomes a pattern.

So, the real questions here are: Are they drafting and signing too many players with medical concerns? Are rehabilitation and return-of-play decisions being rushed?"

Root cause of injury is difficult to quantify. Given the wide array of injuries the Niners have endured over the last year, it's hard to pinpoint one issue as the only culprit. We do know that injury prevention is possible, however, and that the 49ers are not having much success if they are taking preventative measures.

The Niners can weather this storm. Depending on the severity of the injuries, San Francisco could get back several players this season. The problem is whether or not the poor health is preventable and what the team will do to make changes moving forward.

The Niners are still very much NFC contenders. They will need to address their injury problem to stay in contention this year.

title: Alabama reportedly among finalists for elite 2028 defensive lineman
description: Alabama is reportedly among the nine finalists for Tyzon Swann, an elite defensive lineman in the 2028 recruiting cycle.
fullText:
According to Rivals' Hayes Fawcett, the Alabama Crimson Tide are reportedly among the nine finalists for elite 2028 defensive line recruit Tyzon Swann.

The Crimson Tide are joined by Auburn, Florida, LSU, Maryland, Ohio State, Oklahoma, UCLA, and USC in Swann's list of nine finalists, per Fawcett. At this time, a commitment date is not set for Swann.

Swann is currently considered as the nation's No. 10 overall prospect in the 2028 recruiting class, as well as the No. 2 defensive lineman nationally, according to the 247Sports Composite rankings. Rated as a five-star recruit, Swann is also considered the No. 1 2028 prospect in the state of Maryland where he attends Henry E. Lackey High School.

Alabama's 2028 recruiting class currently ranks as the nation's best, per 247Sports, with seven total commitments. The Crimson Tide's class does not feature an interior defensive lineman at the moment, nor a five-star prospect.

title: Jordan Horston scores 17 points in 19 minutes for Seattle at Portland
description: Former Lady Vol Jordan Horston scores 17 points in 19 minutes for Seattle at Portland.
fullText:
Portland (13-19) defeated Seattle (6-28), 100-93, at Moda Center in Portland, Oregon. 15,294 were in attendance for the WNBA contest.

Former Lady Vol Jordan Horston scored 17 points in 19 minutes for the Storm. She converted 6-of-10 field goal attempts, 4-of-6 three-point attempts and 1-of-2 free throw attempts. The 6-foot-2 forward also recorded three rebounds, one assist and one steal.

Jade Melbourne led Seattle in scoring with 23 points, while Dominique Malonga finished with 21 points.

Portland forward Bridget Carleton led all scorers with 24 points. The Fire led for 80% of the game and their largest lead was 15 points.

Horston played at Tennessee from 2019-23. She was a two-time All-SEC First-team selection and a two-time Associated Press and WBCA All-America honorable mention.

Horston appeared in 114 games, including 91 starts, for the Lady Vols, recording 1,145 points, 731 rebounds, 455 assists, 109 blocks and 163 steals.

She was named to the 2023 WNBA All-Rookie Team and was the No. 9 overall selection in the 2023 WNBA draft. Horston went to Tennessee from Columbus Africentric Early College High School in Columbus, Ohio.

title: Diamondbacks lookahead. Rockies at home, road trip to Atlanta
description: The Arizona Diamondbacks schedule moves into the middle of August with games at home against Colorado and away at Atlanta from Aug. 10-16.
fullText:
The Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday, Aug. 9, wrap up seven straight home games with the series finale against the Los Angeles Dodgers at Chase Field.

Left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez is looking to right himself after a disastrous first two innings in a 9-4 loss to the San Diego Padres in his previous start on Aug. 4. Rodriguez went 5⅔-innings in that game.

Then the Diamondbacks have three more games at home, all against the Colorado Rockies from Monday, Aug. 10 to Wednesday, Aug. 12, before hitting the road to Atlanta for the weekend Aug. 14-16.

As August rolls on, the Diamondbacks find themselves in the thick of the race for the postseason. They were 61-54 going into their game on Thursday, Aug. 6, against the Padres, sitting in a National League wild-card position.

Manager Torey Lovullo likes to refer to August as "moving month."

"My favorite month of the baseball season," Lovullo said on Aug. 1 in Cleveland. "The season takes shape. The contenders and pretenders start to separate. The real teams and the ones that are capable of carrying on for the next two months start to separate themselves. It's the purest form of baseball.

"August is just the best month, and heads up, big things start to happen."

The Rockies are led by All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman, who as of Aug. 6 had 33 home runs. They have several players who have put together solid seasons of offense playing in the Denver altitude, but their pitching staff was last in all of Major League Baseball in team earned run average on Aug. 6.

Colorado is in last place in the NL West. The Diamondbacks are 5-2 against them this season with six games to go head-to-head.

The Braves are running away with the National League East lead and had a seven-game winning streak going into Aug. 6. Atlanta didn't make a big splash at the trade deadline but got better with the acquisitions of pitchers Brent Suter and Tyler Mahle and outfielder Lane Thomas.

All-Stars Matt Olson, Ozzie Albies and catcher Drake Baldwin have had big years with the bat and a solid starting rotation is led by veteran Chris Sale, who also made the NL All-Star team.

The Braves and Diamondbacks split a four-game series in Phoenix in April.

This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Diamondbacks lookahead. Rockies at home, road trip to Atlanta

title: Zandvoort updates to be ’crucial’ in Alpine’s quest to top the midfield battle
description: Pierre Gasly hopes Alpine can make a step forward with its update package for the Dutch Grand Prix. At the beginning of the season, Alpine was seemingly the fifth best team on the Formula 1 grid.
fullText:
Pierre Gasly hopes Alpine can make a step forward with its update package for the Dutch Grand Prix.

At the beginning of the season, Alpine was seemingly the fifth best team on the Formula 1 grid. Moreover, after a successful right of review, Gasly scored a podium finish at the Monaco Grand Prix.

Over the past weekends, however, Racing Bulls and Audi both managed to gain on the French outfit, and scored more points. As a result, Alpine is sixth in the constructors' standings, five points behind the Faenza-based team.

"It's not the reality I want to see, but I mean there's no hiding from it and there's been a couple of races where it's kind of the same story. In Qualifying, 12th, 13th, behind Racing Bulls and Audi," Gasly began to GPblog, among others.

"In the race it's like somehow you think that maybe we're going be there and then I can see them but it's just pure pace, we're not there. Yeah, it also doesn't feel good in the car like it's really, the car is not reacting at all the way I'd like it doesn't allow me to drive the way I need. And there's quite a few things to fix."

After the summer break, the F1 season will continue with the Dutch Grand Prix. Gasly expects the team's next update package to perform well.

He continued: "I think the aero is very inconsistent and I think it's something which we know and hopefully will be fixed in Zandvoort.

"That's the standard of Formula 1, if you bring upgrades you expect it to definitely get better and my side I'm not doubting that it's going to do what the team expects.

"It's important because Aston Martin improved by two seconds this weekend, they have another engine coming. Racing Bulls improved by seconds since the start of the year Audi as well and we just didn't do many steps. So, yeah, I think it's critical for us if we want to keep the hope for fifth place in the Championship," the Frenchman concluded.

title: Can Cowboys remain among Top 5 in this key offensive tactic in 2026?
description: The Dallas Cowboys ranked in the NFL's top 5 in yards/RPO last year and there's plenty of reason to lean into that in 2026.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys are always looking for ways to make their offense better and their overall attack more bulletproof. Winning a variety of different ways is key to sustained success in the postseason, so it's been a focus of Klayton Adams as he enters Year 2 as Dallas' offensive coordinator.

Designing and executing a scoring drive in the modern-day NFL is no easy task. With defenses shifting to more umbrella looks in the secondary, big plays can be hard to come by, even for a star-studded team like the Cowboys. Oftentimes the only way to put up points is to put together long, multi-play drives. In drives such as these, unsuccessful plays can have disastrous consequences. It's why many coordinators speak incessantly about "staying ahead of the chains."

The Cowboys used a myriad of techniques to do so, but one that worked to great effect in 2025 and probably even moreso in 2026 is that of the run-pass option.

Staying ahead of the chains means focusing more on success rate than expected points added (today's primary metrics for grading value), which means low-risk/low-reward plays are often preferable to those high-risk/high-reward plays often associated with big shots downfield.

The Cowboys aren't particularly dedicated to any single identity. One moment they will show the patience demanded for sustained and conservative drives, the next moment they're launching missiles downfield looking for homeruns.  While everyone knows a Cowboys offense with Dak Prescott, Ceedee Lamb and George Pickens is proficient in big plays, they're also strong in building multi-play drives.

While the league average for plays per drive was 5.6 last season, the Cowboys were league leaders at 6.5 plays per drive. It might not sound like much but for a well-rounded and fairly aggressive team such as Dallas, being a leader in plays per drive is impressive. One of the ways they achieved this impressive accomplishment is by being proficient in RPOs.

Dak Prescott RPO work, quick screen to CeeDee Lamb pic.twitter.com/94v9BBAzaz

Based on Pro Football Focus play tracking, the Cowboys were fourth in the NFL in yards per play on RPOs last season. At 5.5 yards/RPO, the Cowboys were a full yard above league average. It kept them ahead of the chains and kept defenses on their heels.

RPOs are effective because they put defenders in conflict. Not to be confused with read-option and zone-read which are run-only option plays, RPOs have a legit pass option to their design.

In a nutshell, if a defender plays it one way, the quarterback hands it off. If the defender plays it another way, the quarterback pulls it back and delivers a pass. It's a quick-read play that requires quick decisions. It's low-risk and low-reward but has a success rate of 52.3% compared to that of non-RPO plays which average 48.1%.

An added benefit of an RPO-rich offense is the stress it removes from offensive tackles. With such a quick-strike nature, RPOs get the ball out quickly. Per PFF, Patrick Mahomes, king of the RPO, averaged 1.17 seconds on RPO throws. It's a great way to neutralize a defense that has elite edge rushers.

RPOs also typically favor inside runs. With arguably the best inside offensive line in the NFL, the Cowboys have reason to run plays up the middle. And since most RPOs end up being runs, it plays perfectly to Dallas' strength. With one of the great field generals in the game in Prescott, the Cowboys should by no means become an RPO-rich offense in 2026 but given their proficiency in it, and given their pass protection situation on the edge, a slight uptick might be in order.

It's all about becoming multidimensional and being bulletproof for the postseason. Explosive plays aren't always an option but RPOs have a certain resiliency that ages well in an NFL season. Last seen, the Cowboys were pretty darn good at them, so why not lean into RPOs a little more in 2026 and see if it pays off like the data suggests?

title: Dave Toub applauds Patrick Mahomes' progress during training camp
description: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs Coordinator Dave Toub applauded Patrick Mahomes' progress during training camp | @EdEastonJr
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs special teams coordinator Dave Toub spoke with reporters after practice on Saturday at Missouri Western State University. He applauded quarterback Patrick Mahomes' progress during training camp.

"It really is; it's incredible what we're seeing with (Patrick Mahomes) Pat. I keep watching every day." said Toub, "I'm on the outside watching offense and defense, and I keep watching for anything, any sign of him limping or anything like that, and I don't see anything. He just keeps getting better and stronger. It's exciting, you know it's exciting to see where he's at."

Mahomes was cleared for full practice activities at the start of training camp and has continued to go through drills without any significant issues. The coaching staff is watching his progress but not rushing him or limiting his abilities on the practice field. Toub, weighing in on his improvements, speaks volumes, as he primarily focuses on developing the special teams unit.

title: EJ Exposito and Izaac Pacheco combine for 5 homers
description: Scores, news, and notes, from around the Detroit Tigers’ farm system for Saturday, August 8, 2026.
fullText:
Carl Edwards Jr. took the loss, but that's largely because his defense didn't have his back. The first run was on Edwards. He gave up a double and single in the first, and a fielder's choice made it 1-0. The other four were unearned.

Bennett Lee threw away a dropped third strike that would have been the third out of the third inning. (Triple-triple). A leadoff error by Cal Stevenson at first ruined the start of what should have been a 1-2-3 inning. Instead, it turned into a three-run homer. 5-0, Omaha.

Brant Hurter took over in the seventh. He gave up an RBI single, but Trei Cruz made it a two-run base knock after letting the ball go right by him in center field. Cruz had a chance to throw the lead runner out at home, but you have to glove the ball first to do that. It was a bad night for the defense.

Brant Hurter is making a rehab appearance in Toledo tonight and…Trei Cruz probably wants this one back. pic.twitter.com/Soglb1j6wN

Stevenson made up for his earlier mistake by hitting an RBI double in the bottom of the seventh. He came home a few batters later on a Wenceel Perez sac fly. That was all of the meaningful offense for Toledo, though.

6 gets us on the board 👏 pic.twitter.com/GWBrPjzvlr

Ricky Vanasco faced the minimum in the eighth, thanks to an inning-ending double play, and went 1-2-3 in the ninth.

Stevenson: 2-4, 2B (7), R, RBI, K

Edwards Jr. (L, 4-10): 6.0 IP, 5 R, 1 ER, 7 H, 0 BB, 8 K, HR

Coming Up Next: It's a noon ET start on Sunday. Omaha leads the series, 4-1.

It was a big home run day for Erie, with the SeaWolves sending the ball into the stands six times. Izaac Pacheco and E.J. Exposito each hit multiple long balls, going back-to-back in the first and fifth innings. Pacheco hit a third homer in the seventh for good measure.

SeaWolves homer their way to a 10-6 win over the Curve @PALottery #Sponsored pic.twitter.com/OjBZ5TFcjn

The other home run came from Thayron Liranzo, also in the first. It was a two-run shot and his second in as many games. Roll the tape!

Thayron launches to get us started! pic.twitter.com/OVYSXZHZnS

Pacheco and Exposito were next, and neither were wallscrapers.

Max Alba had plenty of run support to work with after the first, but he gave up four runs over his 5.1 innings of work. A solo homer in the first got Altoona on the board, and a sac fly in the fourth made it 4-2. Alba gave up six hits and two walks overall, so it wasn't a runaway win by any means.

Pacheco and Exposito did it again in the fifth, this time with a little less power, but both went to center field. Exposito leads the team with 20 homers, but Pacheco is closing in after this explosive night.

Izaac Pacheco smashes a 2-run homer to left center. It’s his 2nd of the game. pic.twitter.com/QcqoBHfiak

E.J. Exposito launches a solo homer to dead center for his 2nd home run of the game. Give him 20 on the year now. @ZachSurdenik on the call. pic.twitter.com/zrtcY0PNiU

Alba left the game in the sixth with one out and two on. Tyler Owens took over and immediately gave up a two-run, ground-rule double, with both runs going on Alba's line. Owens wasn't particularly sharp, walking a batter and giving up an RBI single later in the inning, keeping it a two-run game.

Josue Briceno created some separation in the bottom of the sixth with a sac fly, but Wandisson Charles gave that run right back to Altoona in the seventh.

Pacheco's third home run of the night and 15th of the year came in the seventh. It served as the final blow of the game, but a six-homer night ending with a four-run differential feels a bit off. A win's a win, though.

Izaac Pacheco goes yard for a third time this game, another 2-run shot. 🚨🚨🚨 pic.twitter.com/YZe1dzg0LD

Izaac Pacheco with his first pro game in which he has hit 3 home runs. pic.twitter.com/YgRicG27FR

Charles went 1-2-3 in the eighth and Trevin Micahel closed things out with a 1-2-3 ninth.

.@erie_seawolves manager Tony Cappuccili talking to the media after Erie hit six home runs in the 10-6 win pic.twitter.com/Rex6csPQdT

Pacheco: 3-4, 3 HR (15), 3 R, 5 RBI

Liranzo: 1-3, HR (12), R, 2 RBI, BB, K

Exposito: 2-4, 2 HR (20), 2 R, 2 RBI

Alba (W, 2-4): 5.1 IP, 4 ER, 6 H, 2 BB, 0 K, HR

Coming Up Next: It's a 1:35 p.m. ET start on Sunday. Erie leads the series, 3-2.

Back-to-back days with 14 runs for West Michigan. Not too shabby. All of those runs came in the first four innings, with 10 coming in the third alone. You'd think this was another home run barrage, but the Whitecaps had zero homers and just two extra-base hits. Singles and walks, baby. That's baseball at its purest.

Singles from Woody Hadeen and Roberto Campos got things going in the first. Fort Wayne starter Bryan Balzer tried to give West Michigan more runs in the opening frame, but the Whitecaps stranded the bases loaded.

Hadeen doubled in the second, moving Juan Hernandez to third. Bryce Rainer scored him on a sac fly right after.

Brady Smith's first start in the Tigers farm went well, but a two-run homer in the second made it a tie ball game. Those were the only two runs he allowed, though. He gave up two hits and three walks while striking out four over five innings.

Brady Smith broke out his nasty changeup in the 3rd inning… pic.twitter.com/pRRqbCF0Ya

Then, the big inning came. Balzer gave up a leadoff single to Clayton Campbell and hit Luke Shliger. He loaded the bases with a walk to Jackson Strong, and another walk to Andrew Sojka gave West Michigan the lead back.

The TinCaps changed pitchers, but it didn't help. Javie Chacon hit Cristian Santana for another free run, and then Hernandez and Hadeen hit back-to-back RBI singles. All of a sudden it was 7-2, in favor of the Whitecaps.

Woody Hadeen rips an RBI single past the shortstop to put the Whitecaps up 7-2. He has three hits in three innings today. pic.twitter.com/m2w411DrCX

Another single from Roberto Campos gave West Michigan its eighth run, and Campbell walked for the second time in the inning. Shliger hit a sac fly, and Strong reached on an error. Chacon hit Sojka, and Santana singled in Strong to cap off the 10-run frame.

Roberto Campos drops a single into left center for his 2nd RBI of the night. pic.twitter.com/9Ixr8ORng4

Campell hit a sac fly in the fourth, and a wild pitch put West Michigan ahead by a dozen. Smith cruised and turned it over to the bullpen in the sixth.

Logan Berrier gave up three runs over his two innings of work, but that was only enough to cut Fort Wayne's deficit to single digits. Juanmi Vasquez had trouble getting the third out in the eighth, so Jalen Evans had to come in and finish things out. Evans was sharp with three strikeouts.

Hadeen: 4-6, 2B (14), 3 R, RBI, BB, K

Rainer: 1-5, 2B (19), R, RBI, 3 K

Smith (W, 1-1): 5.0 IP, 2 ER, 2 H, 3 BB, 4 K, HR

Coming Up Next: It's a 1:05 p.m. ET start on Sunday. West Michigan leads the series, 4-1.
