title: McKenna claims IBF middleweight title in Dublin
description: Aaron McKenna produces a dominant performance against Etinosa Oliha to claim the IBF world middleweight title in his first professional fight on Irish soil.
fullText:
Aaron McKenna produced a composed and dominant performance against previously unbeaten Etinosa Oliha to claim the IBF world middleweight title in his first professional fight on Irish soil at Dublin's 3Arena.

The Monaghan fighter extended his perfect professional record to 21-0 after controlling much of the 12-round contest to claim a unanimous decision victory at Zuffa Boxing 10.

McKenna earned scores of 118-110, 117-111 and 116-112 on the judges' scorecards to hand the now 22-1 Italian his first professional defeat.

Afterwards, McKenna reflected on fulfilling a childhood ambition after nine years as a professional without fighting in Ireland.

"A new world champion. I said it for years," McKenna told Sky Sports.

"Since I was six years old, I thought about this moment my whole life, so for it to finally happen at 27, it goes to show everyone, don't give up, always stay true to yourself, and you can do anything."

McKenna admitted Oliha provided a sterner challenge than expected and welcomed all challengers.

"Oliha was definitely strong. I made it harder than it should have been, but I got the job done.

"It doesn't matter [who's next], anyone. I'm easy to find now that I have a belt. I want to collect every belt in boxing. I'm the best middleweight in the world, and super-middleweight; I don't mind jumping up either."

Oliha began positively and applied pressure during the cagey opening rounds, enjoying particular success in the second as McKenna looked to establish his jab from the back foot.

McKenna, known as 'The Silencer' gradually found his rhythm, repeatedly landing his jab and uppercut while using his range effectively to avoid Oliha's heavier attacks.

The 27-year-old increasingly took control, forcing Oliha onto the ropes and landing combinations to the head and body.

Oliha continued to march forward, but McKenna's movement and defence largely nullified the Italian's pressure as he continued to land the cleaner shots.

A clash of heads left McKenna bleeding in the 11th, but he remained composed and landed several clean shots in response.

Oliha pushed forward in search of a dramatic finish in the final round, but McKenna continued to frustrate him with his jab before the final bell prompted celebrations from the Dublin crowd.

Simpson avenges only loss in Williamson rematch

In the co-main event, Cork native Callum Walsh defeated former European champion Tyler Denny by decision after a gritty 10-round battle, extending his unbeaten record to 17-0 as native fighters completed a clean sweep of wins in the Irish capital.

Joe Ward marked his return from a two-year absence with a victory over previously unbeaten Artjom Kasparian, as the Athlone boxer settled into the contest and finished strongly to earn a decision win.

In the prelims, Stevie 'The Hitman' McKenna - brother of headliner Aaron - produced an emphatic first-round knockout of Owen O'Neill, dropping the Belfast fighter with a powerful right hand just over a minute into their middleweight contest.

Derry's Connor Coyle improved to 23-0 with a unanimous decision victory over Mark Beuke, while Patrick O'Connor stopped Juan Manuel Moriel after the opening round.

title: Sabalenka and Norrie exit Canadian Open in last 16
description: World number one Aryna Sabalenka suffers a surprise defeat at the Canadian Open, while Britain's Cameron Norrie also bows out in the last 16 in Toronto.
fullText:
Women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffered a surprise defeat in the Canadian Open weeks before she begins her US Open title defence, while Britain's Cameron Norrie also bowed out in the last 16.

Sabalenka lost 7-6 (7-3) 4-6 6-4 to Russia's Ekaterina Alexandrova in a match lasting almost two and a half hours in Toronto.

The Belarusian recovered from a set down to force a decider, but a double fault when serving to stay in the match handed the number 16 seed victory.

It is the latest defeat in what has been a difficult summer for Sabalenka, who was knocked out in the quarter-finals and last 16 of the French Open and Wimbledon respectively.

"I just tried to play every single point as if it was the last one because with her, you don't [get] a lot of chances during the match," Alexandrova said.

"I'm super happy that I could win because after the second set, I thought [the chance] was already past me."

The Russian will face Ukraine's Elina Svitolina for a place in the semi-finals, after she defeated American eighth seed Amanda Anisimova 6-2 6-4.

Third seed Jessica Pegula suffered a first career loss to Diana Shnaider, as the 22-year-old finished both sets strongly to win 6-3 6-3.

The Russian will face Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals, after the seventh seed overcame opening set service troubles to defeat 10th seed Marta Kostyuk 3-6 6-1 6-2.

The six-time Grand Slam winner retired to the locker room after Kostyuk broke her serve four times during a shambolic a 39-minute opening set, but looked much improved when she returned.

In the men's event in Montreal, British number two Cameron Norrie spurned two set-point opportunities as he was defeated 6-2 7-6 (10-8) by 18th seed Arthur Fils.

Norrie saved three match points in the second set to force a tie-break, but the Frenchman broke his serve to win in one hour and 43 minutes.

Fils will meet Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar in the quarter-finals, after the 19-year-old upset eighth seed Jiri Lehecka 6-3 6-3.

Brandon Nakashima and Luciano Darderi also progressed to the next round with gruelling three-set victories over Arthur Rinderknech and Nuno Borges respectively.

Italian Darderi used a mid-match changeover to enjoy an espresso as he battled to a 4-6 6-3 7-5 win.

title: Murder investigation launched after man dies following 'violent disorder' in village
description: Seven men are in custody following the incident in Pontnewynydd, Torfaen, police said.
fullText:
Police have launched a murder investigation following the death of a man who was left in a critical condition after violence broke out in a village.

Anthony "Tony" Jones, 56, from Brecon suffered life-threatening injuries in an incident to which Gwent Police firearms officers were called in Pontnewynydd, near Pontypool, on Thursday.

The force said seven men aged 31, 39, 40, 45, 59, 61, and 73 had been arrested in connection to "disorder" and all seven remained in police custody.

Officers have appealed for anyone with information, CCTV or dashcam footage from the area between 19:00 and 19:30 BST to contact them.

On Saturday police said following Jones's death officers investigating the report of "violent disorder" were now conducting a murder investigation.

They said his family were being supported by specialist officers.

Det Ch Supt Anne-Marie Salwey said: "We're trying to establish the movements of those involved both before and after the disorder and are asking motorists who were driving along Hospital Road, Mill Road and the surrounding areas between 6pm and 9pm on Thursday to check their dashcam footage."

title: Trump suffers first-round defeat at China Open
description: World number one Judd Trump suffers a shock defeat by Thailand's Noppon Saengkham in the first round of the China Open.
fullText:
Judd Trump could lose his world number one ranking before the end of the month after suffering a shock defeat by Thailand's Noppon Saengkham in the first round of the China Open on Sunday.

Saengkham, ranked 45th in the world, claimed a 6-3 victory to set up a second-round meeting with either Ronnie O'Sullivan or Jackson Page.

Trump fought back from two frames down to level, before his opponent won three frames in a row to take control of the best-of-11 contest.

A match-high break of 120 put Saengkham 5-2 up, before the Thai won the final frame 78-0.

Trump, who won the China Open in 2011 and 2016, came into the event off the back of beating Kyren Wilson in the final of the invitational Shanghai Masters last week.

However, the 36-year-old has won just ranking tournaments in the past two years, the most recent of those the German Masters in February.

The China Open has returned to the World Snooker Tour calendar for the first time since 2019, and is now hosted in Taiyuan, 310 miles (500km) south west of Beijing, rather than the Chinese capital.

Trump has topped the world rankings since August 2024 but to have any chance of remaining at the summit he must win the Wuhan Open later this month and hope other results go his way.

Zhao Xintong is currently best placed to overtake Trump, with Neil Robertson and Wu Yize not far behind.

Trump was not the only seeded player to lose in the first round, as Barry Hawkins lost to Liu Hongyu, Mark Williams was defeated by Zhou Yuelong, and Ding Junhui was thrashed 6-1 by David Gilbert.

The winner of the tournament will receive prize money of £250,000, with the runner-up to bank £100,000.

title: Messi misses Miami defeat after death of father
description: Lionel Messi misses Inter Miami's Leagues Cup defeat by Monterrey on Saturday night after the death of his father.
fullText:
Lionel Messi missed Inter Miami's Leagues Cup defeat by Monterrey on Saturday night after the death of his father, as his team-mates led tributes before and during the match.

Jorge Messi died on Saturday at the age of 68 following a long illness.

Jorge, who had also been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14, passed away in a hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina.

Miami paid tribute to Messi's father with a minute's silence before kick-off, while players wore black armbands and Jorge's name was displayed on the big screens at Nu Stadium.

The club added a black ribbon to their social media profile pictures, and in a statement said: "Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family."

Messi's Argentina team-mate Rodrigo de Paul celebrated scoring the opening goal of the 2-1 defeat by taking off his shirt to reveal Messi's.

Fans held up handmade signs offering their support to Messi and paying tribute to his father.

Miami striker Luis Suarez, who missed the match through suspension, wrote on Instagram that Jorge will continue to watch over his son "with pride, as he always did".

Messi's former club Barcelona observed a moment of silence before their 1-0 friendly win against Nottingham Forest in Udine, Italy.

In 2000, Jorge accompanied his 13-year-old son to Catalonia and played a key role in persuading the club to sign him.

Barcelona thanked Jorge "for his commitment to our club, for entrusting us with the beginnings and the most glorious years of his son Leo's football career".

Fans left flags and flowers outside Messi's childhood home in Rosario, while Argentine giants Boca Juniors and River Plate both held periods of silence before their matches.

The Argentine Football Association said it "deeply mourns with sadness and sorrow the passing of Jorge Messi, father of our captain and emblem, Lionel Messi".

It added: "From here, we stand in solidarity with the entire family during this difficult time and send the most heartfelt, warm and affectionate embrace."

Paris St-Germain, for whom Messi played between 2021 and 2023 after leaving Barcelona, said: "The club sends its full support to Leo, his family and loved ones in this painful ordeal. May he rest in peace."

title: What are your favourite new kits for the coming season?
description: BBC Sport has rounded up some of the best new kits released by clubs around the world over the summer - vote for your top 10
fullText:
As a new season draws near, football-hungry fans around the country will be tweaking their fantasy teams, making themselves experts on rumoured transfer targets and keeping eyes keenly trained on new kit releases.

It's an exciting time for collectors, whether they're looking for never-before-seen designs, classic shirts reimagined or niche releases from far-flung lands to impress their colleagues at five-a-side.

BBC Sport has rounded up a non-exhaustive list of some of the best kit releases for 2026-27 so far, ordered alphabetically.

Scroll down to the bottom of the page to vote for your top 10.

Marking 20 years since AC Milan's last Champions League title, the Rossoneri's new away shirt is modelled by legendary former player Filippo Inzaghi - who won the trophy twice with the club, including scoring a brace in the 2007 final in Athens to beat Liverpool - and current defender Davide Bartesaghi.

League One side AFC Wimbledon's away kit, in red and yellow, shares the same colour palette as the kit the team wore on the day of their promotion to the top flight for the first time ever on 3 May 1986.

Marking 20 years since the Gunners moved to Emirates Stadium, Arsenal's new home shirt has a bold red base, with white accents.

Mikel Arteta's men kick off their Premier League title defence against promoted side Coventry City on Friday 21 August.

The north London club have reprised their famous yellow for this season's third strip, with a kit reminiscent of away shirts worn by Arsenal players during the late 1980s.

Aston Villa's new home kit is an instant classic. However, the club were warned over sportswashing after revealing Visit Rwanda - the African country's tourist board - as their new front-of-shirt sponsor last month.

Atletico Madrid's new home shirt platforms the Rojiblancos' famous stripes, together with a subtle trident motif - a symbol associated with the club's fans, who gather at Madrid's Neptune Fountain to celebrate victories.

The Blaugrana have adapted their traditional stripes for this year's home kit. Hansi Flick will be aiming for a third successive La Liga title since taking over as manager in May 2024.

Adidas have gone for a retro revival with many of their kits this year and Bayern Munich's away strip sits very much in that vein - simple, clean and with the traditional trefoil logo. Vincent Kompany's team reached the Champions League final last season and have become one of the most exciting teams to watch in Europe.

Blackburn Rovers' new partnership with Umbro has been launched with an absolute stunner of a kit.

After they survived relegation from the Championship last season, manager Tony Mowbray returned to Ewood Park in June for his second spell in charge at the club.

Bournemouth struck a club-record deal with new kit supplier Hummel in May.

German manager Marco Rose will succeed Andoni Iraola at Vitality Stadium this season after the Spaniard departed having led the Cherries to their first ever European qualification.

In a commitment to affordability and sustainability, Brentford announced earlier this month that their new home kit would also be worn during the 2027-28 season.

Brighton's new home kit, with its subtle pinstripes and white neckline, draws heavily on the strip worn by the Seagulls during the 1983 FA Cup final, which they lost 4-0 in a replay against Ron Atkinson's Manchester United.

Celtic's new home shirt celebrates 60 years since the Lisbon Lions defeated Inter Milan to win the European Cup at the Estadio Nacional in Lisbon, with a commemorative badge and inscription inside the neck.

Chelsea's new home kit pays homage to their nineties 'Italian Renaissance', when Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola helped bring success to the club, including the 1997 FA Cup and 1998 League Cup.

Mexican side Club America's new home shirt is inspired by one worn during the 1998-99 season, with the club's crest blown up across the torso.

Manager Cesc Fabregas has turned Como into a serious outfit and this is a serious kit to match. The Italian side qualified for the Champions League for the first time last season and will be hoping to kick on from there.

Coventry City's new home shirt draws inspiration from the kit worn by players during the 1987 FA Cup final victory over Tottenham Hotspur.

The Sky Blues will return to the Premier League in August for the first time in 25 years after gaining promotion under manager Frank Lampard.

Scottish Championship side Dunfermline Athletic have released a shirt that harks back to the one they wore during the 1994-95 season.

The Toffees' new home shirt draws inspiration from marine flags found around the docks at the Hill Dickinson stadium.

Turkish club Fenerbahce's new away shirt is inspired by the first kit the club ever wore when they were founded in 1907.

Marking the club's centenary, Fiorentina's new home shirt features an embossed pattern inspired by the ornamental frames of Renaissance art found in the city of Florence.

Fulham's away shirt is a reinterpretation of an iconic chequered jersey worn 30 years ago during the 1996-97 season.

In 1996-97, Grimsby Town played in an away kit that was almost identical to one worn by the likes of Roberto Baggio, George Weah and Paolo Maldini at AC Milan. With Lotto returning as the League Two club's kit supplier this season, that design has been revived for a new generation of Mariners fans.

Launching their new partnership with Oxen, Hull City have released a very retro kit for the new campaign, evoking the shirts the Tigers wore during the late seventies.

Sergej Jakirovic's team will return to the Premier League for the first time in a decade this season, kicking off their campaign at home against Manchester United on Saturday 22 August.

Ipswich Town return to the Premier League this season after they were relegated at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

The Tractor Boys' new home kit takes inspiration from the Sir Bobby Robson and Sir Alf Ramsey stands at Portman Road, with a motif copying the one that runs across the roof of the stadium.

After last season's experimental home kit, the Old Lady have returned to their traditional, thick stripes this year.

Leeds' new away shirt takes the Yorkshire rose from its club badge and repeats that motif across the base of the shirt. Blooming marvellous.

Liverpool's away shirt is inspired by the ticket stubs from European nights during the 1970s and 1980s. It also strongly brings to mind away and third kits worn during a successful period in the club's history during the late 1980s.

Liverpool's home kit for the 2026-27 campaign is a very conscious nod to the Adidas kit the Merseyside club wore between 1989-1991, during which time they won the 1989-90 First Division title under manager Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Lyon's home shirt for the new campaign pays tribute to the city, with Lyon's coat of arms silhouetted against the shirt sponsor and appearing as a subtle pattern across the stripes.

Manchester City's new home kit uses a sky blue gradient, with a print inside the neck, which reads, "Not Your Typical City". Following the departure of Pep Guardiola though, will it be typical City under new manager Enzo Maresca?

Manchester United's new away shirt is inspired by the Red Devils' 1988-90 third kit, which was only worn in three matches. The club have a history of success in blue however, having won both the 1968 European Cup final and 2017 Europa League final wearing blue kits.

Manchester United's new home kit, with its flat-knit striped collar and cuffs, is inspired by Red Devils kits from the late seventies.

To celebrate 150 years since they were founded, Championship club Middlesbrough have released this bold red and gold kit, with a special anniversary club badge displayed front and centre.

Napoli celebrate their founding in 1926 with this special kit in 'centenary blue', featuring a 100-year anniversary logo on the club badge.

Napoli's third kit evokes designs famously worn during the 1986-87 and 1988-90 seasons, when a certain Diego Maradona inspired the club to two Serie A titles.

Newcastle's new home kit uses what's been described as a 'disrupted stripe'. Just don't say it looks like a barcode. The Magpies are entering a new era this season after the shock departure of manager Eddie Howe.

French side Nice have released this classic home shirt and it is, dare we say, rather nice.

Nice's away shirt is another contender for kit of the season with its simple, but effective colour palette, classic fold-over collar and piping down the sleeves.

Nottingham Forest's home shirt is inspired by the mist that rolls in from the River Trent.

Oxford United teamed up with local street artist and lifelong U's supporter Andrew Manson to design this season's kit, along with a bespoke piece of artwork.

The European champions haven't tried to reinvent the wheel with this kit, but it oozes class. Can anyone stop Luis Enrique's side from winning a third successive Champions League trophy?

Primeira Liga champions Porto have released an away kit in gorgeous ruby - inspired by the port produced in the region as well as the River Douro.

Rangers' new home shirt is a classy affair. The Glasgow club will hope to exorcise the disappointment of last season's third-place finish under new manager Derek McInnes.

The stripes are narrower and there are interwoven diagonal lines, but this is still very definitely a Real Betis shirt - one of the most recognisable designs in European football.

Real Madrid have released their new away kit in a gorgeous, deep green, reminiscent of their 2012-13 third kit.

To celebrate their 100-year anniversary, La Liga club Real Oviedo have released a kit worth waiting a century for.

La Liga 2 side Real Valladolid's home shirt uses the club's traditional stripes, with a silhouette showing the Province of Valladolid stitched into the kit.

Sampdoria's home kit will remind fans of a certain vintage of Saturdays and Sundays spent watching David Platt represent the Serie A side on Channel 4's Football Italia.

To celebrate the club's 80-year anniversary, the shirt comes with a subtle anniversary logo embossed across the chest.

Sheffield United's away kit revives a classic style worn by the Blades during the 1975-76 season.

That campaign ended in relegation from the First Division for the Yorkshire club, but it's an iconic design nonetheless.

Ligue 1 side Strasbourg have joined the nineties revival. Their new away kit uses diamond graphics synonymous with Adidas kits from that decade, including the strips worn by the French side themselves between 1994-96.

In one of the more unexpected launches this summer, Sunderland have collaborated with the Elvis Presley estate to release this striking kit in a colourway synonymous with the King's early years in Louisiana.

Elvis' 'Can't Help Falling in Love' has been a matchday anthem for the North East club since the late seventies.

For their new home shirt, the Black Cats have drawn inspiration from the shirt worn by players during the club's first FA Cup victory at Wembley over Preston North End in 1937. A jacquard 'S' in the style of the handles of the FA Cup trophy is repeated across the base of the jersey.

After recording their highest ever WSL points total last season, Spurs are looking towards a bright future with big ambitions in the transfer market. Meanwhile, new manger Roberto de Zerbi is hoping to drag the men's side up from the depths.

To dare is to do and this kit is nothing if not daring.

Serie A club Venezia have released some of the most sought-after kits of recent years and this season's home shirt is sure to be no exception.

Wrexham's new home shirt pays tribute to their stadium, the Racecourse Ground, with a pattern reflecting the old Kop's barriers embossed into the weave of the fabric. The stand was demolished in 2023 to make way for redevelopment.

title: Carrington makes 'white privilege' post after ejection
description: Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington is ejected from her side's defeat by Indiana Fever for committing a hard foul, before taking to social media to post "white privilege".
fullText:
Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington was ejected from her side's WNBA defeat by Indiana Fever for committing a hard foul on Sophie Cunningham, and subsequently posted "white privilege" on social media.

Carrington caught Cunningham across the left side of the head with her arm as the Indiana Fever guard attempted a right-handed layup late in the opening quarter in Chicago.

Cunningham hit the ground hard but immediately got up to confront Carrington before team-mates separated them.

The foul was upgraded to a flagrant two foul after review and Carrington was automatically ejected from the match after scoring eight points in four minutes from the bench.

Shortly after leaving the game, Carrington wrote "WHITE PRIVILIGE" on social media platform Threads, tagging Indiana Fever in the post.

Asked about the post after her team won 90-86, Cunningham said: "I think the league is taking care of that.

"This has nothing to do with race. Last year, I did the same thing and I got kicked out, and I deserved to be kicked out. There's no reason even to play that card."

When told of the post, Sky coach Tyler Marsh added: "I have to get back to you on that because I'm just now hearing about that. So yeah, we'll handle that."

Speaking about the foul, Cunningham added: "Clearly, I think it was unnecessary.

"I've never really spoken to her and have no beef with her, but I guess she has some pent-up stuff. So, get your [stuff] off. That's fine - I can take it."

Fever coach Stephanie White said: "It was a hard foul. I don't think that DiJonai intentionally came out to get her across the neck like she did, but it did happen, and I thought it was the right call."

Referee Maj Forsberg said Cunningham was not penalised for her reaction because "we deemed her reaction to the severity of the contact to be acceptable".

Cunningham has become the subject of controversy in recent weeks for her comments on transgender athletes participating in women's sport.

It has led to people showing up inside and outside of Fever games, some to protest against Cunningham and others to express support.

Meanwhile, Fever star Caitlin Clark will avoid a one-match suspension after a technical foul called on her during the third quarter was rescinded after the match.

The technical foul - called when Clark ran into an official after making a pass having been bumped by a defender - would have been her eighth of the season, which triggers an automatic suspension.

title: Unmasking London City's Spanish superstar
description: Alexia Putellas' arrival at London City Lionesses was the biggest transfer in WSL history - but who is the person behind the global stardom?
fullText:
There is not a single empty seat as Alexia Putellas walks into a room at a hotel in Maidstone ready to speak to the English media for the first time.

"Woah," the two-time Ballon d'Or winner says as she opens the door and sees all the journalists looking in her direction, eager to finally meet her.

You would think that somebody who is referred to as 'La Reina' - the queen - in Spain is used to that kind of attention.

She is considered one of the greatest players of her generation, captained Barcelona to a fourth Women's Champions League title in May and is a World Cup winner with Spain.

But Putellas, who signed for London City Lionesses this summer in what is being touted as the biggest signing in WSL history, is embarking on a different journey with her new club that brings all the stresses and uncertainties anyone would face.

She sat down with the BBC's Women's Football Weekly podcast and addressed media in a press conference that helped unmask the global superstar.

From Barcelona to Bromley: Inside Putellas' move to LCL

Putellas was born in a municipality of Catalonia called Mollet del Valles in the province of Barcelona, and regularly watched games at Nou Camp as a child.

Former Spain and Barcelona star Andres Iniesta was an inspiration to her, while she has also named Brazilian duo Rivaldo and Ronaldinho as players she idolised.

Putellas attended summer football camps ran by Xavi and played for local side CE Sabadell as a child.

She spent a year at La Masia, Barcelona's famous youth academy, but had to leave when her girls team was disbanded.

After spells at Espanyol and Levante, she eventually returned to Barca in 2012 - the start of an incredible 14-year career with her childhood club.

"In Spain, football is the typical sport. When I was young, [it was] not for women, but fortunately, nowadays it is," said Putellas.

"I just had the ball at my feet and I was playing all the time - in the park, in the streets, sometimes at home.

"For me, it was normal because in my house Barca games were always on the TV. I started by watching games and then suddenly, I had the ball all day."

The 32-year-old went on to win 38 trophies with Barcelona, including 10 league titles and four European cups.

She was awarded back-to-back Ballon d'Or crowns in 2021 and 2022 and is favourite to win it again this year.

Internationally, she helped Spain win the 2023 World Cup and finish runners-up at Euro 2025.

But Putellas is not done. When asked if she can still get better, she laughed and said: "Yeah, of course. Always. Day after day, I want to learn things.

"That's the way I see this job. Just keep going, never stop and be as good as I can."

She described the journey she has embarked on at London City Lionesses as one that can help her "find where my limits are" as a footballer.

Putellas is enjoying pre-season but her focus never fully switches off.

"It's all about Manchester United," she says as she looks ahead to London City's season opener on 4 September (19:00 BST).

She has given up Champions League football to join London City, an independent women's-only club in its infancy. Will she need to adapt her mindset?

"Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I'm going to bring to the project whatever it needs from me," she added.

"I'm 100% committed. I'm hungry to win, I'm hungry to be better day after day and to fight with my team-mates for the victory."

Her competitiveness shines through in every conversation.

She is handed a present - a game based on the London underground - by BBC Sport.

"Oh yes, I will play with Freya Godfrey, then I can win. I will tell her that," she jokes.

That winning mentality has never changed - but she gained a new perspective when an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury ruled her out of Euro 2022 on the eve of the tournament.

"Since the ACL injury, I enjoy everything. It's not enjoying just having fun, it's about learning something, and then I enjoy learning that thing," she added.

"I'm just a person who loves what she does. I love competition, I love football, I love training, I love to improve.

"I'm just always looking forward to better things and that's why I'm here too, because I always need to be moving as a person and a player."

Putellas is still learning the English language. She reminds journalists of that when she tries to breakdown the WSL's tactics.

"Sorry guys, I'm learning football language. This press conference maybe came early!" she jokes.

Her best friend and team mate Jana Fernandez will likely help her learn quickly, as well as several other Spaniards, including summer signing Mapi Leon from Barcelona.

But she has a better grasp of English than she realises and it is clear by the way she talks that her footballing brain is unique.

Her manager Eder Maestre says Putellas is like a secondary coach on the training pitch and has the ability to conduct the way the team plays.

"In my opinion, if I give you a pass without speaking, you have information. That's one thing I learned in Barcelona," she told the BBC.

"Maybe I am giving you that pass because I want them to receive a message like 'we go' or 'we stay.' If it's a stronger pass, it's for them to control or I want them to switch the game or whatever - it's just football language.

"Maybe I improved that in Barcelona because of the style of play. The best drills I ever trained in is about understanding what's happening in the game.

"If you understand what's happening in the game, you will get one step ahead of the opponents. When I'm training, I try to understand the way we want to play."

Putellas' fame is widespread and her grandeur was epitomised by her London City unveiling alongside billionaire owner Michele Kang in New York.

There was an emotional outpouring at her Barca departure on social media and she has 3.4m followers on Instagram.

A mural of Putellas dressed as a superhero was painted in her hometown and Nike gifted her a custom gold crown following her second Ballon d'Or victory.

"I try to not think about it, and just be like, I don't know if the word is normal, but just be me. For me, it's normal to be me," said Putellas.

She admitted walking into her first English press conference was "a little scary" and she does not generally enjoy being the centre of attention.

Her favourite part of the media day, she joked, was getting away from the cameras.

Even in the dressing room, where she is no doubt idolised by those around her, she says having former team-mates like Leon there "makes her feel more confident".

But despite the shyness, Putellas does not look out of place in the limelight. She has an obvious aura and instantly eases apprehension with humour.

In an exchange about her passing on her crown at Barcelona she quickly interjects: "No, I didn't have a crown! It's just media stuff!"

She adds: "I was just like another team-mate and so I feel like that, even if they call me 'La Reina.'

"I don't think anybody else needs to imagine 'I have a crown' and all of this because they are so good, they don't need anything from me.

"I just hope I left the team in a better position than when I started. That would make me feel so good and I enjoyed playing with them - I hope they enjoyed it as well."

Putellas' first few weeks at London City have been full of the challenges that most normal people experience - searching for a house, learning to drive in London, adapting to a new culture and developing her English.

"I have been looking for an apartment. [It's] not cheap. Well, in Barcelona, it's not cheap as well!" she said.

"Looking for where I have to go for shopping, just normal things that in Barcelona, of course, I knew. Now, here, everything is new. There's a lot of traffic here."

She has had family over to visit and has created a list of things to do in London with best friend and team-mate Fernandez.

Putellas was hoping to have dinner with England international and ex-Barcelona team-mate Keira Walsh last week but it had to be postponed.

Her friends in the WSL did give Putellas a warm welcome though...

"Well, some of them told me that it's a hard league and they're going to kick me! But no problem, I'm ready for that. No, I'm just joking...

"[They said] just enjoy the league because the games are crazy and even if you go to an away game, it's something different, something special."

Most of all, Putellas is learning to adapt to the English way of life.

She has tried a full English breakfast - but is not a fan of baked beans - and her TikTok algorithm is already throwing up typical conversational words like "innit".

"I tried an English breakfast. It's quite different from Spain. [I didn't like] the beans, but the sausages and eggs... It was fine," she joked.

"For Spanish people it's weird. Normally, we [have beans] with dinner or lunch, but not for breakfast. I don't know English culture yet!

"The weather is not bad now but I say that and people tell me, 'okay, wait for October and November.'"

But while Putellas is still adapting to life in England, it is clear she is ready to perform for London City Lionesses in September.

Her debut is likely to attract widespread attention and she hopes to embrace the occasion - after all, this is the challenge she craved.

title: I'm the founder of a private jet company. I eat dinner when the locals do and end most days in my at-home bowling alley.
description: Thomas Flohr is the founder of VistaJet, a private aviation service. He's based in Switzerland but travels often between their 25 offices worldwide.
fullText:
This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Thomas Flohr, the 65-year-old founder, chairman, and CEO of VistaJet, based in St. Moritz, Switzerland, about his daily routine. It's been edited for length and clarity.

I started my career at a Chicago-based technology firm in 1985 and rose through the ranks. I later acquired most of the company's European operations through my company, Comprendium Investment.

My frequent business travel in the early 2000s exposed me to the shortcomings of private aviation. At the time, I found the private jet experience to be inconsistent and underwhelming. The service quality didn't match the level of luxury that clients paying $10,000 to $15,000 an hour expected. I didn't see a good solution in the market and initially thought about paying for fractional jet ownership before deciding against it.

Business Insider's Power Hours series gives readers an inside look at how powerful leaders in business structure their workday. Reach out to editor Lauryn Haas to share your daily routine.

After exploring all other options, I bought a Learjet 60 in 2003, and that plane became the foundation for starting VistaJet in 2004. Vista is a private aviation subscription service that provides access to over 270 customized business jets for clients in 187 countries.

My primary job is building client relationships and setting the company's strategic direction. Here's what a typical day in my life looks like.

Our company is headquartered in Dubai, but I travel frequently and usually work from any of our 25 offices worldwide, including my home office in St. Moritz. I wake up at different times, depending on where I am. If I'm in America, I start earlier to sync with Europe. In the Middle East, I work late into the night to overlap with American and European business hours.

In St. Moritz, my mornings start around 8 a.m. I shower, grab coffee, and ease into the day. I don't eat breakfast.

I prefer not to reach for my phone right away. About 45 minutes after my coffee, I'll respond to overnight emails and messages before diving into the day's activities.

I maintain several offices in different locations so my executives can use them when I'm not around. If I'm home, I'll work from my home office. If I'm on the road, I'll work on the plane or at my destination.

Sometimes, I work from the hotel in the morning and knock out key business tasks. If I'm in Dubai, London, New York, or a city with a VistaJet office, I'll head there in the afternoon for team and client meetings.

I often sit where the action is with the team or join executive committee members in their offices.

I prioritize client meetings before internal ones and don't believe internal meetings should take more than 20 to 30 minutes unless there's a compelling reason.

When clients call me directly, it's usually because they're about to make a significant decision, like buying a plane or finalizing a global flight plan. I also work on product development, brainstorming new services and product feature updates between calls and meetings.

As a founder, I'm still very hands-on, and I'm in constant communication with my finance and operations teams.

For lunch, I keep it very light and healthy. I usually eat vegetable soup, a fruit platter, or a light Japanese sashimi dish.

If I'm having a client lunch meeting, I prefer to eat at restaurants that use high-quality ingredients. Some of my favorite restaurants include Scott's in Mayfair, London, and Gaia in Dubai. When I eat out, I mostly get grilled seafood and boiled potatoes — nothing fancy.

The afternoon often means syncing with our US and European teams. In our business, there's no shortage of unusual requests that require creative solutions. One memorable request involved helping a client run three marathons on three continents in one week. It was a significant logistical undertaking, but we successfully pulled it off for the client.

Another request involved helping a corporate client coordinate the flight of executives from four continents to a board meeting in India, ensuring they all arrived precisely on time and returned home safely afterward.

If there's a gap between meetings, I'll take a 10-15-minute break to walk outside and get some fresh air. I try to prioritize these short breaks to clear my head and reset, but most of the time, the day runs nonstop.

I'm a firm believer in an integrated life. I don't view work and life as separate entities that need to be balanced against each other. Instead, I see everything in life as one endurance effort, whether in business or sports like car racing.

The time I eat dinner varies depending on my location. In some countries, I eat at 7 p.m.; in others, at 9 or 9:30 p.m. I adapt to the time zone and cultural norms. When I'm home, I eat dinner around 8:30 p.m., but I'm always available for client calls if needed.

I enjoy cooking and dining with friends and family. I have a bowling alley in my home, so we head downstairs for a few rounds after dinner. It's a great way to unwind and stir up friendly competition.

With so much digital stimulation during the day, I avoid screens at night. I don't watch TV, but I listen to classical music or rock from the late '70s and early '80s before bed.

I usually fall asleep around 11:30 p.m., sleeping seven hours on weeknights and nine on weekends.

Despite flying around 500 hours annually, I make time for things I enjoy. I'm a big fan of simple living and doing things in nature, like walking, hiking, and shopping at my local market for fruits and vegetables.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

title: Female artists garden told to vacate roof terrace
description: The Artist's Garden on the roof of Temple Station is told to move out for a repair assessment.
fullText:
A free public sculpture space dedicated to the work of female artists has been told to vacate its central London site.

The Artist's Garden on the roof of Temple Station has been told by owner Places for London, Transport for London's commercial property arm, to move out so that the area can be assessed for potential repairs.

Alice Walters, deputy director at theCOLAB, the charity that organises art for the garden, said she was worried the project would be "gone for good" after it moved out.

Westminster City Council, which manages the terrace space, said it was supportive of The Artist's Garden and would work with all parties involved to find a solution.

The sculpture garden, which has existed for five years on the roof, allows visitors to sit with, touch and interact with art.

Walters said: "We welcome over 100,000 visitors here each year completely for free.

"We were told that Places for London would like us to vacate the site entirely by 1 October.

"They've cited the need to carry out essential safety repairs, but once a project like this is gone, it's gone for good and it's not coming back."

Places for London said that the space was legally protected and would always remain publicly accessible.

It added that while it was developing future plans for the terrace at Temple, the organisation was working with the council and stakeholders to explore alternative nearby locations nearby for The Artist's Garden.

Lakwena Maciver exhibited an installation at The Artist's Garden when it opened in 2021.

She said: "I was the first ever artist to exhibit here and it was a takeover of the whole roof terrace with a tiled mosaic.

"For me it was about a return to public space post-lockdown.

"It's just really important to have places that are open access that anyone can come to that you don't have to pay for or book - it's really important that we keep these types of spaces."

Visitors to the sculpture garden told BBC London it was a "gorgeous" place to visit in the capital.

One woman said: It's wonderful to have it in the heart of the city, surrounded by buildings and the river. Just to have this immersive art space, it's great."

Another added: "It's a nice, peaceful place to come, just in the middle of the city. It's just beautiful and there's loads of seating. It's just gorgeous."

Lisa Vandy, who has exhibited two sculptures in the garden, said the site promoted visibility.

"I don't remember in my childhood ever seeing someone like me or their work, so it's [about] visibility, it's cultural importance, it's educational importance. This really has to stay here."

A spokesperson for Places for London said they recognised how the "much-loved" garden had contributed to "artists, young people and the local community".

"However, the terrace and station roof may now require essential repair and safety works, and the space needs to be cleared for the assessment of the extent of the works required," they said.

Places for London said any future proposals for the terrace would protect public access and support the area's cultural character.

title: Taipei says China's traffic control order for Taiwan Strait during typhoon is 'ridiculous'
description: China's attempt to implement traffic control measures on shipping heading into the Taiwan Strait during Typhoon Dolphin is "ridiculous", Taipei said, adding that Beijing has
fullText:
TAIPEI, Aug 8 (Reuters) - China's attempt to implement traffic control measures on shipping heading into the Taiwan Strait during Typhoon Dolphin is "ridiculous", ‌Taipei said, adding that Beijing has no right to restrict access ‌to international waters.

China, which views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, also claims the ​strategic strait through which billions of dollars of trade flow every year — a claim both Taipei and Washington reject.

On Wednesday, Chinese state media said that due to the approach of the typhoon, starting from Thursday night, ships heading north through ‌the southern entrance of ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed traffic control measures.

All vessels must comply with requirements, choose safe waters to shelter from the ⁠storm, and follow the instructions of on-site maritime management authorities to ensure safety at sea, it said.

"The unreasonable and crude statement by the relevant Chinese Communist departments ​reflects an ​ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international ​order and norms. It is utterly ‌ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late Friday.

"Taiwan's own affairs need no meddling from the Chinese Communists," it added.

In a separate statement released at the same time, Taiwan's Coast Guard said it had not detected any "abnormal movements" by Chinese vessels, nor had any shipping companies reported being ‌subjected to "broadcast interference".

Merchant and cargo ships transiting the ​area should disregard any Chinese broadcast demands ​they may receive, and immediately ​report such incidents, the Coast Guard added, saying it would ‌take all necessary measures to ensure ​freedom and safety of ​navigation.

The typhoon is tracking to the north of Taiwan and is expected to make landfall on China's east coast late Saturday or early ​Sunday.

China's military operates in ‌the strait on an almost daily basis.

Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty ​claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future.

title: Florida business owners allegedly scattered 1,500 mothballs on beach to send endangered birds packing
description: Two St. Pete Beach business owners allegedly spread 1,500 toxic mothballs on sand to stop black skimmers from nesting and are facing felony charges.
fullText:
Two Florida business owners have been charged with third-degree felonies after allegedly spreading about 1,500 "toxic" mothballs across a beach in hopes of keeping an "imperiled" bird species from nesting there.

If convicted, they could each face up to five years in prison, fines of up to $5,000 and up to five years of probation.

The problem started in late April when beachgoers noticed mothballs on the white, sugary sand on St. Pete Beach in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Officers with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) and bird-loving volunteers from the Audubon Society mobilized. They plucked about 1,000 of the small, white orbs from the sand behind the Plaza Beach Hotel.

Massachusetts Homeowners Stunned After Town Warns July 4 Flags Threaten Endangered Birds

Then 500 more appeared overnight.

The smelly balls containing pesticides dotted an area where endangered shorebirds known as black skimmers were "attempting to establish a nesting colony," FWC officials said at a news conference. Their placement also meant other wildlife and children "could easily come in contact with them."

It quickly became clear that someone might be targeting the birds, they said.

So FWC investigators flew into action.

The discovery of the mothballs ruffled feathers in the community.

There was "a lot of public outcry," expressing concern for the birds, while investigators tried to locate the source of the mothballs, FWC officials said.

Law enforcement served search warrants, combed through "terabytes" of data and eventually seized cellphones to try to locate the individuals behind the caper.

That work led them to Christopher Monroe, owner and manager of Chris's Beachside Bar, and Robert Czyszczon, owner of the Plaza Beach Hotel, FWC officials said.

Out of fear of lost revenue, the two allegedly hatched a plan to use mothballs to deter birds from congregating on the beach behind their businesses, authorities said.

Hikers Face $25,000 Fine After Off-leash Dog Barked At Grizzly Bear On Banff National Park Trail

Through video surveillance and receipt records, investigators found that Czyszczon spent about $60 buying "a large quantity" of mothballs at a Walmart the day before they first appeared on the beach, FWC officials said.

Upon examining his phone, investigators found "incriminating" text messages between him and fellow business owner Monroe discussing their objections to the native fowl.

Text conversations revealed plans for placement of the mothballs on the beach, officials said. That's what led investigators to Monroe as a suspect.

The men discussed how they "were going to do something" to prevent the birds from nesting on the beach, FWC officials said.

Black skimmers don't nest in trees. They kick beach sand to make depressions on the ground. Then they lay their eggs and raise their young near the surf.

"They're the worst birds," one of the men allegedly wrote in anticipation of nesting season.

"The bird people will put up fence around the area, and then the beach people will not be able to get to and from because they will fence around that space."

Cellphone tower data showed Monroe's phone was at the same location as Czyszczon's phone on both nights when the mothballs appeared on the beach, FWC officials said.

The men feared that nests on the beach would lead to fewer customers and less money being spent there, authorities said.

"Why didn't you tell me we lose $25,000 to $50,000?" one allegedly wrote in a text.

Monroe and Czyszczon were charged with illegal dumping, a third-degree felony, according to Pinellas County court records. They also were charged with the "attempted take of a state-listed imperiled species by harassment," a misdemeanor, according to FWC officials.

Massachusetts Homeowners Stunned After Town Warns July 4 Flags Threaten Endangered Birds

Like What You're Reading? Click Here For More

About 6,800 black skimmers live in Florida. FWC officials estimate that several hundred live on the beaches of Pinellas County.

The pesticide in mothballs can harm people and wildlife that come into contact with their vapors, according to an educational publication by the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (IFAS).

"With any pesticide, the label is the law," Brett W. Bultemeier, director of the UF/IFAS Pesticide Information Office, wrote in a 2021 educational publication about mothballs. "The label language is not simply a set of directions. Rather, they are requirements that are legally enforceable."

The birds probably weren't hurt by the "harassment," FWC officials said.

But it did delay their nesting, they said. That pushes the date that their young can fledge from the nest further back in the season. And that could put them in danger.

A big storm at the end of hurricane season, which ends on Nov. 30, "can wipe out a colony if those young birds haven't fledged yet," an FWC official said.

An attorney for Czyszczon did not respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital. Court records indicate that Monroe doesn't have an attorney. He couldn't be reached for comment.

title: AI push is putting banks at mercy of tech firms, warns Moody’s
description:
Finance sector will gain from the tech but it will need substantial investment and create risks, says rating agency
The rating agency Moody’s has said the race to adopt AI is putting big banks at the mercy of a small group of Silicon Valley firms, leaving them vulnerable to widespread outages and price gouging by profit-hungry tech bosses.
The financial sector’s efforts to integrate AI into day-to-day operations will eventually cut costs and increase revenues across the City and Wall Street, Moody’s said.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Finance sector will gain from the tech but it will need substantial investment and create risks, says rating agency

The rating agency Moody’s has said the race to adopt AI is putting big banks at the mercy of a small group of Silicon Valley firms, leaving them vulnerable to widespread outages and price gouging by profit-hungry tech bosses.

The financial sector’s efforts to integrate AI into day-to-day operations will eventually cut costs and increase revenues across the City and Wall Street, Moody’s said.

But that will require “substantial investments”, and with so many rivals racing towards the same goal, many of those benefits will end up being “competed away”.

AI will also create bigger risks around data privacy, cybersecurity, fraud and so-called “deposit flight”, as well as an overdependence on a small number of tech firms, the rating agency warned.

That will raise concerns for bosses across the financial sector. More than 75% of City companies now use AI, according to a UK Treasury select committee report published in January, with insurers and international banks among the biggest adopters. They are mostly using it to automate administrative tasks or even help with core operations, including processing insurance claims and assessing customers’ creditworthiness.

“The reliance of most financial firms on a relatively small set of foundation AI model and cloud computing providers risks creating a systemic dependency,” the Moody’s report said.

“This is because a model outage at one major provider could potentially spread quickly across customers and sectors. As AI adoption deepens, regulators may increase their focus on operational resilience and third-party concentration in the AI model stack.”

The AI race also risked creating “vendor dependence risk”, Moody’s said, meaning that “a set of dominant AI model and infrastructure providers could, over time, exert control over the price of AI services”. That issue is likely to emerge as the bosses of loss-making generative AI companies, including the ChatGPT creator OpenAI and the Claude owner Anthropic, come under pressure to deliver profits for investors.

“While this could pose credit risks to financial firms, they would nevertheless retain control over key assets, including proprietary data,” Moody’s said. Many big banks and insurers also have longstanding experience negotiating down tech contracts, and may be using open-source AI models, and striking key partnerships, to try to offset “dependency risks”.

Lloyds Banking Group’s chief executive, Charlie Nunn, recently doubled down on AI investment plans with a £13bn strategy that would involve using the technology to lure new business, improve efficiency and increase payouts for shareholders.

That will involve £2bn of cost cuts, which Nunn said would affect staff. “That is going to impact work. It is going to require us to continue to reskill people and hire new people, but that’s been my history for 30-odd years in financial services.”

Moody’s acknowledged the potential blow to some staff, who could be deemed replaceable as a result of new tech. Its report said there was a 20% chance that, by 2030, AI will be able to do the work of a “solid mid-level employee”.

For banks, AI might also make it easier for customers to switch to accounts offering higher interest rates, creating the possibility that large chunks of cash could be moved at short notice. “In this context, depositors’ trust in the institution and the resilience and stability of deposit funding are critical,” Moody’s said.

description: Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.
fullText:
Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.

Tens of thousands of fans attended both of those events, which took place virtually at the same time, right next to each other.

The sidewalks filled with streams of Seahawks fans with their sights set on Lumen Field, while the baseball faithful headed to T-Mobile Park:

For some fans, the choice between two beloved sports teams wasn't so easy.

"Go 'Hawks, go Mariners baby!" said Preston Erikson, who acknowledged it was impossible for him, his brother and their cousins to attend both. "No, we're not. We wish."

Fans of both teams acknowledged it was a fun problem to have. Seattle boasts a number of top-tier professional men's and women's sports teams, and it won rave reviews for its enthusiasm while hosting six World Cup matches.

"We are a great sports town. I just think- look across the street, you've got Mariners fans, you've got Seahawks fans. It just brings the whole city out. Everyone comes together," said Tijera Loggins.

Trey Erikson told KIRO 7 that there's something special about a sports town and the fans who support their teams.

"We've been in Seattle our whole lives, and it's just something where cultures come together, people come together. It's something words can't even describe. It's emotional. It's important, it's impactful, and it's powerful," he said.

There is an economic impact as well. Local shops and restaurants say business increases every time there's an event at Lumen or T-Mobile.

The economic impact of the World Cup alone here was predicted to be $850 million.

title: ODI Tri-series is back! ECB Chief says triangular ODI series' being planned after Shubman Gill comments
description: ECB chief Richard Gould confirms England remains open to reviving the triangular series. Get the details.
fullText:
ODI Tri-series is back! ECB Chief says triangular ODI series' being planned after Shubman Gill comments originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

ECB chief Gould confirms England remains open to tri-series fixtures.

India captain Shubman Gill wants multi-team tournaments back.

Several tri-series already scheduled under ICC's 2023-2027 FTP cycle.

England and Wales Cricket Board chief executive Richard Gould has responded positively to Indian ODI captain Shubman Gill's appeal for the return of triangular cricket tournaments, confirming that several tri-series fixtures are already lined up over the coming 12 to 18 months.

Gill has thrown his support behind the ICC's decision to leave the 50-over format untouched, describing the ODI World Cup as cricket's most prestigious global event. Rather than trimming matches down to 40 overs, he believes reviving multi-team formats like tri-series and quadrangular tournaments would do far more to reignite excitement around ODI cricket.

"I grew up watching 50-over cricket a lot, and it remained an integral part of my childhood," Gill said ahead of the first ODI in Birmingham against England. "When I think of the World Cup, the first thought that comes to mind is the 50-over World Cup. For me, the 50-over World Cup is the most prestigious World Cup. I don't think it should be changed to 40 overs."

Gill also fondly recalled watching several triangular series growing up, particularly those involving India, Australia and Sri Lanka, and described them as genuinely entertaining to follow.

"One thing is that we used to play a lot of triangular series and it was really fun to watch. India, Australia and Sri Lanka used to play those tournaments," he said.

"If I ever get a chance to play in a triangular series, it will be fun because you are not playing one team continuously. If we want to make this format more interesting, instead of having bilateral series, we can have triangular or quadrangular series. That'll be interesting to play and to watch."

MORE: India's 2036 Olympic bid receives ECB support

According to Dainik Jagran, Gould acknowledged that there's still room within international cricket's calendar for tri-series to make a comeback.

He noted that England's own scheduling priorities currently lean toward formats that don't stretch the calendar excessively, though the ECB remains open to exploring tri-series as a viable option going forward.

MORE: Brett Lee ignores Sachin Tendulkar as ex-Australia star names his pick

Several tri-series tournaments have already found their way back into cricket's calendar under the ICC's Future Tours Programme covering 2023 to 2027.

Pakistan hosted a tri-series in February 2025 involving New Zealand and South Africa, serving as a warm-up event ahead of that year's ICC Champions Trophy.

Looking further ahead, a T20I tri-series is scheduled for August-September 2026 in Windhoek, Namibia, bringing together South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, the three co-hosts of the 2027 World Cup.

Pakistan is also set to host another tri-nation series in October 2026, featuring two visiting nations as part of the broader FTP schedule.

MORE: 'Sooryavanshi has skill but…': Dhawan gives his verdict on Vaibhav

Gill's argument taps into something cricket fans have quietly missed for years. i.e. the unpredictability and variety that triangular tournaments once brought to the format.

Bilateral series are easy enough to slot into a calendar, but they rarely bring the kind of shifting challenge that comes from facing several different opponents within one tournament window. Tri-series used to deliver exactly that as teams had to constantly adjust their tactics against contrasting styles of different teams, which kept things interesting for viewers.

Bringing the format back on a larger scale won't be simple, though. Cricket's calendar is already stretched thin, and squeezing in more multi-team tournaments will be difficult. The cricket administrators should find a way to balance them against existing bilateral series and league commitments without burning out players further.

Gould's measured stance, leaving the door open for tri-series without treating them as an urgent priority, seems like a reasonable way forward. Done right, rather than tacked on as an afterthought in the schedule, this format could bring back some of the spark ODI cricket has been missing, without piling even more strain onto an already packed calendar.

title: Ben Simmons makes eye-opening Instagram post amid NBA comeback attempt
description: Ben Simmons shared a reflective message that hints at exactly where his head is as his comeback attempt continues to take shape.
fullText:
Ben Simmons makes eye-opening Instagram post amid NBA comeback attempt appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Ben Simmons is sending another signal that his NBA career is far from over. The former No. 1 overall pick shared a reflective message on Instagram Saturday, posting a photo of himself looking physically imposing near a basketball hoop alongside a caption that read as both a farewell to his turbulent past and a declaration of intent for what comes next.

"I wouldn't change the story," Simmons wrote on Instagram. "The highs, the lows, the pain, the time, the lessons, I embrace all of it. Every chapter built something in me that I couldn't have built any other way. Grateful for where I've been. Proud of where I stand. Ready for wherever this goes."

The post landed just days after he shared a photo of LeBron James' signature sneakers on his Instagram Story, another quiet hint that a return to the league, and possibly a reunion with his original franchise, remains on his mind.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Simmons has not played since appearing in 18 games for the Los Angeles Clippers during the 2024-25 season, averaging just 2.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 3.1 assists in 16.4 minutes. He sat out the entire 2025-26 campaign after his previous contract expired, but has repeatedly made clear in recent interviews that retirement is not on his mind.

Simmons' career has followed a dramatic arc since Philadelphia made him the top pick in the 2016 draft. He won Rookie of the Year and earned three All-Star selections behind his rare combination of size, playmaking, and defensive versatility, drawing comparisons to some of the league's most unique talents.

A mix of injuries, a well-documented mental health battle, and a messy split with the 76ers organization eventually derailed that trajectory, leading to his 2022 trade to the Brooklyn Nets and a steady decline in role and production ever since.

Now 30, Simmons appears intent on writing a new chapter. Speculation about a reunion with Philadelphia has picked up since LeBron James signed with the 76ers this offseason, given the two share the same representation in Rich Paul and Klutch Sports.

Whether that speculation turns into anything concrete remains unclear, but for a player once at the center of one of the NBA's most talked-about breakups, his latest message suggests he is done running from his past and ready to write whatever comes next.

fullText:
While the New York Yankees remain a very competitive team in the American League, they have been trying to stay afloat despite three injuries to their offensive core.

Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Cody Bellinger remain out due to injury. Despite their absence, the Yankees have found ways to win baseball games.

Throughout their last eight games, New York has gone 5-3. It isn't ideal, but the Yankees are staying afloat enough to allow their stars to get healthy. The hope is that they can return at some point down the final stretch of the regular season heading into the playoffs.

On Saturday, August 8, New York revealed a new update about Stanton. He hasn't played a game since April 24 when he went down with a calf injury.

Aaron Boone, the Yankees' manager, revealed some new details about Stanton. His latest update provides some optimism about a potential return sooner rather than later.

He stated that Stanton jogged in the outfield on Friday and "started the introduction to some bases." Boone also said that "I expect him back here at some point. He'll be in there when the time's right."

Stanton is still a very feared player at the plate when healthy. He may be 36 years old now, but he's still capable of taking baseballs out of the park.

Prior to the injury, Stanton played in just 24 games. He hit three home runs to go along with 14 RBI and a slash line of .256/.302/.422. Adding his production back into the lineup would be a big step towards legitimate World Series contention for New York.

Fans across the baseball world were quick to make their comments heard on social media.

"Unbelievable how this dude can barely move every season. Was on a massive hall of fame trajectory," one fan wrote.

Another chimed in, "Imagine being an MLB player and being introduced to touching a base again due to a strained calf."

"I can't wait for this dead weight to no longer be a Yankee. All time bad acquisition. The NTC should never happen again for any contract," a third fan commented.

Yet another fan said, "Honestly these updates are ridiculous and the whole Stanton situation is absurd."

"Have this man strap up for the Old Timers game at this point," another comment read.

Needless to say, fans are frustrated with how much time Stanton has missed. At 36, recovering from an injury gets a bit more difficult. Hopefully, more good news will be coming regarding the slugger in the near future.

title: Cavaliers, Hawks, Clippers, Bucks in bidding war for $11M NBA champion, 23-year-old young star
description: The Cavaliers, Clippers, Bucks, and Hawks are in need of a starting wing. It seems they are fighting it out for one of the top remaining free agents.
fullText:
Cavaliers, Hawks, Clippers, Bucks in bidding war for $11M NBA champion, 23-year-old young star originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

NBA rosters for the upcoming season are still being adjusted with free agency continuing to unfold. LeBron James' decision held up the process for several organizations and players looking for new homes, and there are still plenty of major moves left to be made.

One player searching for a potential new home is Peyton Watson, who is a restricted free agent. Watson and his camp are reportedly seeking a hefty contract as negotiations continue.

"Peyton Watson and his camp want something in that $28 million north range and the offers so far have been fluctuating between that $20-24 million per year range… When you're Peyton Watson, you want more than Christian Braun," ClutchPoints' Brett Siegel wrote.

The biggest challenge for Watson is that, as a restricted free agent, he cannot simply choose whichever team he wants. A deal has to be worked out between Watson and the Denver Nuggets, which would likely come in the form of a sign-and-trade. However, with Denver in a difficult financial situation, there has been discussion about Watson potentially accepting his qualifying offer instead.

"The top restricted free agents — Jalen Duren, Peyton Watson and Bennedict Mathurin — are now all considering taking their qualifying offers to become unrestricted in 2027. As negotiations stall out across the board, these three could become trendsetters against the RFA process," NBA reporter Evan Sidery posted.

Denver does not want to lose Watson, but the organization's financial situation could ultimately force its hand. Teams such as the Atlanta Hawks, Cleveland Cavaliers, Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Clippers have all expressed interest in getting a deal done for the young wing.

"That is why teams like the LA Clippers, Milwaukee Bucks, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Atlanta Hawks have all expressed sign-and-trade interest in Watson over the last month. Interest from the Clippers, Bucks, and Cavs is real, yet there are still some limitations to each potential sign-and-trade scenario," Siegel wrote.

The teams clearly want Watson, but the Nuggets are not going to let him leave unless they receive a package they believe is worth it.

Watson has earned $11 million throughout his young NBA career. Given Denver's current financial situation, the Nuggets also do not have much flexibility to work with in a potential trade. For now, the Hawks, Cavaliers, Clippers and Bucks will continue battling for Watson's services. If none of those teams can get a sign-and-trade completed, Watson could ultimately take his qualifying offer and enter unrestricted free agency in 2027.
