fullText:
Red Bull Junior Programme's future director Gwen Lagrue, much like Helmut Marko, has built a reputation over the years for identifying and developing a number of promising talents who later established themselves in Formula 1. But who are they, and how many drivers has he helped on their way to the top?

While Helmut Marko helped shape a generation of drivers who went on to become some of Formula 1's biggest stars, most notably Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen, Lagrue can also boast an impressive track record of his own. He will effectively take over the Austrian's role in identifying and developing the next generation of outstanding talents for the Milton Keynes-based team's junior programme.

While Kimi Antonelli and George Russell are now well known as the two leading products of Mercedes' junior system since the creation of its young driver programme, Lagrue also played a key role in identifying and developing other talents who remain on the Formula 1 grid today.

Lagrue first became involved in Ocon's career long before either of them became part of the Mercedes set-up. With the Frenchman's family struggling to cover the considerable costs of climbing the junior single-seater ladder, Eric Boullier saw enough potential in Ocon to connect him with Lagrue, who was working for Gravity Sport Management at the time. The Lotus/Renault-linked organisation subsequently stepped in to provide the financial and management support Ocon needed to continue his progression through the lower categories.

Their paths remained closely linked when Ocon became associated with Mercedes in 2015. Around the same period, Lagrue also joined the German manufacturer and later took responsibility for its young-driver programme. His involvement with Ocon continued throughout the following years, including after the Frenchman established himself elsewhere.

Ocon ultimately never became a Mercedes F1 race driver, but his career still represents one of the earliest examples of a talent whose rise was closely supported by Lagrue. Nearly a decade after making his Formula 1 debut, the Frenchman has become a constant presence on the grid.

The Thai is another current Formula 1 driver whose path crossed closely with Lagrue well before reaching the top category. The pair first became acquainted during Albon's karting career, where he emerged as one of the standout names of a highly rated generation that also featured Max Verstappen. When the programme supporting Albon chose to part ways with him at the end of 2012, Lagrue stepped in and offered him an opportunity within the Lotus set-up.

Their relationship continued as Albon progressed through Formula Renault, Formula 3, GP3 and Formula 2, with Lagrue supporting him throughout those stages. Albon also completed simulator work for Mercedes before being released when the opportunity arose for him to return to the young driver programme that previously dropped him.

In a lengthy post on social media, Lagrue looked back on his 11-year journey with Mercedes following his final Grand Prix with the team in Hungary, placing particular emphasis on the drivers he helped nurture during his time in charge of the junior programme. Among them were Esteban Ocon, Nyck de Vries, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, alongside Fred Vesti, Doriane Pin and the many other young talents who passed through the Mercedes system over the years.

For Lagrue, seeing those drivers develop and progress towards the highest levels of motorsport was one of the most rewarding aspects of his role. He encouraged the current and former members of the programme to continue pursuing their ambitions, working hard and making the most of every stage of their journey, while underlining the importance of the team surrounding them in helping them reach their full potential.

Rather than focusing on Mercedes' championships, victories and records, Lagrue highlighted the people he worked with and the opportunity to guide young drivers through crucial stages of their careers as the most meaningful part of his time with the team. He also expressed his gratitude to Toto Wolff for the trust placed in him and thanked the entire Mercedes organisation, bringing an 11-season chapter to a close before moving on to the next stage of his career.

title: Lakers urged not to sign $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, focus on Klay Thompson, PJ Washington
description: The Los Angeles Lakers have been all in on a young NBA champion. However, it now seems like they are being told to move onto potential trades for either Klay Thompson or PJ Washington.
fullText:
Lakers urged not to sign $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, focus on Klay Thompson, PJ Washington originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Los Angeles Lakers have been all-in on Jonathan Kuminga since LeBron James informed the team that he would no longer be returning. However, it has been a lengthy process for Los Angeles to get a deal done.

Even throughout this process, the Lakers have not wavered and remain focused on Kuminga. Landing a deal for the young forward remains LA's top priority as the offseason continues.

"Jonathan Kuminga remains the Lakers' top free agent target before finishing their offseason. As the Cavaliers have pivoted to chasing Peyton Watson, Kuminga is the sole focus currently for Los Angeles. There could soon be momentum gathering on Kuminga to LA via sign-and-trade," NBA reporter Evan Sidery wrote.

With the Lakers seemingly being Kuminga's preferred destination, it still appears that his camp and the Atlanta Hawks are creating obstacles to a potential sign-and-trade. Nothing has moved in weeks, largely because Atlanta has not been satisfied with the trade package it could receive in return.

"It has reached the second month of what has become a second consecutive prolonged Kuminga free agency process. The Lakers met with Kuminga in the early hours of free agency, pitching him on a high-minutes role for a high-profile fringe contender in desperate need of athletic help on the wing. The opportunity appealed to Kuminga, but the sign-and-trade contract offer (years, money, package going back to Atlanta) didn't satisfy all sides. The Lakers remain interested in him, league sources said, but movement toward a deal has remained stalled for weeks," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote.

With the process continuing to drag on, the Lakers have now been urged to move on from Kuminga and prioritize a trade for either Klay Thompson or P.J. Washington.

"Obviously, anything can change during the NBA offseason, as Kuminga could have a change of heart or decide Los Angeles is the best situation for him, but it seems like it is time for the storied franchise to move on. Perhaps the Lakers should focus on trading for Klay Thompson or P.J. Washington, both of whom have experience playing with Doncic," SI's Ryan Ward wrote.

At this point, it is fair to say that moving on from Kuminga would not necessarily be a bad idea. The Lakers have been pursuing him for nearly two months, and nothing has been finalized.

Kuminga was on a $46 million contract last season, while the Lakers are looking for someone who can make an immediate impact. It remains unclear whether Kuminga would be able to do that right away, but Thompson and Washington have already proven themselves throughout their careers.

For the Lakers, the decision ultimately comes down to how long they are willing to wait for Kuminga versus how quickly they can find another option to strengthen the roster around Luka Doncic.

title: Elina Svitolina Makes Feelings Known on Beating Amanda Anisimova in Toronto – ‘I Was Expecting Her To Come Back’
description: Elina Svitolina has advanced to the quarterfinals of the 2026 Canadian Open, triumphing over Amanda Anisimova in a blockbuster fourth-round clash. After securing a comfortable victory, Svitolina shared her thoughts on her battle with the American.
fullText:
Elina Svitolina has advanced to the quarterfinals of the 2026 Canadian Open, triumphing over Amanda Anisimova in a blockbuster fourth-round clash. After securing a comfortable victory, Svitolina shared her thoughts on her battle with the American.

After triumphing over Jéssica Bouzas Maneiro and Anastasia Potapova, No. 9 seed Svitolina set up a highly anticipated battle with No. 8 seed Anisimova in the fourth round of the WTA 1000 event in Toronto.

Entering the contest with a 4-1 lead in her head-to-head record against Anisimova, Svitolina continued her dominance over the American at the Canadian Open. She raced through the opening set and went up a double break in the second. Although Anisimova fought back to save four match points, Svitolina held her nerve to secure a 6-2, 6-4 victory.

During her post-match press conference, Svitolina acknowledged that she struggled to close out the second set. She praised Anisimova as a formidable player and said that she had expected the American to make a stronger comeback before expressing satisfaction at emerging victorious.

"Yeah, it was not easy to close that second set. I think she came back, she was playing a bit better. It was not easy, with a little bit of wind, and the nature of the game, was not an easy one," Svitolina said.

"So, yeah, I mean, she is, of course, a hell of a player, so I was expecting her to come back a little bit more. Sometimes she's playing really sharp. So, yeah, it was not an easy one, but I'm really happy with the way I could handle the 5-4 and serve it out to close the match," she added.

Svitolina also reflected on her own campaign at the WTA 1000 event, pointing out the improvements she had made since edging out a hard-fought 6-7(5), 7-6(4), 6-4 victory over Jéssica Bouzas Maneiro in her opening match.

"Well, I think I improved match by match. The second round was not the best performance from my side. But I'm happy that I went through that tough battle. Having one day off I think helped me to again find my game, work on few things, and feeling better on the court. Also physically, one day off is helping me to just be more fresh," she said.

MORE: 'Our Closeness Let Me Spiral' – Amanda Anisimova Takes Responsibility After Rehiring Coach Hendrik Vleeshouwers

Up next, Elina Svitolina will take on No. 16 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open. Meanwhile, Amanda Anisimova will begin gearing up for the Cincinnati Open, aiming to make a deeper run at the WTA 1000 event, which begins on August 13.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: This veteran to arrive at Newcastle United and be the positive influence needed?
description: Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out. After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.
fullText:
Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out.

After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.

There are fresh faces through the door, players returning from the World Cup, and a new manager and coaching staff putting the squad through its paces in La Manga, Spain.

From what I have seen of the early training sessions, the intensity is certainly there. Throw in temperatures of 30-plus degrees and the lads are going to know they have been working hard this week!

One thing that particularly pleased me was the apparent passion on show. Both the players and coaching staff looked fully engaged, and there seemed to be a real intensity about the sessions.

Of course, training is one thing — now we need to see that same attitude and commitment transferred onto the pitch when it really matters.

And then there is Pierre-Emile Højbjerg.

Reports linking the 31-year-old with a move to Newcastle have raised more than a few eyebrows, with a fee of around £10m-£15m being bandied about.

Personally, I don't see what all the fuss is about.

In fact, I think it could be a very sensible piece of business.

Højbjerg is a seasoned Premier League player with considerable experience, and at around £10m-£15m, he certainly wouldn't break the bank. More importantly, he could bring somethingNewcastle United will need in abundance — experience.

With several young players coming into the squad, having an experienced head in the dressing room could prove invaluable. Højbjerg knows the Premier League, understands the demands of playing at the highest level and, importantly, has been there before.

Sometimes the value of a player cannot simply be measured by goals, assists or statistics.

It can be measured by what happens around him.

The influence he has on younger players. The standards he sets in training. The calmness he brings when things aren't going according to plan. The voice in the dressing room when the pressure starts to build.

We have already seen how important that kind of experience can be.

Our noisy neighbours down the road benefited considerably from the addition of Granit Xhaka, while Newcastle themselves saw the impact Kieran Trippier made when he arrived at St James' Park.

Trippier wasn't just a footballer. He brought leadership, experience and standards — qualities that had a positive influence on those around him.

That kind of influence should never be underestimated.

So, while some supporters may question whether Højbjerg is the right age or whether the money would be better spent elsewhere, I would be more than happy to see him arrive on Tyneside.

Newcastle United have plenty of young talent. What they also need is the experience to help that talent flourish.

If Højbjerg can provide that, then perhaps this is one transfer we shouldn't be scoffing at.

Instead, we should be asking whether another experienced head could be exactly what this new-look Newcastle United needs.

title: Real Madrid academy prodigy set to stay this summer amid Fulham links
description: The future of Thiago Pitarch has become a key talking point at Real Madrid this summer, as the squad continues to go through some recalibration after the slew of new signings.Pitarch has been linked w...
fullText:
The future of Thiago Pitarch has become a key talking point at Real Madrid this summer, as the squad continues to go through some recalibration after the slew of new signings.

Pitarch has been linked with a move to Fulham, with former coach Alvaro Arbeloa keen on reuniting with the young midfielder at Craven Cottage.

This has led to question marks over Pitarch's future at the Santiago Bernabeu heading into the new season.

Mourinho wants Pitarch to stay. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

According to Diario AS, Pitarch will not be leaving this summer and will instead be part of Jose Mourinho's first-team plans.

The decision is said to be a direct result of Mourinho's wishes, with the Portuguese having played a crucial role in keeping the youngster at the club.

Despite being registered with Castilla due to an overabundance of senior squad numbers, Pitarch will be treated as a full-time first-team player rather than relegated to the reserves.

It represents a significant show of faith in the breakout star of last season, and fulfils Pitarch's own desire to succeed at Real Madrid.

Mourinho was opposed to sanctioning the departure of both Pitarch and Brahim Diaz, viewing them as useful options for the campaign ahead.

Pitarch will fight for a place in the first-team. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Pitarch is staying despite some genuinely attractive offers, the most compelling of which came from Fulham.

The appeal there was obvious, with Arbeloa's presence, the financial package and the promise of a prominent role all in Fulham's favour. Above every option, though, Pitarch prioritised staying and fighting for his place at Real Madrid.

His pre-season was disrupted by a torn medial collateral ligament in his left knee, an injury expected to keep him out for around six weeks. However, the setback has done nothing to change Mourinho's mind.

Once fit, Pitarch faces fierce competition in Mourinho's midfield, with Aurelien Tchouameni, Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga and Bernardo Silva all vying for spots in the double pivot.

Notably, with Rodri now heading to Barcelona rather than the Bernabeu, an opportunity may yet open up for the talented teenager to stake his claim.

title: Ranking Fiorentina’s number 10s
description: A hundred years of tens would be, what, 17 million?
fullText:
Fiorentina will retire the famous 10 jersey in its centenary year as an olive branch to Giancarlo Antognoni. The legendary playmaker's relationship with the club has soured over the past few years and he's threatened to skip the celebrations. It's a sad state of affairs when the greatest player in Viola history is so mad at management that they refuse to participate in what should be a joyful occasion. That's all I have to say about that.

What I'm really interested in is the 10 shirt itself. Albert Guðmundsson has worn it for the past couple years but will have to find a new one. That's fine by me. I've made no secret of my opinion about him and seeing the sport's most hallowed number on his narrow shoulders is a constant, low-level irritation. It did get me thinking, though, about all the 10s in Fiorentina history. I enjoyed thinking about it so much that I made a tier list.

A quick bit of history. Serie A teams started wearing numbered shirts during the 1939-1940 season. Back then, every starting lineup was numbered 1-11, meaning players would cycle in and out of squad numbers through the season. The FIGC mandated annual squad numbers ahead of the 1995-1996 season, setting up the system still in use and leading to Rui Costa's teammates pranking the absolute hell out of him.

While I don't have data for a full century of number 10s, I was able to check Transfermarkt going back to the 1950-1951 season, when 4 players rotated through it. In total, there are 50 guys listed who've worn it, which is a lovely round number for a centenary. I didn't think I'd be able to rank them 1-50 so I've gone for tiers instead, taking into account impact, length of tenure, and how large a portion of Viola history they hold. That might sound subjective but it's not. It's all very scientific and I'm not sharing my trailblazing methodology with anyone but the Nobel committee. You can rest assured it's completely and unimpeachably correct so no arguing is allowed.

Giancarlo Antognoni (1973-1977, 1979-1984, 1986-1987): His current feud with the club aside, there's a reason he's l'unico dieci for now and forever.

Roberto Baggio (1986-1990): He didn't win the club any trophies and his Ballon d'Or came after he left Florence but you can't tell the story of calcio without him.

Rui Costa (1994-2001): The platonic ideal of the 1990s trequartista and maybe the finest playmaker of his generation.

Miguel Montuori (1955-1957): El Artillero wore 8 and 9 as well throughout the course of his storied career, which was cut tragically short when he got hit in the face with a ball and suffered permanent vision damage aged just 28. Had he gotten another couple years, he might well have led Fiorentina to silverware and moved up a level.

Kurt Hamrin (1957-1958): He's an all-time great without a doubt but mostly played on the wing and thus sported the number 7.

Giancarlo de Sisti (1965-1970, 1973-1974): Only the old-timers remember Picchio but 8 seasons with Fiorentina, including a key role in the second scudetto, make him one of those hallowed names. He was more of a metronomic passer than a playmaker but gets credit for his attitude and general cuteness, as well as returning to coach the Ye-Ye teams of the early 1980s.

Adrian Mutu (2006-2011): You all know that I'm a Mutu fetishist. What did you expect?

Egisto Pandolfini (1951-1952): A regular for club and country, he also wore 8 and 9 at times during his 4-year tenure.

Guido Gratton (1955-1956): 6 seasons as a regular in some magical teams but he was always part of the supporting cast behind guys like Montuori and Hamrin, often in a deeper midfield role. Has the Italy caps and the scudetto, though, to remind you of his class.

Amarildo (1967-1968): He helped fire Fiorentina to its first scudetto but was more about moments than sustained excellence, scoring 16 goals across 3 seasons. Probably more of a Milan legend than a Viola one. He's also the last surviving participant in the 1962 World Cup final.

Claudio Merlo (1972-73, 1974-1975): A deeper midfielder than what one might usually associate with the 10, he was the tempo-setter for the second scudetto run. He only scored 29 goals across 345 seasons but he's got the 6th-most appearances in club history as a regular for 11 (!) seasons.

Massimo Orlando (1990-1994): Never hit the predicted heights, largely due to injury, but boasted technical excellence and selflessness during those early Cecchi Gori years.

Anselmo Robbiati (1994-1995): Never the most prolific but he helped get Fiorentina back to Serie A and had some memorable nights, particularly in the cup competitions, while mostly serving as Rui Costa's backup.

Alberto Aquilani (2012-2015): The Aquaman was the most mercurial of the 3 tenors but when he was on song, he was marvelous. Bonus points for coming back to win silverware as Primavera coach.

Federico Bernardeschi (2015-2017): Calling him a good servant is obviously not quite right but he was the centerpiece of the attack for a couple (pretty lean) years. I also have it on good authority that he's grown into a genuinely nice man so I'm willing to put it all down to youthful idiocy.

Gaetano Castrovilli (2020-2023): He'll always be an almost, a what-if, but his determined returns from his constant injuries and underrated work without the ball elevate him in my mind, even if he never came close to the ceiling I saw for him.

Nico González (2023-2024): One of the least 10ish 10s here as a player who relied on his physical excellence but he spearheaded the attack in his own inimitable way for years and deserves a ton of credit for keeping the Viola in Europe.

Rodolofo Beltrandi (1951-1952): He earned 47 appearances with 10 goals across 4 seasons but never secured a regular role.

Dan Ekner (1951-1952): As far as I can tell from the game logs, the Swede was the first man to pull on the 1o shirt for Fiorentina. He also played in England, France, Spain, the Netherlands, and the US.

André Roosenburg (1951-1952): The 9-time Netherlands international scored 17 goals across 3 seasons, throwing hands with defenders and getting banned in his home country for playing professionally.

Luigi Milan (1959-1961): Struck a brace in Glasgow against Rangers and another in the return leg to lead Fiorentina to the 1960-1961 Cup Winner's Cup. Was mostly a bit part player outside of that season but he's about as cult a figure as you'll find.

Renato Benaglia (1964-1965): More of a regista than a trequartista but was a regular presence in his 2 seasons in Florence.

Mario Brugnera (1965-1966): Had 4 productive seasons (32 goals in 94 games) but is more famous for helping turn Cagliari into a deeply unlikely Serie A champion in 1969-1970 and is definitely more of their legend than ours.

Vincenzo Guerini (1975-1975): He was more of a holding midfielder and never anything approaching a star but he was a solid backup and is undefeated as Fiorentina manager so he gets a little extra boost, even if he never really deserved the 10.

Antonio di Gennaro (1976-1977): Had the misfortune to be an attacking playmaker while Antognoni was at the club. The pair never figured out how to coexist on the pitch and di Gennaro left the club. He was very good, helping Hellas Verona win the scudetto in 1984-1985 and leading Bari to promotion and the capture of the Mitropa Cup, but his Viola tenure was sadly muted.

Daniele Massaro (1983-1984): He's best remembered as one of the key figures in those 1990s Milan sides under Arrigo Sacchi but he spent 4 years in Florence as one of Antognoni's runners, although he only scored 15 goals in that time.

Eraldo Pecci (1984-1985): Took over the 10 in the last of his 4 seasons in Florence. He vacillated between solid and good but mostly played under Antognoni's shadow.

Sergio Battistini (1985-1986): He was quite good as a player but split time between rightback, holding midfield, and sweeper. He mostly wore 4, 5, 6, or 13 for the Viola, at least, but I simply can't get behind a defensive player wearing 10.

Roberto Onorati (1985-1987): Looked a promising youngster blessed with pace and technical ability but never put it together, scoring a single goal in 92 appearances across 4 seasons before establishing himself at Genoa and enjoying a fine career.

Diego Fuser (1980-1981): Milan loaned him to Fiorentina for his single season and he flourished, scoring 9 goals from the wing. Would've been a great guy to have around for the Batistuta and Rui Costa era.

Luboš Kubík (1990-1991): Hell of a player with a wild backstory. Scored 9 goals across 2 seasons in Florence while playing primarily as a sweeper. I have to dock him a couple points for that. A centerback shouldn't wear 10, even a goalscoring libero. Just ain't right.

Fabrizio Di Mauro (1992-1993, 1994-1995): The veteran midfield schemer enjoyed a decent run, earning 3 Italy caps in his first season at the Franchi, but never hit those heights again.

Cristiano Zanetti (1994-1995): A promising youth player, he made just 5 senior appearances before leaving in search of regular playing time. The Viola should've kept him around, as he ended up being one of the better registe of his generation, earning 17 caps while turning out for the likes of Roma, Inter Milan, and Juventus. He came back to Florence in the twilight of his career as part of the Felipe Melo move and helped his old side, which was fun.

Riccardo Maspero (2003-2004): He was winding down his career when he joined Florentia Viola in Serie C2 and provided depth in the promotion push to Serie B, making a further 17 appearances before ending his professional career.

Hidetoshi Nakata (2004-2005): He wasn't great in Florence but he's so cool. Walk into any bar with a Nakata Fiorentina shirt and your social capital doubles.

Stefano Fiore (2005-2006): Formed a good relationship with Luca Toni that propelled the Viola to 4th until the Calciopoli scandal saw the league dock them 19 points and nearly sent them down to Serie B. That mayhem ensured that first-year sporting director Pantaleo Corvino didn't redeem his loan, which is a shame on purely nominal terms.

Pietro Maiellaro (1991-1992): Following 4 fantastic seasons at Bari, he arrived at the same time and for nearly the same price as Batistuta and was expected to create the chances for him and Mazinho (double whoops). Instead, he was shuffled off to Venezia the following summer.

Dunga (1991-1992): A fantastic player but anyone who's ever seen him play knows that, excellent as he was, he was nothing resembling a number 10. If this was about pure talent and impact, though, he'd be in that second tier.

Domenico Morfeo (2001-2002): In hindsight, buying a hyped-up youngster when the tridente of Batistuta, Rui Costa, and Lulu Oliveira was already in place was a mistake. There were some bright moments but the arrival of Edmundo rang down the curtain on his time and he spent the next several seasons getting farmed out on loan, where injuries and a prickly temperament meant he never fulfilled his potential.

Santiago Silva (2010-2011): Inheriting Mutu's number would've been a tall task for anyone. Handing it to a 31-year-old journeyman was a disaster. El Tanque scored, at least. Once. From the spot. At the death. In a truly insane 3-0 win over Roma that featured 3 red cards. But hey, nice penalty.

Rubén Olivera (2011-2012): A jobbing hardman midfielder, he became a target of mockery as the 2nd consecutive bald Uruguayan to hold the 10 shirt for no good reason. He took 5 the following season, which fit his persona much better, but also yikes, man.

Valentin Eysseric (2017-2018): Never a good sign when you can't beat out Cyril Thereau's washed carcass for minutes but that's what happened. It's no coincidence that Val's brief apotheosis occurred when he was wearing 92.

Marko Pjaca (2018-2019): I feel bad for Pjaca, who was a ballyhooed prospect done in by knee injuries and whose body was obviously not up to the task at that time. But handing the 10 shirt to a Juve loanee just a year after Bernardeschi lit it on fire on the way to the Juvenuts wasn't a good look for anyone.

Kevin-Prince Boateng (2019-2020): The first number 10 of the Rocco Commisso era, he brought name recognition but not much else. He scored once while playing a bit part and moved to Beşiktaş in January. Even so, I remain rather fond of him for reasons I can't articulate.

Albert Guðmundsson (2024-2026): Again, I just don't like the guy and I don't think his Viola tenure can be graded as anything but a massive disappointment given his price. I think he perfectly reflected last year's team and that's about as far from a compliment as I can make it.

title: Infantino saga: FIFA defends embattled president after fresh UEFA allegations
description: FIFA has launched a strong defence of Gianni Infantino after a turbulent week for football’s governing body.They accused his critics of attempting to undermine the president through allegations and ...
fullText:
FIFA has launched a strong defence of Gianni Infantino after a turbulent week for football's governing body.

They accused his critics of attempting to undermine the president through allegations and misinformation.

The intervention came after UEFA confirmed that a payment was made to a female employee who was alleged to have been involved in a relationship with Infantino during his time as UEFA general secretary.

Reports have described the payment as a substantial exit settlement, adding to the controversy around a FIFA president already facing growing opposition from European football.

Still, Infantino refuses to resign and continues to battle on.

FIFA has rejected the allegations against Infantino and insisted that the Swiss-Italian remains in office with a legitimate democratic mandate from the organisation's 211 member associations.

A FIFA spokesperson said the organisation would not support or facilitate any attempt to challenge the presidential election process outside its established statutes and governance procedures.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its President," FIFA said.

They also claimed there was an ongoing effort by some individuals to undermine both FIFA and Infantino.

They argued that those without sufficient support among member associations should not attempt to achieve through allegations what they cannot accomplish through democratic processes.

The statement comes against the backdrop of an increasingly bitter relationship between FIFA and UEFA.

UEFA said it would continue to boycott competitions under Infantino if he remains president, following the collapse of his controversial proposal to sell £3.1 billion worth of World Cup commercial stakes to private investors.

FIFA maintains that Infantino's record should be judged on his contribution to football over more than three decades.

The governing body highlighted his efforts to broaden access to resources and opportunities across world football.

It also insisted that legitimate scrutiny is welcome, but warned that inaccurate or misleading reporting would be challenged directly and vigorously.

Meanwhile, UEFA are ready to open an investigation into Infantino's time with the body as they continue to bring the strongest offence against the FIFA chief.

title: Team USA dominates sprints and hurdles at World U20 Championships
description: Tate Taylor and Mia Maxwell made history as the first athletes from one country to sweep 100- and 200-meter World U20 gold.
fullText:
Tate Taylor and Mia Maxwell made history Aug. 8, becoming the first athletes from the same country to sweep the 100- and 200-meter titles at the World Athletics U20 Championships track and field meet.

The two sprinters from Texas were adorned in gold for the second time in the last three days as they each won their respective 200 finals Saturday during the fourth day of the five-day meet at Hayward Field. Both won their 100 golds on Thursday.

"More to come, better to come," Maxwell said. "This is just the beginning of what me and Tate and all the Americans' future in the sport is, so I'm excited to see what the future holds."

Taylor won the men's 200 in a meet-record 19.83 seconds, with silver going to fellow American Blake Hamilton (20.31) and bronze going to Jayden Green (20.55) of Barbados.

"To go out there and execute the way I wanted to, felt pretty good," Taylor said.

A second-place finish capped a surprisingly successful track season for Hamilton, who will soon be joining Southern California's football team for fall camp as a wide receiver.

"I mean, this silver means everything," Hamilton said. "(Going from) four months ago not really thinking about track to becoming No. 2 in the world is really big."

Maxwell won the women's 200 in a personal-record 22.37, with world season-leading Shanoya Douglas of Jamaica earning silver in 22.68 and Mia's twin sister Mariah Maxwell getting the bronze in 22.77.

"The 200 is a little bit out of my comfort zone since I'm a little bit used to running the 100 more," Mia Maxwell said. "But coming into the 200, I definitely had to come in with a different mindset and not get too comfortable off my win in the 100. I'm glad that I executed everything well. ... I'm really tired."

"Go Dawgs!" Madeline Cooper shouted with a big smile and a gold medal dangling around her neck.

It indeed was quite the night in the hurdles for the Georgia track team.

Cooper and Bulldog teammate Le'Ezra Brown swept the women's 100 and men's 110 hurdles, respectively, with Brown also tying the world U20 record.

"It's crazy," Brown beamed. "I didn't know it was gonna be that fast."

Brown finished in 12.72, comfortably ahead of silver medalist Jeremy Koga (12.97) of Japan and fellow Team USA member Zacchaeus Brocks, who equaled his PR at 12.98 for bronze.

"I knew I could do it," Brown said. " I didn't want to say it in an interview because I wanted to stay humble, but in my mind I was like, ' I'm gonna go get it.' I didn't have a great a start and I was like oh my God they're gone, but my top end is crazy, as you see."

Brown's victory came not long after Cooper schooled the women's field with her win in 12.91.

"Man, we've been talking about this since after nationals and we did it," said Brown, who was a freshman last season with Cooper. "I can't wait to see her. We probably gonna scream, yell, it don't matter. I'm proud of her."

Cooper's winning time equaled her world U20 lead. South Africa's Tumi Rankgopa was second in 12.96 and Jamaica's Tiana Marshall set a PR with her bronze-medal finish in 12.97.

"I just really had to be like, you know what, I'm the world lead, I have to trust mt abilities," Cooper said. "I know what I can do. I just ran out there. I just ran like it was a regular race. I just forgot about all the cameras, forgot about all the people here, all the pressure, and I just let it all go."

Men's 800 final: Imad Bouchajda of Morocco shot to the front with 200 to go and held on to win gold in 1:44.64. Austrailia's Daniel Williams was second in 1:45.36 and Spain's Alejandro Rios third in a PR 1:46.25.

Women's 3,000 final: Ethiopia's Yordanos Tsigab and Shito Gumi won gold and silver, respectively. Tsigab crossed in a PR 8:43.95 and Gumi in 8:45.06. The bronze went to Uganda's Charity Cherop, the 3,000 gold medalist from Wednesday.

Women's 800 final: Poland's Ziva Remic and Greece's Ioulianna Roussou ran side-by-side down the homestretch with Remic winning by a step at the finish line in 2:03.03 to 2:03.08. Great Britain's Shaikira King took bronze in 2:03.52.

Men's long jump final: Daniele Leonardop Inzoli won gold with a mark of 26 feet, 1¾ inches, but Australian Mason McGroder made him sweat when he went a PR 26-1½ on his final jump to claim silver. India's Shahnavaz Khan was third at 25-8¾.

Men's high jump final: All three medalists cleared the same height (7-3) but it was Algeria's Younes Ayachi with the fewest misses en route to a gold medal. India's Basant claimed the silver and Great Britain's Otis Poole earned the bronze.

Women's pole vault final:  Nicole Krutilova was the winner with a clearance of 14-7¼. Ukraine's Olha Belchenko cleared 14-5¼ to win silver and American Kylie Neira cleared 14-3¼ to win bronze.

Decathlon final: Sweden's Liam Belo Da Silva took the title with an 8,112-point performance. Mikai Snoek of the Netherlands was second with a PR 7,887 points and Adam Julis of Czechia was third with a PR 7,877 points.

Mixed 4x100 relay final: Italy won the gold medal with a time of 41.21 and Great Britain's Sophie Thomas outleaned American Ava Kitchings in a photo finish for silver, 41.38 to 41.39.

Men's discus prelims: Incoming Oregon freshman and reigning U.S. U20 champion Simon Rosselli advanced to Sunday's final with mark of 199-7 on his one and only attempt.

Women's 400 hurdle semifinals: U.S. U20 champion Natalie Dumas tripped over a hurdle and crashed as the race was entering the homestretch. She still finished the race but was ninth in her heat in 1:11.76. One of two captains for Team USA, Dumas won gold in the mixed 4x400 relay earlier this week.

Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men's basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com and you can follow him on X @chansen_RG

title: Manchester United target Guardiola-approved “excellent” star but face €100m asking price

fullText:
Manchester United are interested in signing the Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton.

They could use another player who can control the tempo of the game and protect the team defensively. However, they are likely to be priced out of a move for the English midfielder.

Wharton has been linked with a move away from Crystal Palace in recent months. He could be attracted to the idea of joining a bigger club. Manchester United will be able to provide him with Champions League football and the platform to fight for trophies.

It will be interesting to see if they are prepared to test the resolve of the London club with an attractive offer before the window closes. Someone like Wharton could take the Manchester United midfield to a whole new level. They will be hoping to do well next season and fight for trophies. They need top-quality players in order to compete with Arsenal and Manchester City.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are looking to add more control in the middle of the park, and it is no surprise that they are keen on the Crystal Palace star. However, they will not be able to offer him Champions League football next season, and that could be a problem when it comes to attracting elite talents.

title: Female chess team 'must include a male player'
description: The She Plays to Win Lionesses A team won promotion promotion to the top flight of competitive chess.
fullText:
An all-female chess team faces having to replace one of its players with a male team member, under current league rules.

The She Plays to Win Lionesses A team were crowned champions of the second division of the Four Nations Chess League (4NCL), earning promotion to the top flight.

They will be the first all-female team to compete in the top division of the UK's national chess league but a rule introduced to boost female participation requires teams to field at least one player of each sex.

The 4NCL said there was "no significant appetite" to change the rule.

Only 11% of rated chess players are female, so in an effort to address the imbalance the top division of the 4NCL requires teams to field at least one player of each sex.

She Plays to Win is a charity organisation which encourages schoolgirls and young women to take up chess.

Team member, Oxford University student Emily Maton, 18, said: "I love the logical aspect of chess, it's such a challenge, you really get to think.

"Most people are supportive but we do still face some comments, people telling us we don't belong, that we're going to struggle at that level, that we're good 'for a girls' team."

Having earned the right to compete in the top division, Maton is frustrated that the rule could lead to changes to the team.

"It obviously has great intentions. It's a really good effort to try and get more women playing that top level, but I don't think they ever expected a female team to get promoted and for that to become a problem".

She said the team may have to include a "token man".

Lorin D'Costa founded She Plays to Win six years ago and has since helped 1,800 female chess players.

He thinks they should still be allowed to field an all-female team when the league starts in October.

He said there was "some discussion" as to what the team should do.

"The team, the community and the camaraderie of the team is so important for females in chess", he adds.

"You can go to most tournament halls and its just a sea of men".

Seventeen-year-old Larissa from Poole in Dorset also competes for She Plays to Win.

"When I'm at tournaments I'm usually one of the only girls because there's not a lot of women who play chess", she says.

"But we're hoping that that can change".

Larissa is disappointed that the all-female team would be allowed to compete in the top division, under the current rules.

She said the team had "put in a lot of effort" to get to the top flight.

"The girls should be able to play as a team because they're representing all women," she said.

In a statement, the 4NCL said that requiring all teams in the top division to have at least one female player "actively encourages female participation in chess".

"We surveyed all the team captains during the 2025/2026 season about whether the rule should be changed; there was no significant appetite on the part of the captains to do so".

"We remain open to changing the rule in future should captains' opinions change".

title: Fermin Lopez talks Rodri, Ferran, Araujo exit and more – “It’s a shame since he was a captain”
description: Fermin Lopez made his long-awaited pre-season return this summer after overcoming the fractured fifth metatarsal that cost him a place at the World Cup.The midfielder featured in Barcelona’s triangu...
fullText:
Fermin Lopez made his long-awaited pre-season return this summer after overcoming the fractured fifth metatarsal that cost him a place at the World Cup.

The midfielder featured in Barcelona's triangular tournament in Udine, where the Catalans beat Nottingham Forest before losing to hosts Udinese, and afterwards spoke to the media on a range of topics.

Araujo is set to join Liverpool. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

One of the main subjects was the departure of Ronald Araujo, who is closing in on a loan move to Liverpool.

Fermin admitted he was sad to see a teammate and captain leave, but wished him well.

"He has come to say goodbye. It's a shame, because he's a captain and I have a good relationship with him. He has decided to continue growing and hopefully he will return next season," said Fermin (h/t Diario SPORT).

The Andalusian was also asked about Ferran Torres and potential new arrival Rodri, though he insisted he did not have much information.

On Ferran's possible exit, Fermin said: "I don't want to go into that, because I don't have the necessary information. He is a good companion and a friend; I hope he decides what's best for him."

Fermin is gearing up for an important season ahead. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

He adopted a similar stance regarding Rodri, who has reportedly chosen Barcelona after his MVP-winning World Cup.

"Rodri is a great player, but he is not at the club. Whatever Deco and the sporting management decide will be fine and, if it has to happen, it will happen," he added.

Fermin, who won a decisive penalty against Nottingham Forest before being rested against Udinese, admitted he is still building up his sharpness after a difficult summer.

"Good. I still have to get into the rhythm, but I felt good. I wanted to play. It's been a very hard summer, but I'm already well and looking forward to this season," he said.

One would expect Fermin to play a key role for Barcelona next season as they look to replace the productivity of Robert Lewandowski and possibly Ferran Torres.

title: Real Madrid playmaker unsure about his place in the team despite top form in pre-season
description: Arda Guler has been one of Real Madrid’s standout performers throughout pre-season, continuing to build on an encouraging campaign under Jose Mourinho.Yet despite his fine form, the Turkish playmake...
fullText:
Arda Guler has been one of Real Madrid's standout performers throughout pre-season, continuing to build on an encouraging campaign under Jose Mourinho.

Yet despite his fine form, the Turkish playmaker faces an uncertain battle for regular minutes, with competition for places fiercer than ever at the Bernabeu.

And much of that uncertainty stems from the impending return of Jude Bellingham.

According to Diario AS, Guler has been Real Madrid's most in-form attacking player this pre-season, leaving a mark in every outing.

Can Guler finally become Real Madrid's most important player next season? (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Against Fiorentina, he was the pick of the bunch even in a disappointing second-half display, and he followed that up with another influential showing in the 2-1 win over Ferencvaros in Budapest.

There, Guler was involved in both goals without registering a goal or an assist himself, providing the corner for the first and a delicate touch to set up the second.

Mourinho has clearly earmarked him for the number 10 role, and Guler has thrived there, orchestrating Real Madrid's attacking play with his vision and creativity.

On current form, it would be almost inconceivable to leave him out of the starting eleven if the season began tomorrow.

Guler vs Bellingham fight could be interesting. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images)

The problem for Guler is that his best position is also occupied by one of the club's biggest names.

Mourinho asked the club to have two players for every position, and in attacking midfield, that means Guler competing directly with Bellingham.

Should the Englishman rediscover the form of his debut campaign, there would be little argument over who starts. However, Bellingham's output dipped over the following two seasons, and there was already debate last term about his place in the side.

For now, circumstances favour Guler. The Turk enjoyed his best season yet with six goals and 14 assists, and with Bellingham unlikely to be at peak fitness for the league opener, Guler should get a run in the opening few matches.

Beyond that, the competition only intensifies, with Diomande, Brahim Diaz and a returning Rodrygo all adding to the battle for attacking spots.

title: The Manchester City manager will select his team’s captain and there is a clear favourite
description: There will be a completely different vibe at Manchester City in the Enzo Maresca era. With a plethora of Manchester City’s experienced players having left the club, Maresca has the opportunity to se...
fullText:
There will be a completely different vibe at Manchester City in the Enzo Maresca era. With a plethora of Manchester City's experienced players having left the club, Maresca has the opportunity to select City's next batch of leaders. It has been reported that this is an option that the Italian manager will pursue. Sam Lee has reported for The Athletic that Enzo Maresca will select Manchester City's captain for the 2026-27 season. There is a clear-cut favourite for that role in City's squad, which is Ruben Dias. The Portuguese international is his team's defensive leader and should be awarded the Manchester City captaincy for next season.

Sam Lee has reported for The Athletic that Enzo Maresca is set to decide who be Manchester City's captain for the 2026-27 season. Pep Guardiola typically let his players vote on who would captain his team during his decade as the manager of Manchester City. Last season however, Guardiola personally selected Bernardo Silva to be Manchester City's captain. Ruben Dias, Rodri, and Erling Haaland formed City's captaincy group with Bernardo Silva for the 2025-26 season. Enzo Maresca is set to follow suit and personally choose Manchester City's captain in his first season as City manager. It is also reported by Lee that Ruben Dias is in line to be Manchester City's captain for next season. However, no decision on this had been made as of yet by Enzo Maresca.

Sam Lee further reports that Rodri is likely to be replaced in Manchester City's leadership group. The Ballon d'Or-winning midfielder is expected to sign with Barcelona this summer. If Maresca employs a four-man leadership group, Maresca will have to replace Bernardo Silva and Rodri. Lastly, Sam Lee reports that Maresca wants a homegrown presence in City's leadership group. Phil Foden and Marc Guehi are the top contenders for this particular role.

There is a standout candidate to be Manchester City's captain for next season. That is Ruben Dias. Ever since Dias joined Manchester City, he has been an inspirational figure for his team. Dias' presence inspires those around him and he has been Manchester City's defensive leader for some time now. Also, Ruben Dias knows what is expected at City and how high the standards must be for his team to succeed. If Enzo Maresca wants a player who sets the standards amongst the players to lead his team, Ruben Dias is that player.

You could mount an argument for Erling Haaland to be Manchester City's captain. Haaland was in City's captaincy group last season and the Norwegian international has learned to become a leader during his time as a member of Pep Guardiola's squad. Erling Haaland is also contracted with City until 2034. However, Haaland may have to wait his turn as Ruben Dias does look to be the next man up in terms of the captaincy at Manchester City. Haaland may well get his opportunity to wear the captain's armband in the 2027-28 season. But that is looking too far ahead for now.

Enzo Maresca will take on the duty of selecting Manchester City's captain for the 2026-27 season. Ruben Dias is the prime candidate for the role. Dias is a natural leader and wearing the captain's armband may elevate his game to another level.

title: Enzo Maresca offered every Manchester City player an opportunity to make an impression
description: At the end of the 2025-26 season, it did seem obvious which players would depart Manchester City this summer. However, Enzo Maresca’s arrival as manager did give City’s players an opportunity to i...
fullText:
At the end of the 2025-26 season, it did seem obvious which players would depart Manchester City this summer. However, Enzo Maresca's arrival as manager did give City's players an opportunity to impress their new manager. Maresca spoke yesterday and said his arrival at City was a reset for Manchester City's players. Judging by Maresca's comments and the performances of the City players in their two friendlies against Inter Milan and the K-League All-Stars, it is easy to see which players have taken the opportunity on offer.

Speaking yesterday ahead of Manchester City's final preseason friendly in Asia against Atletico Madrid, Enzo Maresca revealed that every player started from the same position at the beginning of Manchester City's preseason. Maresca added that how his players performed during their preseason would shape who would depart the club this summer. He explained: "The only thing I have said since I start to the players is that for me it's a new reset. All of them start at same level."

"Pre-season will dictate a little bit the transfer window. This has been the same message for everyone – for me it is a reset."

Manchester City have played two preseason friendlies with one more to come. Those matches and the training sessions have offered Enzo Maresca an opportunity to see his players up close. Judging by the performances of City's players in the two friendlies it is easy to see which players have taken the opportunity on offer.

Nico Gonzalez is the first player that comes to mind. The Spanish midfielder fell down the pecking order in Pep Guardiola's squad throughout the second half of last season. Nico has taken his opportunity to impress in midfield and is now set to play a more prominent role for Manchester City next season.

Savinho is another player who has taken the reset on offer. The Brazilian international was another who fell out of favour last season. However, in the two friendlies that Manchester City have played, Savinho has played well. Yes, the areas of his game that need to drastcially improve remain. It was expected that Savinho would leave Manchester City this summer. But now you wonder if his preseason performances have seen Maresca view him as an important player for his team for next season.

There are other players who have impressed throughout Manchester City's preseason. Divin Mubama, Rico Lewis, and Vitor Reis come to mind. Enzo Maresca offered his squad a reset, and a host of players have taken the opportunity that was on offer. All of a sudden, the Manchester City squad may have a different look than what was expected when the 2025-26 season ended.

title: Wales must learn from Bosnia loss in Euros bid - Rush
description: Ian Rush says reaching Euro 2028 is a must for Wales as they bid to put their 2026 World Cup qualifying heartbreak behind them.
fullText:
Ian Rush believes Wales must learn from their painful World Cup play-off semi-final defeat by Bosnia and Herzegovina as they bid to qualify for Euro 2028.

The Red Dragons are winless in four matches so far this year and failed to qualify for the summer global showpiece in the USA, Canada and Mexico following their penalty shootout loss to Sergej Barbarez's side in March.

Their task is set to get tougher over the remainder of 2026 as Wales take on Portugal, Norway and Denmark in Nations League A.

But Wales legend Rush believes Craig Bellamy - who came close to leaving the Football Association of Wales to become Burnley boss earlier this summer - has the talent to deliver success with the national side.

"We have to be looking at qualifying [for Euro 2028], it's as simple as that," said Rush.

"Against Bosnia and Herzegovina, we should have won that. They beat Italy as well.

"The Euros are going to be in this country, so we need Wales to be in there."

The former Liverpool striker added: "I speak to Craig quite a lot.

"He's very, very good, so I'm looking forward to a good season and some good rounds from them because it's going to be difficult, looking at Norway, Denmark and Portugal."

Rush urges Liverpool to give Iraola time to succeed

The summer that changed Welsh football

A number of Welsh players have secured moves during the summer going into the 2026-27 season.

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow left Leeds United to join Manchester United while Harry Wilson, arguably the star performer of the Bellamy era, moved from Fulham to Leeds.

Liverpool youngster Lewis Koumas, who scored his first international goal against Ghana in June, is also expected to secure another loan switch away from Anfield having had spells with Birmingham City and Hull City last season.

"I've seen Lewis quite a lot in pre-season, he looks very, very good," said Rush, who scored 28 times in 73 appearances for his country.

"Harry Wilson, he came on in the second half, he was a major influence for Leeds in beating Liverpool.

"We're looking forward, but we've got to keep it as a team, it's up to them to do that, but I can see us doing alright."

Wales start their Nations League campaign against Portugal in Lisbon on 24 September and face Denmark in Copenhagen three days later.

Bellamy's side then host Norway and Denmark at Cardiff City Stadium in October.

The final two matches of the campaign take place in November with Wales travelling to Norway before hosting Portugal.

title: New season, new boss - will Alexander-Arnold be key figure at Real Madrid?
description: Trent Alexander-Arnold faces a defining second season at Real Madrid as he looks to prove his worth under Jose Mourinho.
fullText:
More than 14 months after leaving Liverpool for Real Madrid, Trent Alexander-Arnold will soon begin his second season with the Spanish club under a third manager in Jose Mourinho.

The 27-year-old right-back arrived with huge expectations.

When signing him, Real Madrid regarded him as one of the most versatile defenders in the world and one who could influence games through his passing range, crossing ability and experience in managing high-pressure moments.

However, his first season was disrupted by injuries, managerial changes and the difficulty of adapting to a new league and environment as he failed to make England's World Cup squad.

Now, after encouraging signs during pre-season, Alexander-Arnold will hope to finally establish himself as a key figure in the Spanish capital in the forthcoming campaign.

Real Madrid paid Liverpool a reported 10m euros (£8.4m) for Alexander-Arnold, releasing him from his contract on 1 June 2025, a month early.

But an eagerly awaited debut campaign never reached the heights many expected.

Two separate injuries affected him. A hamstring issue last September sidelined him for seven weeks, while a thigh problem in December kept him out for a further two months.

That denied Alexander-Arnold the sustained run of games needed to build momentum and a connection with supporters.

Overall, he featured in 35 of Real Madrid's 62 matches across all competitions last season, but was not first choice, starting 27 times as he shared the right-back role with club legend Dani Carvajal.

However, the defensive doubts that plagued him throughout his Liverpool career remained part of the conversation in Madrid - even as his quality in possession continued to stand out.

He showed glimpses of his undoubted ability, but there was a feeling among some supporters that they had not yet seen enough of Alexander-Arnold to judge his impact.

"Madridistas you have welcomed me with open arms." he wrote. "From the first day I arrived you have had my back. It took me a few months to find rhythm and settle in the new environment but I feel completely at home now.

"I will take a good break and put the work in over the summer. I promise we will bring trophies back to this amazing club next season."

As one of only a handful of Real players who did not feature at the World Cup, Alexander-Arnold has enjoyed a full pre-season under new boss Mourinho, who replaced Arbeloa in June for a second spell at the Bernabeu.

BBC Sport understands the Portuguese has been impressed by the England international's performances, values and the versatility he brings to the squad.

Mourinho views Alexander-Arnold as different from many traditional full-backs because of his ability to move into central areas and contribute to attacks from midfield positions.

His passing, crossing, through balls and set-piece delivery remain among the strongest parts of his game.

Alexander-Arnold has also spoken positively about the opportunity to work with the ex-Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham manager, describing it as a privilege.

"I have always admired the coach," he said. "I've played against him a couple of times, and it's a pleasure to work with him and his team.

"It's intense. The principles and the level of demand are very high, so I'm looking forward to seeing how, the more we get to know each other, the more we learn and the more he can teach us.

"We're all willing and eager to learn and improve. I'm sure he'll teach us many things and help us win trophies this year."

Competition for places is nothing new at Real Madrid, where virtually every position is contested by world-class players.

While Carvajal has left after his contract expired, the arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan will maintain the challenge Alexander-Arnold faces for a starting place.

The Netherlands international, 30, offers physicality, athleticism and defensive solidity.

However, during their recent 2-2 friendly draw with Fiorentina, Mourinho chose to start both players - Alexander-Arnold operating at right-back, while Dumfries played further forward on the same side.

Alexander-Arnold also took responsibility for set-pieces and moved into midfield areas during build-up play, highlighting the tactical flexibility Mourinho may want from him.

The increased competition may also provide the motivation for Alexander-Arnold to rediscover the form that made him one of Liverpool's most influential players during a period where the Reds lifted the Premier League, Champions League and Club World Cup.

Consistency will be the key for him as Mourinho looks to shape a squad capable of challenging for domestic and European success again.

For Alexander-Arnold, this season will also represent a great chance to establish himself at the club and force his way back into Thomas Tuchel's England plans.

title: Meta CTO told employees AI gains should go into more work
description: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth told staff that AI productivity gains should go into building more products, not more vacation. He called the question "very dumb."
fullText:
Meta CTO Bosworth told employees AI gains should go into more work, not more time off. Called the Meta Days vacation question “very dumb.” Meta cut 8,000 jobs this year while spending $135B on AI.

Meta’s chief technology officer Andrew Bosworth told employees at a July Q&A that AI productivity gains should be used to build more products, not to take more time off. An employee had asked whether the gains could be channelled into reviving “Meta Days,” a cancelled holiday programme that gave staff a few extra days off. Bosworth’s answer was blunt: “Stop asking about Meta Days. It’s very dumb.”

“I hope that what we do with our extra time is do even more and cooler stuff for the users who use our products every day,” Bosworth said, according to three people on the call. “I get an extra hour. You know what I do with it? I put it into that.” He told the employee to ask their parents what they would think of using every chance to talk to a boss to request more days off. He later said he was sorry for coming down “too hard” and acknowledged the question may have been “tongue-in-cheek.”

The comments land in a specific context. Meta cut 8,000 jobs in May while spending up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure this year. The company replaced its cancelled Meta Days with two “choice days” and provides four weeks off plus public holidays. Bosworth himself stands to earn up to $921 million from a stock option programme tied to Meta reaching a $9 trillion valuation by 2031. The message to employees is that AI makes them more productive, the company keeps the productivity, and the reward is the privilege of building more.

The broader debate is whether AI productivity gains belong to workers or employers. Jeff Bezos has said he expects AI to let households return to a single earner. Morgan Stanley predicted AI would help millions take on second and third jobs. Bosworth’s position is the employer’s version: more output, same hours, no extra days. At a company that cut 10% of its workforce this year, told survivors to train their AI replacements, and installed keystroke-tracking software on employee laptops, the answer to “can we have more time off?” was always going to be no. Bosworth just said it out loud.

In next-generation optical data centers, the fundamental bottleneck appears to be shifting from electrical memory bus limits to Optical Transmission Jitter and phase-shift misalignment caused by thermal variance in optical transceivers and optical network interfaces (ONIs).

Standard communication stack protocols traditionally rely on runtime loop branches (if/else) and heavy software buffers to realign delayed light-pulses. However, in our observations, this approach often triggers costly warp divergence and pipeline stalls inside the accelerator’s streaming multiprocessors (SM).

The photonic-mesh-fng-router project represents an exploratory effort to re-examine this boundary:

title: Driving a 7.3" 6-Color E-Paper Display in `no_std` Rust (ESP32-S3)
description: Rust Embassy Examples for Seeed Studio reTerminal E1002 This repository contains idiomatic Rust examples for the Seeed Studio reTerminal E1002 carrier board (powered by the XIAO ESP32-S3 MCU), buil...
fullText:
This repository contains idiomatic Rust examples for the Seeed Studio reTerminal E1002 carrier board (powered by the XIAO ESP32-S3 MCU), built using the Embassy async framework, esp-hal (v1.1), and defmt logging over USB-UART / RTT.

Reads the Li-Po battery voltage through the onboard 1:2 resistor voltage divider. Drives the active-HIGH enable pin (GPIO21) HIGH before sampling ADC1 (GPIO1) and LOW afterward to avoid wasting battery current through the divider circuit.

About Battery Monitoring:
The onboard circuit halves the battery voltage before feeding it to ADC pin GPIO1. To calculate true battery voltage:
$$V_{\text{batt}} = 2 \times V_{\text{adc}}$$

Monitors the three user buttons (KEY0, KEY1, KEY2) with time-based debouncing (50ms stability threshold) and logs press and release events via defmt.

Drives the onboard passive buzzer on GPIO45 using ESP32-S3 LEDC hardware PWM. Demonstrates an ascending 3-note startup chime, a double beep, and a low-to-high frequency alert sweep.

Plays the Imperial March (Darth Vader theme from Star Wars) using a custom musical score player that supports regular notes, dotted notes, and rests at 120 BPM.

Controls the onboard user LED on GPIO6. Demonstrates digital blinking and smooth brightness fading using LEDC hardware PWM.

Note on Active-LOW Logic: Driving GPIO6 LOW (0% PWM duty) turns the LED ON, while driving GPIO6 HIGH (100% PWM duty) turns the LED OFF.

Reads and sets the onboard PCF8563 Real-Time Clock over I2C (SDA: GPIO19, SCL: GPIO20). Sets initial date/time at startup and logs the current timestamp every second.

About PCF8563:
The PCF8563 is an ultra-low power CMOS Real-Time Clock / calendar chip from NXP with an I2C slave address of 0x51.

Reads temperature (°C) and relative humidity (%RH) from the onboard Sensirion SHT40 sensor over I2C every 2 seconds.

Mounts the onboard microSD card slot over SPI2 (SCK: GPIO7, MISO: GPIO8, MOSI: GPIO9, CS: GPIO14). Enables slot power (GPIO16), verifies card insertion (GPIO15), lists root directory contents, and writes/reads /HELLO.TXT using the embedded-sdmmc crate.

Displays 24-bit or 32-bit uncompressed BMP images from a microSD card on the 7.3" Good Display GDEP073E01 6-Color ACeP panel using the local epdsi driver library (Ed2208Controller).

A Python helper script is provided in the repository root to convert any input photo or image (JPG, PNG, WEBP, etc.) into an uncompressed 800x480 BMP formatted for the reTerminal E1002 microSD card:
